# PAGAMENOS — M7 — OUTCOME + EVIDENCE — EFFECTIVE SPECIFICATION V1.1

```
M7 EFFECTIVE SPEC V1.1: CANDIDATE / NOT ACCEPTED
M7 IMPLEMENTATION: NOT AUTHORIZED
AUTHOR CANDIDATE — NOT SELF-ACCEPTED — AWAITING INDEPENDENT RE-AUDIT
AUTHOR REVISION       : ROUND 5 (closes M7V11R5-AUD-01 … 02)

NEW CONSENT SEMANTICS : 0
NEW A1 SEMANTICS      : 0
NEW A2 SEMANTICS      : 0
NEW B SEMANTICS       : 0
NEW C SEMANTICS       : 0
```

**Nature.** A specification candidate for the M7 milestone (*"Outcomes + VS ladder + evidence (hardened, verify-then-purge)"*, Phase 0A-2 FINAL §40). It changes no runtime code, no Prisma schema, no migration, no CI, no `authority/` artifact, and edits no accepted specification or the root register. SQL in §19 is **normative specification text**, not an executed migration.

**Conventions.** MUST / MUST NOT / MAY are normative. `M7-*` identifiers belong to this candidate. "Register §n" = `PAGAMENOS_SPEC_AUTHORITY.md`. "A1 §n" = `PAGAMENOS_M3_5B_A1_EFFECTIVE_SPEC_V2_1.md`. "A2 §n" = `PAGAMENOS_M3_5B_A2_EFFECTIVE_SPEC_CANONICAL_V1.md`. "CCA §n" = `PAGAMENOS_A1_A2_M7_CONSENT_COMPATIBILITY_AMENDMENT_01.md`. "JBA §n" = `PAGAMENOS_M3_5B_B_ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACT_V1_9.md`. "RAT" = `PAGAMENOS_M3_5B_B_SEMANTIC_RATIFICATION_V1_3.md`. "FINAL §n", "RT-n", "Rev2 §n" = the Phase 0A-2 base-study chain. Every table name, column, enum label, role, function and trigger that this document calls normative is defined in §19; §19.14 inventories them.

Replaced by the three-phase lock discipline, the per-function lock-order matrix, the implicit-wait table and the LG-THEOREM of §16.2.5–§16.2.8, each derived from the SQL of §19, and by one class-0 order shared by every `c_*` function |
| a backend-liveness rule defined as *"every write of a row carrying `backendSha256`"* | `M7V11R4-AUD-03`: that predicate is not the safety property, it named `w_renew_outbox_lease_v1` although its body took no lock, and it forced meaningless locks on paths that only mutate or remove obligations. Replaced by the exact definition of §11.10.3 (**create** a drain obligation or **mint** external write authority; re-open and extend proved empty by BL-9) and the mechanically derived set of §11.10.4 |
| a capability-mint expiry decision taken on a clock sampled before blocking locks | `M7V11R4-AUD-04`: a call could start before `grantExpiresAt`, wait across it, and persist a mint stamped with the pre-wait instant. Replaced by a clock read after every blocking lock and a trigger-stamped `mintedAt` (XF-14) |
| two separate foreign keys proving grant identity and generation identity of a mint | `M7V11R4-AUD-05`: nothing proved both referenced the **same** grant row. Replaced by one composite foreign key over grant id, generation identity, envelope and capability kind (XF-11) |
| inventory subtotals that do not add up to their total | `M7V11R4-AUD-06`: §19.14 summed to 40 tables while stating 39. Every subtotal now carries its own derivation rule and is regenerated from the final text (§19.14.1) |
| a no-deadlock proof premised on a compatible row-lock request **bypassing** an incompatible request already waiting on the same tuple (round-4 PG-1) | `M7V11R5-AUD-01`: PostgreSQL's tuple-lock arbitration exists precisely so that incoming share lockers do not starve a waiting exclusive locker, and a later compatible request may queue behind it. Under that behaviour the round-4 design admits the three-way cycle *scheduler → SO-2 → backend retirement → scheduler*. Replaced by the **conservative** premise PG-1 (a compatible request MAY wait behind an incompatible waiter), which the proof uses and never contradicts, and by the rule that no M7 transaction ever *is* such a waiter on a row that work transactions hold in a shared mode (§16.2.5 LG-10) |
| a backend or profile retirement that **waits** for the class-10 `FOR UPDATE` (bounded only by `lock_timeout`) | `M7V11R5-AUD-01`: a waiting `FOR UPDATE` is exactly the incompatible waiter behind which a later `FOR SHARE` may queue. Replaced by `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` on every lock both retirement functions take, mapped to the governed retry/failure contract RR-1…RR-7 (§11.10.8); work is never cancelled or delayed to let a retirement through |
| a session revocation that **waits** for `FOR UPDATE` on the session row | found by this round's re-derivation under the conservative premise, not named by the audit: `r_record_erasure_request_v1` holds the session `FOR SHARE` and then waits on the assignment, while SO-1/2/3 hold the assignment and then request the session `FOR SHARE`, which may queue behind a waiting revocation — a cycle of the same kind (§16.2.8, T-191). Replaced by an insert-first revocation whose quiescence is probed with `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` (RV-1…RV-5, §8.2) |
| batch deletion schedulers inserting executions — and so taking the implicit assignment `FOR KEY SHARE` — in an order unrelated to the assignment | found by this round's re-derivation: two batch schedulers could take `FOR KEY SHARE` on assignments `X`, `Y` in opposite orders and, with A1 withdrawals of `X` and `Y` waiting between them, form a cycle under the conservative premise. Replaced by ascending `assignmentId` order for every P3 loop that can reference more than one assignment (LG-8, T-192) |
| the unqualified sentence *"row mechanisms are idempotent on replay"* | `M7V11R5-AUD-02`: `w_execute_row_purge_v1` had no replay check, so a replay with `retainDeletionHistory = true` reached the completion `INSERT` again and failed `23505`; redaction's check ran only before the assignment lock, so a **concurrent** duplicate failed the same way; and with `retainDeletionHistory = false` there is by design no stored count to return. Replaced by the replay contract RM-1…RM-7 (§15.7.1), which states a different, exact outcome for each case |

## 2. Scope

M7 V1.1 specifies, at executable level:

1. the **`Outcome`** root and its append-only participant-authored **assertions** (FINAL §21, §30; RT-09; JBA §7);
2. **`SavingEvidence`** — the durable record of one participant evidence-submission act — and its object-storage lifecycle (FINAL §22; RT-09; RT-17);
3. the **trusted participant session capability** that makes participant substitution DB-rejectable (§8);
4. the **immutable storage identity model** — storage backend, storage profile, canonical generation — binding every historical object to the exact physical storage authority under which it was created, across control-plane rotation, and separating the profile that **issued** a capability from the profile that **executed** it (§7.4, §11.1, §11.6, §11.8, §12.4);
4a. **true external write fencing**: an immutable per-generation **authorization envelope** (one operation, one exact key, one backend, one absolute expiry), a **sealed capability signer** that resolves that envelope itself and exposes no key or expiry parameter, and a persisted write fence, so that once an object stops being writable nothing M7 can mint may create it, and a proof of absence is permanent rather than momentary (§11.7);
4b. a single **drain predicate** governing both storage-profile and storage-backend retirement (§11.9), and the **two-sided backend liveness protocol** that serializes retirement against exactly the paths able to create a drain obligation or mint external write authority (§11.10);
4c. the **complete transaction-owner model** (TO-1…TO-8, the capability signer included) and a **lock graph derived from the SQL**, with a stated no-deadlock theorem and the real-PostgreSQL concurrency cases that can falsify it (§16.2);
5. the **one-use upload capability**, storage staging state machine, externally fenced leases, transactional outbox with a per-effect **bound policy**, and reconciliation (§10–§12, §15.11.6, §16–§17);
6. append-only **correction and integrity adjudication** for assertions and evidence (§14);
7. **withdrawal-triggered, retention-triggered and legally authorized deletion** with DB-verifiable authorization, an explicit machine-readable **completion-deadline budget**, and honest recording of budget failures and late completions (§15, §15.11.6);
8. the **PostgreSQL role, ownership, privilege and `SECURITY DEFINER` model**, provisioned fail-closed, with a manifest-driven **exact-set** catalog verifier (§18, §19.13);
9. the M7 **control-plane manifest**, the separation of immutable manifest identity from installation events, executable rotation and rollback, and what a later selector rotation must prove (§23–§24);
10. the **trusted-generation facts M7 exposes** for a possible future B1S S-2 contract, without deciding grounding (§21.3);
11. the adversarial real-PostgreSQL verification contract and invariant register (§25–§26).

M7 V1.1 applies the register's reading rule (register header). No universal total order is asserted.

| study-wide invariants (RT-09, RT-10, RT-13, RT-16, RT-17, RT-18, Rev2 §6.E) | base study chain (§1 of register), by its own internal precedence | consumes |

| decision chain and `Decision` physical identity | A2 / M3.5A | consumes, unchanged; adds no A2 privilege semantics |

| B terminology, S-2/S-4 consumption rules, `DB-03B`, legal-deletion architecture | RAT V1.3 → JBA V1.9 → JBA Amendment 01 | **orthogonal**; M7 does not amend B; M7 conforms where B describes upstream M7 artifacts |

| **AC-07** | CCA §7 maps two operations → two policies; M7 evidence submission has an issuance step and a completion step | both steps are operations of the *SavingEvidence upload* family and are bound to the **same** fixed evidence policy; no third policy exists (§9.2) |
| **AC-08** | RT-17 states a **completion** SLA (*"deleted ≤ 30 days if never verified"*); an asynchronous outbox with bounded retries cannot complete at the instant a row becomes eligible | RT-17 controls the completion bound. V1.1 therefore never treats the RT-17 number as a scheduling offset: it decomposes the bound into `schedule deadline + scheduler worst-case lag + effect completion budget ≤ hard deadline`, enforced by CHECK constraints and per-row due dates (§15.11). Reducing the constant arbitrarily is **not** the resolution; the explicit budget is |
| **AC-09** | FINAL §3 names a concrete storage stack ("Vercel Blob"); RT-17 and JBA §18.2 **E-D** require *proof of absence* for a specific object | a stack name is neither a capability guarantee nor an identity. V1.1 binds every historical object to an **immutable storage profile** (§11.1); conformance is verified per profile (§11.2), never assumed from the stack name; and absence is provable only against the bound backend (§15.7, M7-I88) |

---

## 5. Terminology

| Term | Meaning in this document | Never confuse with |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **`Decision`** | the accepted A2/M3.5A decision, physically one `public.purchase_intent_decision_binding` row (A2 §7) | a purchase; an `Outcome` |
| **`Outcome`** | the M7 root (`m7.m7_outcome`): one per accepted `Decision`, carrying no authored content | `PurchaseOccasion` (B2); an assertion |
| **outcome assertion** | one immutable participant-authored fact about what followed a `Decision` (`m7.m7_outcome_assertion`) | a status column; a VS level |
| **status label** | one of the participant-assertable FINAL §21 labels, persisted as provenance (JBA BI-23) | a real-world proposition |
| **upload intent** | the **evidence candidate**: a one-use, participant- and `Decision`-bound upload capability (`m7.m7_evidence_upload_intent`) | a `SavingEvidence` record |
| **storage backend** | the immutable identity of one physical storage authority — provider class, container, region, endpoint identity, staging prefix, evidence prefix, **provider write-completion window** — digested as `backendSha256` (`m7.m7_storage_backend`) | a credential; a manifest; a deployment |
| **storage profile** | an immutable operational binding *onto one backend*: credential-profile identity and generation, upload transport, decoder and encoder generation, storage capability version, conditional-create mode, **write-capability mode** (`m7.m7_storage_profile`) | the backend itself; the active manifest |
| **issuance profile** | the storage profile that **minted** an upload capability, recorded once on the intent. It is transport and replay provenance (§11.8) | the profile that later executed anything |
| **executing profile** | the live storage profile a particular step **actually ran under** — the claim, the observation, the accepted artifact, an effect attempt. It is re-resolved at each step and recorded there (SI-4) | the issuance profile; the currently active profile |
| **credential rotation** | a new storage profile over the **same** `backendSha256` | backend rotation, which is a different `backendSha256` and never addresses the same bytes |
| **canonical generation** | one `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)` pair, the unique canonical object key allocated to it at claim time, its executing profile, and its **write fence** (`m7.m7_canonical_generation`) | the upload intent; the accepted artifact |
| **generation write grant** | the immutable **authorization envelope** of one generation's canonical write — one operation, one exact key, one backend, one absolute expiry — identified by an opaque `generationGrantId`. The database records the envelope and every mint of it, never a signature (`m7.m7_generation_write_grant`, `m7.m7_generation_capability_mint`, §11.7) | a presigned staging URL; a credential; a token count |
| **authorization envelope** | the four-component bound on what a minted provider write capability may do: `operation = CANONICAL_CREATE`, `objectKey`, `backendSha256`, `validUntil = grantExpiresAt`. What §11.7 proves is that nothing M7 can mint has a **wider** envelope — not that only one capability was ever signed (§11.7.0) | a signature; a token; a secret |
| **sealed signer edge** | the single M7 interface that returns a capability envelope, `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1(manifestSha256, generationGrantId)`, reachable only by `pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt`, which holds EXECUTE on nothing else. Its only input is an opaque identifier; it resolves every envelope component **and the signing authority** itself (§11.7.3 XF-12, XF-17) | an interface in which the caller supplies a key, an expiry or a credential; a worker-reachable signer |
| **signing profile** | the live storage profile, over the grant's own backend and of the grant's own capability kind (`writeCapabilityMode`, `envelopeEnforcement`), whose signing credential the signer uses for one mint. Resolved by the database after the liveness lock (XF-17) and recorded on the mint row; never selected by the worker or the signer | the envelope; the issuance profile; a caller parameter |
| **transaction owner** | one of the eight enumerated principals permitted to open an M7 database transaction (TO-1…TO-8, §16.2.3), each with its own CCA class, `DatabaseExecutionContext` registration, credential, process and lock profile | a module; a role; a function family |
| **lock profile** | the published sequence of lock acquisitions of one M7 function: its **P1** explicit locks in the canonical order, its **P2** liveness locks, and the implicit waits its **P3** writes can incur (§16.2.5–§16.2.7) | a lock class |
| **backend liveness lock** | the `m7_storage_backend` row for a backend, taken `FOR SHARE` in phase P2 by every function that **creates a drain obligation or mints external write authority** on that backend (§11.10.3 BL-2), and `FOR UPDATE` first by both retirement functions; lock **class 10** (§11.10.3, §16.2.2) | `m7.i_require_routable_profile`, which answers a different question and takes no lock; a lock on paths that only mutate or remove obligations, which take none |
| **write fence** | the instant after which no capability M7 **can mint** authorizes creating a given object — because every envelope M7 can mint for it expires at the object's own `grantExpiresAt` (XF-11), independently of how many were signed: `grantExpiresAt + providerWriteCompletionWindow + writeFenceSkewAllowance` for a generation key, `uploadExpiresAt + …` for a staging key. No absence proof for that object is executable before it (SI-5) | a lease expiry; a deletion deadline |
| **drained (of a backend)** | the single predicate `m7.i_backend_is_drained` returns NULL: no live artifact, no open intent, no open effect, every write fence elapsed, and every canonical and staging key M7 wrote there has a `CONFIRMED` delete effect (§11.9) | "no live artifacts"; "retired" |
| **bound policy (of an outbox effect)** | the retention policy resolved through the effect's own family — its deletion execution, its upload intent or its reconciliation run — and the only source of its lease, renewal, attempt-ceiling and backoff values (DL-5) | the active manifest's policy |
| **accepted generation** | the single canonical generation whose observation was recorded under the then-current lease epoch and which the `SavingEvidence` submission binds | any other generation, which is by definition an orphan |
| **storage observation** | a storage-worker-authored record of what the server itself read back from a named canonical generation key, under that generation's **executing** profile and its pinned encoder (`m7.m7_storage_observation`) | a client success claim |
| **`SavingEvidence`** / **evidence submission** | the canonical record of one participant submission act, created only by consuming a validated upload intent (`m7.m7_evidence_submission`) | a verification; proof of a purchase |
| **raw evidence artifact** | the re-encoded image object at the accepted generation's canonical key (`m7.m7_evidence_artifact` tracks it) | the submission metadata |
| **participant session capability** | a server-side handle binding one participant to an unexpired, unrevoked session; DB stores only the SHA-256 of a 256-bit secret (`m7.m7_participant_session`) | `TrustedParticipantContext` (A1); a consent authorization |
| **staging object** / **canonical object** | untrusted client-written bytes at a staging key / server-written re-encoded bytes at a generation-bound canonical key | each other |
| **outbox effect** | a durable request for an irreversible storage effect, routed to one immutable backend; it is **not** the effect (`m7.m7_storage_outbox`) | a confirmation |
| **lease epoch** | a monotonically increasing fencing token per leased row; for upload intents it also **names the canonical generation** | a timestamp |
| **control-plane manifest** | the immutable reviewed artifact identity `(manifestVersion, manifestSha256)` and its bindings (`m7.m7_control_plane_manifest`) | an installation |
| **control-plane installation** | one *event* of making a registered manifest active (`m7.m7_control_plane_installation`); rollback is a new installation event of an already-registered manifest | the manifest identity |
| **hard deadline / schedule deadline / completion budget** | the instant a deletion MUST be *completed* / the instant it MUST be *scheduled* / the time allowed between them (§15.11) | each other; RT-17 states the first |
| **control plane** | everything a guarantee depends on besides data: functions, triggers, ACLs, roles, the installed manifest, the storage backends and profiles, the catalog expectation set (JBA §19.2) | data |
| **E-A … E-E** | JBA §18.2 enforcement classes (integrity rejection; fail-closed read; end-to-end fidelity; proof of absence; capability/provenance) | Model A consent read (A2 §4.1) |
| **owner-class actor** | superuser, migration owner, member of `pagamenos_m7_owner`, or accepted-table owner | a runtime role |
| **runtime-role actor** | any actor holding exactly the grants of one M7 login role, able to issue arbitrary SQL through it (P-10) | an owner-class actor |

## 6. Domain model

### 6.1 Chain M7 attaches to (accepted, unchanged)

```text
public.study_participant
  └─ public.experiment_assignment                    (A1 §7)
       └─ public.purchase_intent_capture_token       (A2 §5)
            └─ public.purchase_intent                (A2 §5)
                 └─ public.purchase_intent_decision_request   (A2 §16, UNIQUE(intentId))
                      └─ public.purchase_intent_decision_binding  (A2 §7, UNIQUE(decisionRequestId), UNIQUE(snapshotId))
                           └─ public.decision_snapshot (M3.5A)
```

### 6.2 M7 structure

```text
m7_outcome                       1 per accepted Decision binding          (RT-09 entity cardinality)
 ├─ m7_outcome_assertion         0..N participant-authored, append-only   (FINAL §21 "append"; JBA §7.7)
 │    └─ m7_outcome_command_receipt   transport idempotency
 └─ m7_evidence_submission       0..N SavingEvidence                       (FINAL §22/§30)
      ├─ m7_storage_observation       exactly 1 (via its upload intent)    — digest lives here (RT-09)
      ├─ m7_evidence_artifact         exactly 1 raw-object lifecycle row, bound to ONE accepted generation
      ├─ m7_evidence_integrity_finding 0..N system adjudications
      └─ m7_evidence_submission_receipt transport idempotency

m7_evidence_upload_intent        evidence candidate; bound to a Decision binding AND to one storage profile
 └─ m7_canonical_generation      1 per lease epoch; each owns a distinct canonical object key

control plane (never participant-scoped)
  m7_storage_backend ◀─ m7_storage_profile ─┐
  m7_retention_policy ─────────────────────┤
  m7_merchant_vocabulary (+ entry) ────────┼─▶ m7_control_plane_manifest ─▶ m7_control_plane_installation
  m7_expected_* (catalog expectation set) ─┘        (immutable identity)        (repeatable events)
```

### 6.3 What M7 does not assert

| Statement | Status in M7 |
| :-- | :-- |
| an `Outcome` proves a purchase | **false** (JBA BI-01, §7.7) |
| a status label asserts its English name | **false** (JBA BI-23) |
| evidence existence proves verification | **false** (JBA BI-21) |
| `evidence-submitted` is a label | **not stored** — object-implied by an existing `m7_evidence_submission` row (JBA §7.6) |
| `evidence-verified` is a label | **not stored** — it would be implied by a C1 verification record, which does not exist (§22) |
| the "current" status / VS level of an `Outcome` | **not stored, not projected** (P-14 principle; §13.6) |
| an object found at an M7-shaped key is M7 evidence | **false** — ownership exists only by a key having been allocated to a canonical generation and bound to a consumed intent (§17.4) |
| the active control plane says where a historical object lives | **false** — only the row's own `storageProfileId` does (§7.4) |

### 6.4 Participant-assertable status labels

FINAL §21 enumerates seven labels and defines none (JBA §7.3). M7 persists exactly the five a participant can assert without implying an independent object:

| FINAL §21 label | Persisted value | Author |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| intended | `INTENDED` | participant |
| attempted | `ATTEMPTED` | participant |
| self-reported | `SELF_REPORTED` | participant |
| failed | `FAILED` | participant |
| abandoned | `ABANDONED` | participant |
| evidence-submitted | — (object-implied) | — |
| evidence-verified | — (C1) | — |

## 7. Identity model

### 7.1 Identity versus provenance

| Row class | Scientific / domain identity | Transport identity | Never identity |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7_outcome` | `id` (DB-minted); natural uniqueness `UNIQUE(decisionBindingId)` | — | assignment, participant, timestamp |
| `m7_outcome_assertion` | `id`; command identity `UNIQUE(outcomeId, clientCaptureKey)`; allocation `UNIQUE(outcomeId, assertionSeq)` | receipt `UNIQUE(operationScope, assignmentId, idempotencyKey)` | seq, label, time, payload, **vocabulary version** |
| `m7_evidence_upload_intent` | `id`; issuance identity `UNIQUE(decisionBindingId, clientCorrelationNonce)` | — (A2 token pattern, A2 §5) | object key, nonce alone, **storage profile** |
| `m7_canonical_generation` | `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)`; `UNIQUE(canonicalObjectKey)` | — | the key's hex suffix alone |
| `m7_evidence_submission` | `id`; domain identity `UNIQUE(uploadIntentId)`; command identity `UNIQUE(outcomeId, clientCaptureKey)` | receipt `UNIQUE(operationScope, assignmentId, idempotencyKey)` | content digest (RT-09: reuse **detection** only), object key |
| `m7_participant_session` | `id`; secret identity `UNIQUE(handleSha256)` | — | participant, issuance time |
| `m7_storage_backend` | `backendSha256` (PK, DB-recomputed from the immutable identity fields) | — | a container name alone; a credential |
| `m7_storage_profile` | `id`; `UNIQUE(storageProfileVersion)`; `UNIQUE(profileSha256)` | — | the backend alone; any credential secret |
| `m7_control_plane_manifest` | `manifestVersion` (PK); `UNIQUE(manifestSha256)` | — | an installation |
| `m7_control_plane_installation` | `id`; `UNIQUE(installationSeq)`; at most one active | — | the manifest digest — **an installation is an event, not an identity** (§23.2) |

**Every `id` is minted inside PostgreSQL by `pg_catalog.gen_random_uuid()` in an M7 function.** No M7 function accepts an identity for the row it creates (DB-12 principle, JBA §18.6). The one exception in form, not in substance, is `m7_storage_backend.backendSha256`, which is a **content digest recomputed by PostgreSQL** from the supplied identity fields and refused on mismatch (R-B-14 principle).

### 7.2 JBA S-2 / S-4 source identity mapping

JBA §7.7 fixes S-2 source identity as *"`Outcome` row id plus its M7 idempotency key"*; S-4 re-proof traverses *"evidence → outcome → decision → intent → token → assignment"*.

| JBA term | M7 physical fact |
| :-- | :-- |
| "`Outcome` row id" (the S-2 source assertion) | `m7_outcome_assertion.id` — the root carries no authored content and is not an assertion |
| "M7 idempotency key" | the `(operationScope, assignmentId, idempotencyKey)` of the assertion's **originating** receipt (`resultKind = 'RECORDED'`), exactly one per assertion (partial unique index, §19.7) |
| `Outcome` as RT-09 unit / S-4 FK target | `m7_outcome.id` |
| S-4 submission record | `m7_evidence_submission.id` |
| "correction/retraction … a new observation explicitly superseding the prior" | a new assertion row with `assertionKind ∈ {CORRECTION, RETRACTION}` and `supersedesAssertionId` (§14) |

### 7.3 Participant derivation (DB-provable)

`participant(o)` for an `m7_outcome` `o`:

```text
o.decisionBindingId → binding.decisionRequestId → request.intentId → intent.captureTokenId
  → token.assignmentId → assignment.participantId
```

`m7_outcome.assignmentId` is **stored** and **verified equal to the derivation** by a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger (§19.10, `m7.t_outcome_coherence`). All chain rows are append-only under accepted A1/A2 triggers and `m7_outcome` is append-only, so the stored value cannot diverge after insert (**E-A** against every non-owner actor). No other M7 row stores a participant or assignment identifier except `assignmentId` on receipts, upload intents, erasure requests and deletion rows, each trigger-verified against its own derivation.

### 7.4 Storage identity derivation (DB-provable) — closes `M7V11-AUD-01` and `M7V11R2-AUD-02` at the identity level

Three different questions are asked of a storage-bearing row, and V1.1 answers each with a **different, separately persisted** identity. Collapsing any two of them is what produced both findings.

| Question | Answer column | Never derived from |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **where are the bytes physically?** | the row's own `backendSha256` | the active control plane (SI-1) |
| **which profile issued the capability this object exists under?** | `m7_evidence_upload_intent."issuanceProfileId"` | anything but the active manifest at issuance (SI-2) |
| **which profile actually executed the provider reads/writes and the codec pipeline that produced these bytes?** | the `executingProfileId` of the **generation**, of its **observation**, of the **artifact**'s accepted generation, and of each **effect attempt** | the intent's issuance profile (SI-4) |

For any storage-bearing row `r`, the **physical storage authority** of its object is defined *only* by that row's own immutable binding, never by the active control plane:

```text
r.<profile column> → profile.backendSha256 → backend(providerClass, containerId, regionId,
                                                     endpointIdentity, stagingPrefix, evidencePrefix)
```

`backendSha256` is additionally **stored on every storage-bearing row** and trigger-verified equal to `profile.backendSha256`, so routing checks are single-predicate and composite foreign keys are possible without traversing a mutable path.

> **SI-1 (normative).** No M7 function, trigger, view, index predicate or worker instruction resolves the physical backend of an **existing** object through `m7_control_plane_installation`, `m7_control_plane_manifest`, or any "active" selector. It resolves it only through the row's own profile column and `backendSha256`.
>
> **SI-2 (normative).** The active control plane is consulted **only** to choose the **issuance** profile of a **new** upload intent (§10.2). Once written, that choice is immutable for the life of the row and is *transport/replay provenance*, not an execution fact.
>
> **SI-3 (normative).** A lifecycle operation on an existing object executes only under a storage profile whose `backendSha256` equals the bound row's `backendSha256`, and that profile must not be retired. `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` is accepted only under that condition (§15.7, §19.12.4, M7-I88).
>
> **SI-4 (normative, closes `M7V11R2-AUD-02`).** Every row that records an **execution** — a canonical generation, its storage observation, the accepted artifact, an effect attempt, a reconciliation finding — persists the `executingProfileId` of the profile that was live and used **for that execution**, and never a copy of the intent's `issuanceProfileId`. `issuanceProfileId` and `executingProfileId` may differ, and after any credential, transport or codec rotation on the same backend they normally do.
>
> **SI-5 (normative, closes `M7V11R2-AUD-01`; re-derived for `M7V11R3-AUD-01`).** Every object M7 can create has a persisted **write fence** instant after which **no authorization envelope M7 can mint** authorizes creating it — the envelope-form claim of §11.7.1, which does not depend on counting physical tokens (§11.7.0). No delete-and-confirm-absence effect for an object is executable before that object's fence (§11.7).

SI-1…SI-5 are enforced by DDL and function bodies, not by prose: see `m7.i_require_routable_profile` (§19.11.1), the `m7_storage_effect_attempt` backend columns and their trigger (§19.9, §19.10), the `t_outbox_guard` O6 branch (§19.10), the `(executingProfileId, encoderGeneration)` composite FK of §19.8 (SI-4), and the fence predicates of `m7.i_enqueue_delete` and `m7.t_outbox_coherence` (SI-5).

## 8. Trusted participant session capability

### 8.1 Why A1's `TrustedParticipantContext` is necessary but not sufficient

A1's context (`src/study/participant-context.ts`) is a module-private `WeakSet` registration: unforgeable **in process**, invisible **to PostgreSQL**. Against a runtime-role actor issuing SQL directly (P-10), a `participantId` parameter is just a value. M7 therefore adds a capability the database itself verifies. It **consumes** A1's context and **does not change it** (A1 §12, CCA §12 signature unchanged).

### 8.2 Design

| Property | Specification |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Issuer** | the M7 session module (`services/m7-participant-session.ts`, illustrative path), invoked by the trusted session adapter immediately after A1 `resolveTrustedParticipantContext` succeeds for an authenticated request; it calls `m7.s_issue_participant_session_v1` over a connection authenticated as `pagamenos_m7_session_issuer_rt` |
| **Material** | 32 random bytes from the OS CSPRNG (`crypto.randomBytes(32)`), the **session secret** |
| **Persisted** | `handleSha256 = sha256(secret)` (32 bytes), `participantId`, `issuedAt`, `expiresAt`, `issuedBy = session_user`, `installationId`. **The secret is never persisted and never sent to the issuance function** |
| **Represented to the process** | server-side only, inside the authenticated study session (encrypted http-only cookie managed by the auth layer). In process it is held in a module-private `WeakMap<TrustedParticipantContext, SessionSecret>` registered by the M7 session module for the lifetime of one request. It is **never** a field of CCA operation `input` and never returned by any M7 operation |
| **Consumers** | (a) the CCA assignment-lock function `m7.p_lock_and_prove_assignment_v1` (§9.4 step F); (b) every participant write/read function (`m7.p_*`); (c) `m7.r_record_erasure_request_v1`. Each receives the **secret** and recomputes the digest in PostgreSQL |
| **Binding fields** | `participantId` (FK → `public.study_participant`). Assignment is **not** bound into the session; it is re-proved per operation from the locked assignment row (`assignment.participantId = session.participantId`) |
| **Operation binding** | none in the session itself — operation binding is by the one-use upload intent (§10) and by per-operation idempotency identity. The session is an identity capability, not an operation authorization |
| **Lifetime** | `expiresAt = issuedAt + policy.sessionTtl`, `sessionTtl ≤ 24 h` (CHECK). The auth session may be longer (FINAL §28, study-duration TTL, open wave config); the M7 capability is re-issued on expiry by the same adapter path |
| **Freshness** | every consumer compares `pg_catalog.clock_timestamp() < expiresAt` **inside PostgreSQL**. Application clocks are not consulted |
| **Replay resistance** | the secret is a bearer credential for its lifetime by design. Operation replay is closed separately: outcome/evidence idempotency identities (§7.1), one-use upload intents (§10), and receipts. A replayed secret after revocation or expiry is rejected |
| **Revocation** | append-only `m7_participant_session_revocation` via `m7.s_revoke_participant_session_v1` (logout, rotation, re-authentication, administrative). Consumers take `FOR SHARE` on the session row and then check for a revocation row on a fresh statement snapshot. Revocation **never waits** (§16.2.5 LG-10): it first inserts the revocation row, then probes quiescence with `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` on the session and returns `QUIESCENT` or `DRAINING`. The contract is RV-1…RV-5 below |
| **Revocation contract** | **RV-1** a revocation is *effective* at its commit: every validation whose check statement starts after that commit fails `28000`. **RV-2** a transaction that validated the session **before** that commit may still commit afterwards (it holds the session `FOR SHARE`, so it is serialized before the revocation). **RV-3** `QUIESCENT` means the revocation acquired `FOR UPDATE` on the session in the same transaction that holds the committed-or-committing revocation row, so at that instant no validated transaction was in flight and none can commit afterwards. **RV-4** the session module reports a revocation as *complete* to its caller only after a call returned `QUIESCENT`; while it returns `DRAINING` the module re-invokes the function with bounded backoff (the second and later calls insert nothing: `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`), and a module that exhausts its budget reports *revoked, not yet quiescent* — never *complete*. **RV-5** the revocation function holds no lock while any other transaction can wait on it except the session row it acquired `NOWAIT`, after which it performs no further waiting request (§16.2.8 N3) |
| **Invalidation on withdrawal** | **none**. Withdrawal is not a session event; collection after withdrawal is refused by CCA consent evaluation (§9), and privacy requests must remain possible after withdrawal (§15.6) |
| **Transactional validation** | `m7.i_require_session(secret, participantId)` inside the same transaction as the write, under `FOR SHARE` |
| **Failure semantics** | unknown digest, expired, revoked, or participant mismatch → `RAISE` with SQLSTATE `28000` (`invalid_authorization_specification`), message `M7_SESSION_INVALID`. The four causes are **not distinguished** to the caller (no oracle); the application maps it to generic `NOT_AUTHORIZED` |
| **Logging** | issuance and revocation rows are the audit trail (`issuedBy`, `revokedBy` = `session_user`). The secret, its digest, and cookies are forbidden log fields (RT-16; `docs/LOGGING_PRIVACY_POLICY.md` "session token; cookies"). The M7 implementation MUST add no logging of these values |

### 8.3 Why this is not a detachable consent authorization token

The capability carries **no consent material**: no grant identity, no interval, no `optionalEvidenceConsent`, no policy, no purpose, no evaluation result, no operation identity. Possessing it authorizes nothing; every consent-conditioned write still enters the sealed CCA procedure, which evaluates the unchanged A1 predicate at the sampled collection instant (CCA §8, §30). It cannot be used as, or converted into, an authorization result, and it reaches no M7 business caller as a value (CCA §5, §31).

### 8.4 What the capability proves, and its boundary

| Actor | Can act for participant P without P's live session secret? |
| :-- | :-- |
| holds only `pagamenos_m7_participant_rt` (runtime-role actor) | **No** — every `m7.p_*` function re-derives P from the secret digest (**E-A**) |
| holds only `pagamenos_m7_session_issuer_rt` | can mint a session for any P, **cannot write any M7 fact** (no EXECUTE on `m7.p_*`) |
| holds both login credentials | **Yes** — the root of participant trust is authentication (FINAL §28; A1 §12). Separation of the two credentials is required (§18.3) and residual **M7-R-02** records the limit |
| owner-class | no technical guarantee (JBA §19.4) |

---

## 9. Consent-conditioned operation boundary

### 9.1 Consumed exactly

M7 V1.1 consumes Amendment 01 **as accepted** and re-decides none of: sealed per-operation entry points (§6, §10); caller-unselectable policy (§7); unchanged predicate, reader, clock, AGR (§8); no authorization probe (§9); immutable operation input (§12); `LockedCollectionScope` (§13); fixed executor and executor capability contract (§14–§20); tracked adapter and zero-in-flight gate (§21–§25); atomic lock-ordered adapter methods (§26–§27); replay closure (§28); `DatabaseExecutionContext` and re-entry (§29); canonical procedure (§30); accepted-owner allowlist (§33–§39); static enforcement (§42–§45).

```
business operation
→ sealed operation-specific entry point
→ CCA internal transaction boundary
→ assignment lock / ownership re-proof
→ canonical A1 consent evaluation
→ fixed trusted executor
→ operation-specific tracked adapter
→ private adapter implementation
→ hidden TransactionClient
```

### 9.2 M7 sealed operations (the complete set)

| # | Sealed operation (illustrative name) | Leaf module (illustrative) | Fixed policy (CCA §7) | Adapter method | Single DB function |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| SO-1 | `recordAuthorizedOutcomeAssertion` | `src/db/m7-authorized-outcome-operation.ts` | Outcome collection → A1 §8.8 general | `executeOutcomeAssertionCollection` | `m7.p_record_outcome_assertion_v1` |
| SO-2 | `beginAuthorizedEvidenceUpload` | `src/db/m7-authorized-evidence-upload-operation.ts` | SavingEvidence upload → A1 §8.8 + RT-17 | `executeEvidenceUploadAuthorization` | `m7.p_begin_evidence_upload_v1` |
| SO-3 | `submitAuthorizedSavingEvidence` | `src/db/m7-authorized-evidence-operation.ts` | SavingEvidence upload → A1 §8.8 + RT-17 | `executeSavingEvidenceCollection` | `m7.p_finalize_evidence_submission_v1` |

**No other M7 participant write is consent-conditioned, and no other consent policy exists.** SO-2 and SO-3 are both steps of the *SavingEvidence upload* family and use the one evidence policy (AC-07). Treating SO-2 (issuance) as consent-conditioned is conservative: it prevents minting an upload capability for a participant who could not lawfully upload. SO-3 re-evaluates at the instant the submission fact is created, which is *"upload time"* in RT-17's sense for the durable record.

Each leaf, executor and adapter is separate (CCA §10, §20). SO-2 and SO-3 executors may share **pure** helpers only (CCA §15 item 4).

### 9.3 Operation input grammars (validated before CCA, CCA §9.1)

All strings are length-bounded; unknown keys rejected; every field below is immutable from entry (CCA §12). **This table is the complete definition of *caller request material* (RQ) for §9.5.**

| Op | Field | Type / rule | Role |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| SO-1 | `purchaseIntentId` | UUID | selects the `Decision`; assignment derived from it (§9.4) |
| SO-1 | `clientCaptureKey` | 16–128 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` | domain command identity |
| SO-1 | `idempotencyKey` | 16–128 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` | transport identity |
| SO-1 | `assertionKind` | `ORIGINAL` \| `CORRECTION` \| `RETRACTION` | |
| SO-1 | `supersedesAssertionId` | UUID, required iff kind ≠ `ORIGINAL` | |
| SO-1 | `statusLabel` | §6.4 value, required iff kind ≠ `RETRACTION` | |
| SO-1 | `occurrenceAssertion` | `NONE` \| `ATTEMPTED_PURCHASE` \| `REALIZED_PURCHASE`, required iff kind ≠ `RETRACTION` | |
| SO-1 | `merchant` | `{kind:'NOT_ASSERTED'}` \| `{kind:'VOCABULARY_MERCHANT', merchantRef}` \| `{kind:'UNLISTED_MERCHANT'}` | §13.4 |
| SO-1 | `eventTime` | `{kind:'NOT_ASSERTED'}` \| `{kind:'INSTANT', at: RFC 3339 with offset and ≤ 6 fractional digits}` \| `{kind:'LIMA_DATE', date:'YYYY-MM-DD'}` | §13.5 |
| SO-2 | `purchaseIntentId` | UUID | |
| SO-2 | `clientCorrelationNonce` | 22–128 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, ≥ 128 bits entropy (A2 §14.1 pattern) | issuance identity |
| SO-3 | `uploadIntentId` | UUID | |
| **signer** | `generationGrantId` | UUID, opaque; the **only** parameter of `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` beyond the control-plane digest. No object key, prefix, backend, expiry, interval, operation, storage profile or credential identifier is accepted anywhere as a capability-request parameter (XF-12, XF-17). A capability request is **not** a participant operation and is not consent-conditioned: it authorizes nothing new, it re-states an envelope the claim already fixed | resolves exactly one immutable envelope |
| SO-3 | `clientCaptureKey`, `idempotencyKey` | as SO-1 | |
| SO-3 | `supersedesEvidenceId` | UUID or absent | participant replacement (§14.3) |

**Forbidden in every input:** participant id, assignment id, session secret, object key, digest, size, media type, storage profile, backend, lease epoch, vocabulary version, manifest version, policy version, timestamps other than the participant-asserted `eventTime`, policy, operation id, executor, callback, transaction.

### 9.4 How the canonical procedure (CCA §30) is realized for M7

| CCA step | M7 realization |
| :-- | :-- |
| A | per-op grammar (§9.3) |
| B–D | unchanged |
| E | the private CCA engine opens a READ COMMITTED interactive transaction on its **hidden** Prisma client whose datasource authenticates as `pagamenos_m7_participant_rt` (§18.2). This client is constructed only inside the CCA engine module (CCA §33 class B) |
| F–H | **target assignment reference** is resolved read-only from the A2 chain for `purchaseIntentId` (SO-1, SO-2) or from `m7_evidence_upload_intent.assignmentId` (SO-3). The CCA engine then calls `m7.p_lock_and_prove_assignment_v1(secret, participantId, assignmentId)` **inside the hidden transaction**: it validates the session, takes `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on `public.experiment_assignment`, and requires `assignment.participantId = session.participantId = trustedParticipantContext.participantId`. On success the engine binds `LockedCollectionScope { assignmentId, participantId, operationId, policy }` |
| I | accepted service clock sampled once, after F (unchanged). The value is carried into the adapter as `capturedAt` |
| J | consent facts read through the **accepted reader** on its own READ COMMITTED connection (A2 §4.1 Model A; CCA §8.2) — **not** through the M7 role and **not** through any M7 function |
| K–M | unchanged A1 predicate; AGR for SO-2/SO-3; generic `NOT_AUTHORIZED` + rollback |
| N–O | executor receives `(input, LockedCollectionScope, adapter interface)`; its sole DB edge is the adapter method in §9.2 |
| P–S | unchanged zero-in-flight gate, commit |

**Adapter-to-function binding.** Each adapter method issues exactly one `SELECT m7.p_…_v1(…)` via `$queryRaw` on the hidden `TransactionClient`, passing: the session secret (from the M7 session `WeakMap`), `LockedCollectionScope.participantId`, `LockedCollectionScope.assignmentId`, `capturedAt`, the expected control-plane manifest digest, and the §9.3 input fields **and nothing else**. Because each function is atomic and internally lock-ordered (§16.2), the adapter exposes no orderable low-level methods (CCA §26).

### 9.5 Replay and idempotency identity across control-plane rotation (closes `M7V11-AUD-05`)

**The defect being repaired.** If the request hash mixes a *current* control-plane selector the caller never supplied — the active merchant vocabulary version, the active upload transport, the active storage profile — then rotating the control plane changes the hash of an unchanged request and an exact replay is reported as a conflict. That contradicts the exact-replay invariant. The repair is a strict three-way separation, enforced at the level of function signatures.

#### 9.5.1 The three disjoint sets

| Set | Definition | May enter the request hash? | Where it lives |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **RQ — caller request material** | exactly the operation's §9.3 input fields, plus the operation-scope literal and the `assignmentId` derived deterministically from caller-supplied `purchaseIntentId` / `uploadIntentId` | **yes — and nothing else may** | the request hash and the created row |
| **CP — historically derived control-plane facts** | `vocabularyVersion`, `retentionPolicyVersion`, `storageProfileId`, `backendSha256`, `uploadTransport`, `installationId`, `mediaPolicyVersion`, generated object keys, deadlines | **never** | persisted on the created row **and** on its originating receipt, so the historical resolution is recoverable without recomputation |
| **RS — replay result material** | whatever a replay returns to the caller | — | read from the persisted historical rows only; **never** recomputed from the current control plane |

Normative statements:

| # | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| **RP-1** | `m7.i_outcome_request_hash` and `m7.i_evidence_request_hash` take **only** RQ values. No CP value is a parameter of either function (verified by signature inspection and by T-101) |
| **RP-2** | Every receipt row stores the CP facts resolved for the original operation: `m7_outcome_command_receipt.resolvedVocabularyVersion` and `resolvedInstallationId`; `m7_evidence_submission_receipt.resolvedActiveProfileId` and `resolvedInstallationId` |
| **RP-3** | A replay returns RS read from the historical rows. `m7.p_begin_evidence_upload_v1` returns `uploadTransport` and the staging key **of the intent's own `storageProfileId`**, never of the active installation |
| **RP-4** | A *new* (non-replay) operation resolves CP from the **active** installation and fails closed if the caller's material is not admissible there (for example a `merchantRef` absent from the active vocabulary). Rotation therefore changes what may be *created*, never what an exact replay *returns* |
| **RP-5** | `merchantRef` values are stable identifiers drawn from the accepted corpus release ledger. A `merchantRef` MUST NOT be reused for a different merchant across vocabulary versions (§13.4; MA-4). With RP-5, `(merchantKind, merchantRef)` is a stable caller-level identity and the vocabulary-free hash is unambiguous |
| **RP-6** | `m7.i_assert_control_plane` still requires the caller's manifest digest to equal the **active** installation's digest, on replay paths too. That is deliberate fail-closed behaviour against a drifted deployment (§23.6). It gates *whether the current deployment may act at all*; it never reinterprets what a historical row says |

#### 9.5.2 Replay mechanics

- **Pre-CCA optimistic lookup:** SO-1 and SO-3 first call `m7.p_lookup_outcome_receipt_v1` / `m7.p_lookup_evidence_receipt_v1` on a short read-only transaction (session-validated). If a receipt with an equal DB-computed RQ hash exists, the historical result is returned **without consent evaluation and without writes** (CCA §28.1; M7 idempotency authority is this section).
- **In-transaction recheck:** each write function re-checks the receipt and domain identity under its locks (§16.2) before creating anything.
- **SO-2** has no receipt: `UNIQUE(decisionBindingId, clientCorrelationNonce)` returns the existing intent (A2 §5 token pattern). A replay of SO-2 still enters CCA because the lookup is not separately exposed; it creates nothing new and returns RS from the existing intent row (RP-3).

#### 9.5.3 What this makes true across a rotation

| Sequence | Result |
| :-- | :-- |
| SO-1 created under vocabulary V1 → rotate to V2 → exact replay of the same caller material | historical assertion returned, `replayed = true`; **no conflict**; the assertion keeps V1 by FK |
| SO-1 created under V1 → rotate to V2 → same transport key, **changed** caller material | `M7_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` — correctly, because RQ changed |
| SO-1 under V1 → rotate → new transport key, identical caller material | `CAPTURE_ALIAS` receipt recording `resolvedVocabularyVersion = V2` for the alias, while the assertion keeps V1 |
| SO-2 issued on storage profile A → rotate to profile B → exact replay of the same nonce | the same intent, the same staging key, the same `uploadExpiresAt` ceiling, and **A's** `uploadTransport` |
| SO-3 replay after any rotation | the historical submission; no reinterpretation |

### 9.6 What the database proves about the consent boundary, stated honestly

| Property | Enforcement class | Actor it holds against |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| participant substitution in any consent-conditioned write | **E-A** (session digest + assignment re-proof inside every `m7.p_*` function) | every non-owner actor lacking the victim's live secret |
| a consent-conditioned M7 write serializes against A1 withdrawal on `experiment_assignment` | **E-A** (every `m7.p_*` write function takes `FOR UPDATE` on the assignment row itself, a no-op when CCA already holds it) | every non-owner actor |
| the unchanged A1 predicate was actually evaluated as authorizing before the write | **E-E** (CCA module-capability topology + the `pagamenos_m7_participant_rt` credential being reachable only from the private CCA engine) | application-layer actors; **not** a runtime-role actor issuing SQL with that credential |

The third row is **not** strengthened by a database consent check, because that would be a second consent algorithm, which CCA-SEM forbids (§1.3). It is the same boundary A1 and A2 already accept for their own consent-conditioned writes (A2 §4.1, CCA §40.2, §45). It is recorded as residual **M7-R-01** (§28.3). §18.3 makes the credential-scoping requirement a **verified deployment condition** rather than a convention, and §18.3.1 strengthens the topology and its verification without duplicating consent semantics.

## 10. Evidence candidate model — the one-use upload intent

### 10.1 Definition

An **upload intent** (`m7.m7_evidence_upload_intent`) is the evidence **candidate**: a one-use, time-bounded capability authorizing exactly one server-validated evidence object to become at most one `SavingEvidence` record for one participant's one `Decision`, on exactly one immutable storage profile. It is **administrative/operational**, not a domain fact: it asserts nothing about any purchase, creates no scientific denominator effect, and is never read by B or C as evidence.

### 10.2 Bound facts (all immutable after insert)

| Column | Source | Binding purpose |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `id` | DB-minted | capability identity; embedded in the staging key and in every canonical generation key |
| `decisionBindingId` | derived in PostgreSQL from `purchaseIntentId` (§7.3) | the `Decision` the evidence will attach to |
| `assignmentId` | = `LockedCollectionScope.assignmentId`; trigger-verified against the binding chain | participant scope |
| `participantSessionId` | resolved from the secret in PostgreSQL | issuing session (provenance) |
| `clientCorrelationNonce` | op input (RQ) | issuance idempotency |
| **`issuanceProfileId`** | the **active** manifest's storage profile at issuance (SI-2); immutable thereafter | *issuance* provenance: which profile minted this capability, which transport it was issued under (RP-3), and what SO-2 historical replay reports. **Not** a claim about which profile later executed anything (SI-4, §11.8) |
| **`backendSha256`** | copied from the issuance profile and trigger-verified | single-predicate routing identity (SI-1); the **physical home** of every object of this intent, for the life of the row |
| `stagingObjectKey` | DB-generated: `issuanceProfile.backend.stagingPrefix ‖ id ‖ '/' ‖ 32 hex` | the **only** key a client may write |
| `maxBytes`, `mediaPolicyVersion` | copied from the bound retention/media policy | expected content constraints |
| `issuedAt` | `clock_timestamp()` | control-plane time |
| `uploadExpiresAt` | `issuedAt + policy.uploadUrlTtl` (≤ 300 s) | staging write window; signed URL expiry ceiling |
| `intentDeadlineAt` | `uploadExpiresAt + policy.finalizeWindow` (≤ 900 s) | last instant any non-expiry transition may occur |
| **`stagingWriteFenceAt`** | `uploadExpiresAt + backend.providerWriteCompletionWindow + policy.writeFenceSkewAllowance` (SP-9) | the instant after which **no** accepted staging `PUT` can still become visible. No staging delete effect may be executed before it (SI-5, §11.7) |
| `capturedAt` | CCA sampled collection instant | consent-evaluation instant of issuance |
| `retentionPolicyVersion`, `installationId` | active control plane at issuance | binds policy and records the installation event; **never re-read to route storage** |
| `generationPath` | `'M7_BEGIN_EVIDENCE_UPLOAD_V1'` | provenance |

**No `canonicalObjectKey` column exists on the intent.** Canonical keys are allocated per lease epoch in `m7_canonical_generation` (§11.6) — this is the structural half of the `M7V11-AUD-02` repair.

**No `executingProfileId` column exists on the intent either.** An intent executes nothing; it is a capability. The profile that executed a generation is recorded on that generation (§11.8).

Mutable columns — `state`, `stateVersion`, `leaseOwner`, `leaseEpoch`, `leaseExpiresAt`, `acceptedLeaseEpoch`, `rejectionReason`, `failureReason`, `updatedAt` — change only through the §12.1 transitions, enforced by `m7.t_upload_intent_guard` (§19.10).

### 10.3 Relationship chain (the one-use property)

```text
participant session ──validates──▶ SO-2 ──creates──▶ upload intent (ISSUED, staging key, storage profile, expiry)
                                                        │
                        server presigns PUT for stagingObjectKey only, on THIS intent's profile,
                        expiry ≤ uploadExpiresAt
                                                        │
client PUT ─▶ staging object ─▶ storage worker claims (epoch e) ─▶ generation(e) allocated with its OWN
                                  canonical key ─▶ reads back, validates, re-encodes,
                                  conditional-creates generation(e)'s key, reads it back
                                                        │
                   storage observation (epoch e, generation key, size, sha256, media, profile) ─▶ VALIDATED
                                                        │
participant session ──validates──▶ SO-3 ──consumes──▶ intent CONSUMED + SavingEvidence + artifact
                                                     (one transaction; UNIQUE(uploadIntentId),
                                                      UNIQUE(observationId))
                                                        │
                            every generation ≠ acceptedLeaseEpoch ─▶ swept as an orphan (§17.4)
```

| Threat | Closure | Class |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| object-key substitution | no M7 function accepts an object key; the staging key is generated in PostgreSQL at issuance, canonical keys at claim; the observation function copies the key from the generation row | E-A |
| cross-participant use | SO-3 requires `intent.assignmentId = LockedCollectionScope.assignmentId` and `assignment.participantId = session.participantId` | E-A |
| cross-operation reuse | an intent is bound to one `decisionBindingId`; the submission's `outcomeId` must resolve to that binding (trigger) | E-A |
| replay / double consumption | `CONSUMED` is terminal; `UNIQUE(uploadIntentId)` and `UNIQUE(observationId)` on submissions | E-A |
| stale authorization reuse | every transition compares `clock_timestamp()` with `uploadExpiresAt` / `intentDeadlineAt` inside PostgreSQL | E-A |
| **stale-epoch canonical write adopted by a newer epoch** | each epoch writes its **own** canonical key; the observation for epoch *e* may only name generation *e*'s key, and the guard requires `leaseEpoch = intent.leaseEpoch` (§11.6) | E-A |
| replacing an already consumed object | clients can write only the staging key; canonical objects are created by the worker with conditional create on a fresh per-generation key and are never re-written; staging bytes are irrelevant after `VALIDATED` | storage protocol + E-A |
| finalizing an unissued object | a submission requires an existing intent in `VALIDATED` and its own observation row bound to the accepted generation | E-A |
| caller-controlled trusted metadata | size, digest, media type, encoder generation and executing profile are written only by `pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt` under a matching lease epoch; SO-3 input has no such fields | E-A (role + function ACL) |
| **stale epoch re-creates its own key after that key was deleted and proved absent** | generation `e`'s key can be created only with a capability whose **authorization envelope** is generation `e`'s own, and every such envelope's provider-enforced validity ends at exactly `grantExpiresAt` — **however many capabilities were signed** (XF-11); the key's delete effect is not executable before `writeFenceAt = grantExpiresAt + providerWriteCompletionWindow + writeFenceSkewAllowance` (§11.7) | storage protocol + E-A + E-D + **E-E** (the signer half, M7-I119) |
| **false execution provenance after a rotation** | generation, observation and artifact persist the **executing** profile, and the observation's `encoderGeneration` is composite-FK-bound to that profile's pinned encoder (§11.8) | E-A |
| client-supplied storage success claim | the only success evidence the DB accepts is a worker observation of bytes the worker itself read back from the bound profile | storage protocol + E-A |
| **historical object addressed on the wrong backend** | every storage-bearing row carries `storageProfileId` + `backendSha256`; routing and confirmation require backend equality (SI-1…SI-3) | E-A / E-D |

## 11. Object-storage capability model

### 11.1 Storage identity: backend, profile, generation (closes `M7V11-AUD-01`)

#### 11.1.1 The failure this replaces

With storage properties held only in the rotatable manifest, the following state is representable and produces a **false proof of deletion**:

```
manifest/storage profile A  →  canonical object K physically stored in container A
rotate to storage profile B
later deletion of historical K
  → worker executes DELETE / HEAD against container B
  → B reports absent
  → DB records ABSENT_CONFIRMED / DELETED
  → bytes still exist in container A
```

No amount of prose or application-side mapping fixes this, because PostgreSQL has nothing to bind the historical row to. V1.1 therefore gives PostgreSQL the binding.

#### 11.1.2 Two levels of identity

| Level | Table | What it fixes | Digest |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **backend** | `m7.m7_storage_backend` | `providerClass`, `containerId`, `regionId`, `endpointIdentity`, `stagingPrefix`, `evidencePrefix`, `providerWriteCompletionWindow` — *where the bytes physically are, and how long an accepted write there may still land* | `backendSha256` (PK), recomputed by PostgreSQL from those seven fields |
| **profile** | `m7.m7_storage_profile` | one backend **plus** `credentialProfileId`, `credentialGeneration`, `uploadTransport`, `decoderGeneration`, `encoderGeneration`, `storageCapabilityVersion`, `conditionalCreateMode`, `writeCapabilityMode`, `envelopeEnforcement` — *how the server is currently entitled and equipped to act on that backend, and **which layer holds the write-capability envelope*** (§11.7.4) | `profileSha256` (UNIQUE), recomputed by PostgreSQL from the profile fields **including** `backendSha256` |

The backend additionally fixes `providerWriteCompletionWindow` — the provider-enforced upper bound on the time from a write request being accepted to its object becoming visible (SP-9). It is an identity field of the backend and therefore a component of `backendSha256`: changing it is a **new backend**, because every write fence M7 ever computed depends on it.

No secret is stored. `credentialProfileId` **names** a credential set held by the deployment; `credentialGeneration` counts its rotations. `endpointIdentity` is a host/authority identity string, not a URL carrying a token. `writeCapabilityMode` names the *kind* of exact-key write capability the profile can mint (§11.7), never a key or signature.

#### 11.1.3 The distinction the audit requires: credential rotation versus backend rotation

| Operational act | Effect on identity | Effect on historical objects |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **credential rotation** (new keys, same container) | a **new profile row**, `credentialGeneration + 1`, **same `backendSha256`** | fully addressable: routing requires only backend equality (SI-3), so lifecycle operations continue |
| **transport change** (`PRESIGNED_PUT` ↔ `SERVER_MEDIATED`) | new profile, same backend | historical intents keep their own transport (RP-3); new intents use the new one |
| **codec generation change** (decoder/encoder pinned versions) | new profile, same backend | historical observations record the **executing** profile that produced their bytes and composite-FK its `encoderGeneration` (§11.8); canonical-generation interpretation is never re-derived from the active profile |
| **backend rotation** (different container, region, provider or prefix) | a **new backend row**, new `backendSha256`, and a new profile over it | historical objects remain bound to the old backend and MUST continue to be addressed there. The old backend MUST NOT be retired while any live object is bound to it (§11.4) |

#### 11.1.4 Where the binding is carried

| Row | Profile column | Role of that column | Carries `backendSha256` |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7_evidence_upload_intent` | `issuanceProfileId` | **issuance**: which profile minted this capability (SI-2) | yes |
| `m7_canonical_generation` | `executingProfileId` | **execution**: the live profile the claim ran under, whose codec pipeline and credentials produce this generation's bytes (SI-4) | yes |
| `m7_storage_observation` | `executingProfileId` | **execution**: the bytes were read back through this authority under this profile; its `encoderGeneration` is FK-bound to that profile's pinned encoder | yes |
| `m7_evidence_artifact` | `acceptedExecutingProfileId` | **execution**: copied from the **accepted generation**, never from the intent | yes |
| `m7_storage_outbox` | `enqueuedProfileId` | *provenance of enqueueing only.* Routing at execution time is resolved fresh by `m7.i_require_routable_profile(backendSha256)`; nothing trusts this column to route | yes |
| `m7_storage_effect_attempt` | `executingProfileId` | **execution**: proves which authority the attempt actually addressed | `executingBackendSha256` |
| `m7_reconciliation_finding` | `executingProfileId` | **execution**: the profile the listing ran under | yes |
| `m7_generation_write_grant` | — (none) | **envelope**: the immutable authorization envelope of one generation's canonical write. It names the backend directly and no profile at all, because a credential rotation must not be able to alter an envelope already issued | yes |
| `m7_generation_capability_mint` | — (none) | **evidence**: one append-only row per mint of that envelope, carrying the envelope digest; its backend is FK-bound to the grant's | yes |

Every one of these is trigger-verified for internal coherence (`profile.backendSha256 = row.backendSha256`, enforced declaratively by a composite FK to `m7_storage_profile (id, backendSha256)`) and for parent coherence on the axis that is actually invariant:

> **The invariant that travels up the chain is the BACKEND, not the profile.** A generation's `backendSha256` equals its intent's; an artifact's equals its accepted generation's; an outbox row's equals the row that enqueued it. The **profile** is re-resolved at each execution step and recorded there. Requiring profile equality up the chain is exactly the defect `M7V11R2-AUD-02` names, and V1.1 does not do it.

#### 11.1.5 Lifecycle, allowed rotations, rollback, retirement

| Concern | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| creation | backends and profiles are created only by `m7.c_register_storage_backend_v1` / `m7.c_register_storage_profile_v1`, owner-class only, inside a governed rotation transaction |
| immutability | every identity column of both tables is immutable; the **only** permitted update is a one-way retirement (`retiredAt`, `retiredBy`), guarded by `m7.t_storage_profile_guard` / `m7.t_storage_backend_guard` |
| re-registration | supplying an existing `storageProfileVersion` with different content, or an existing `backendSha256` with different fields, **fails** (`55000`) — §23.8 |
| selection for new work | the active manifest names exactly one `storageProfileVersion`; only that profile may be the **issuance** profile of a **new** upload intent (SI-2). Work already issued is *executed* under whichever live profile shares the row's backend at execution time (SI-4) |
| historical routing | SI-1 / SI-3: by `backendSha256` equality against a **live** profile |
| rollback | rolling the manifest back to an earlier version re-selects that manifest's profile for **new** work. It changes nothing about historical rows, and it cannot resurrect a retired profile: `m7.c_activate_manifest_v1` refuses to activate a manifest whose storage profile is retired (§19.11.2) |
| profile retirement | permitted whenever **another live profile exists over the same backend** (the ordinary credential-rotation case). Retiring the **last** live profile of a backend is permitted only when `m7.i_backend_is_drained` returns NULL for that backend — the *same* predicate `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` uses (§11.9) |
| backend retirement | permitted **only** when (a) the backend is **not** the one the **active** manifest's profile routes to (RT-2, §11.10.2 — checked first and refused distinctly with `55000`, because this is a coherence question and not a drain question), **and** (b) `m7.i_backend_is_drained` returns NULL. There is exactly **one** definition of "drained" in this specification, it covers seven classes (§11.9), and both retirement functions call it. `m7.c_retire_storage_backend_v1` raises `M7009` with the blocking class in `DETAIL`; `m7.c_retire_storage_profile_v1` raises `M7011` with the same `DETAIL`. Both take the backend's **liveness lock** `FOR UPDATE` before evaluating anything (§11.10.3 BL-3) |
| quiescence | drain includes **write quiescence** (§11.7 XF-7): no generation of the backend may still be inside its `writeFenceAt`, and no upload intent of the backend inside its `stagingWriteFenceAt`. A backend whose fences have not all elapsed is never drained, because a write M7 already authorized could still land on it |
| the consequence | a backend can only be retired once **every** byte M7 ever wrote there is confirmed absent through a `CONFIRMED` delete effect on that backend, *and* no authorized write to it can still arrive. Retirement is therefore a *drain*, never a *reassignment* |

#### 11.1.6 What is now impossible

| Attempt | Outcome |
| :-- | :-- |
| rotate to backend B, then delete historical object K created on A | the outbox row for K carries A's `backendSha256`; a worker executing under B's profile is refused at `m7.w_record_effect_attempt_v1` (`M7011 M7_STORAGE_ROUTING_MISMATCH`); no `ABSENT_CONFIRMED`, no `DELETED` |
| rotate to B and retire A while K still exists | `m7.c_retire_storage_backend_v1` raises `M7009` (§11.9) |
| retire A's **last** live profile while an `ISSUED` or `PROCESSING` intent, an open effect or an un-elapsed write fence remains on A | `m7.c_retire_storage_profile_v1` calls the same `m7.i_backend_is_drained` predicate and raises `M7011` with the blocking class (§11.9) |
| retire the backend the **active** manifest routes to, even when it is drained | `m7.c_retire_storage_backend_v1` refuses `55000` before consulting the drain predicate (RT-2). The only route is rotate → drain → retire, in that order (RT-3, T-172, T-177) |
| issue an intent, allocate a generation, create an artifact, mint a capability or enqueue an effect **between** the drain predicate returning NULL and the retirement committing | the backend **liveness lock**: every path that creates a drain obligation or mints external write authority takes the backend row `FOR SHARE` in phase P2 and re-reads `retiredAt` before its first write (BL-2), and both retirement functions hold it `FOR UPDATE` across the predicate and the update (BL-3). A requeue, lease, attempt or finding only mutates or removes an obligation that already blocks drain, so it cannot race a successful retirement at all (BL-9). The BL-THEOREM of §11.10.6 proves the predicate is evaluated on a state nothing uncommitted can extend (T-173…T-176, T-179, T-182, T-184) |
| rotate credentials/codecs on A, then claim an intent issued under the old profile | permitted, and the generation, observation and artifact record the **new** (executing) profile; the intent keeps its issuance profile (§11.8) |
| rotate credentials on A, then delete K | permitted: the new profile shares A's `backendSha256`; routing succeeds; confirmation is valid |
| mark K deleted after observing absence on B | impossible: absence is only recorded through an attempt row whose `executingBackendSha256` equals the outbox row's, and `t_outbox_guard` O6 re-checks it |
| let an application map decide the backend | the map is irrelevant: the DB refuses any attempt whose declared executing profile does not match, and the worker is *told* the profile by `m7.w_lease_outbox_v1` rather than deriving it |

### 11.2 Provider requirements (profile-declared, deployment-verified, fail closed)

Requirements are asserted **per storage profile**, recorded in the manifest's `storage` block, and verified before a profile may be registered. A backend that cannot satisfy them cannot carry M7 evidence.

| # | Requirement |
| :-- | :-- |
| **SP-1** | private container; public access blocked; no public or CDN URL for any M7 key |
| **SP-2** | presigned PUT restricted to one exact key, provider-enforced expiry, signed `Content-Type`, enforceable maximum `Content-Length` — **required only when** the profile's `uploadTransport = PRESIGNED_PUT` |
| **SP-3** | server credentials scoped to the backend's prefixes, and **no standing write capability over the evidence prefix**: the *staging* credential may write only exact keys under `<stagingPrefix>`; the *worker* credential may `GET/HEAD/DELETE/LIST` under both prefixes and **has no `PUT`, `POST`, `COPY`, multipart-initiate or any other create/overwrite capability under `<evidencePrefix>`**. Canonical bytes are created **only** through a per-generation exact-key write capability (SP-9). This is the deployment half of `M7V11R2-AUD-01` and is an operational prerequisite (IMP-04), not a catalog-verifiable fact |
| **SP-4** | conditional create on server PUT (`If-None-Match: *` or an equivalent atomic create-if-absent), declared as `conditionalCreateMode` |
| **SP-5** | object versioning disabled, or a provider guarantee that `DELETE` leaves no retrievable version within the RT-17 windows |
| **SP-6** | prefix listing |
| **SP-7** | strongly consistent read-after-write and read-after-delete for single-key `HEAD`/`GET` |
| **SP-8** | the backend's identity is stable: `containerId`, `regionId` and `endpointIdentity` designate the same storage namespace for the life of the backend row. A provider-side rename or re-point is a **new backend**, never the same one |
| **SP-9** | **exact-key, time-bounded write capability, with a bounded completion window.** The provider MUST be able to issue a write capability that (a) authorizes creation of **one exact key** and nothing else, (b) has a **provider-enforced** validity end instant after which a request presenting it is rejected, and (c) has a provider-enforced upper bound `W` on the time from a request being *accepted* to its object becoming *visible*, such that a request accepted before the validity end either becomes visible within `W` or is aborted without creating the object. `W` is declared as the backend's `providerWriteCompletionWindow` and is part of `backendSha256`. The capability kind is declared per profile as `writeCapabilityMode` (`EXACT_KEY_PRESIGNED_PUT` or `EXACT_KEY_SCOPED_TOKEN`) |
| **SP-10** | the provider MUST reject a create for a key the capability does not name, including a key differing only in the epoch segment, and MUST NOT accept a capability that names a prefix rather than a key |

If the deployed provider cannot satisfy SP-2, the profile MUST declare `uploadTransport = SERVER_MEDIATED` (the client sends bytes to the server upload route, which writes the staging key itself under the same state machine, with the same exact-key capability). If SP-1 or SP-3–SP-10 cannot be satisfied, M7 evidence operations are **disabled** (control-plane fail-closed, §23.6). FINAL §3's "Vercel Blob" is a stack choice, not a capability guarantee (AC-09).

**SP-9 is stated as a capability requirement with an arithmetic consequence, not as an assumption.** `W` is a deployment commitment in exactly the way `schedulerWorstCaseLag` already is (IMP-08): it enters the fence arithmetic of §11.7 explicitly, it is verified at backend registration, it is published in the manifest, and its value is an identity component of the backend so that no rotation can change it silently. A deployment that cannot bound `W` cannot register a backend, and therefore cannot run M7 evidence operations. This is recorded as **IMP-15** (§28.1) and as author judgement call **J-14** (Appendix A.4). It is not an authority conflict: no controlling artifact says anything about provider write-completion semantics, so nothing is being overridden — a requirement is being added.

### 11.3 Content pipeline (storage worker; RT-17)

| Step | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| 1 | select work with `m7.w_list_claimable_upload_intents_v1`, then claim the intent with `m7.w_claim_upload_intent_v1`, which returns epoch `e`, **the freshly allocated canonical key of generation `e`**, generation `e`'s **write-grant expiry and write fence** (§11.7), and the **live executing profile** and backend identity the worker must use — never the intent's issuance profile (§11.8) |
| 2 | using **that profile's** credentials, `HEAD` then `GET` the staging key with a read cap of `maxBytes + 1` bytes; absent → release (`m7.w_release_upload_intent_v1`) |
| 3 | size `≤ maxBytes`, else reject `SIZE_EXCEEDED` |
| 4 | **magic bytes decide the family**: JPEG `FF D8 FF`; PNG `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`; WEBP `52 49 46 46 ?? ?? ?? ?? 57 45 42 50`. Anything else → `MAGIC_BYTES_MISMATCH`. The declared `Content-Type` is ignored for classification (AC-02) |
| 5 | decode with the **executing profile's** pinned `decoderGeneration` in a bounded sandbox (pixel count `≤ policy.maxPixels`, CPU/time/memory limits); failure → `DECODE_FAILED` |
| 6 | re-encode from decoded pixels with the **executing profile's** pinned `encoderGeneration` to `policy.canonicalMediaType`; no EXIF/XMP/IPTC/comment segments are emitted; failure → `REENCODE_FAILED` |
| 7 | **ask the sealed signer for generation `e`'s write capability, passing only the opaque `generationGrantId` returned by step 1** (§11.7.3). The worker holds no object key, backend, expiry or operation it could vary, holds no signing credential (XC-3, XC-5), and has no EXECUTE on `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` (XF-13). The signer resolves the envelope itself — `CANONICAL_CREATE`, generation `e`'s exact key, that backend, `validUntil = grantExpiresAt` — **and the signing profile** (XF-17: the generation's executing profile if still live, otherwise the live profile of the same backend and capability kind), records the mint, **commits**, and only then signs **that** envelope with **that** profile's credential and nothing else (XF-16). The worker then conditional-creates generation `e`'s own canonical key with the returned capability. Because that key was allocated to epoch `e` alone, is globally unique, and no envelope M7 can mint is wider (XF-11), a conflict means the same epoch already wrote it (safe idempotent retry); a conflict is never another epoch's object. A request not accepted before `grantExpiresAt` is rejected by the provider, and the signer refuses to mint at or after that instant (`M7013`, XF-14); the worker MUST then stop and let the lease lapse. **Re-asking the signer is permitted and harmless** — it returns the identical envelope (Corollary 4) — but it cannot buy more time |
| 8 | `GET` generation `e`'s key back; compute SHA-256, byte size, media type **of the stored bytes** |
| 9 | `m7.w_record_validated_observation_v1(intentId, e, size, sha256, mediaType, executingProfileId, encoderGeneration, providerEtag)` — the function rejects unless `e` is still the intent's current lease epoch, unless `executingProfileId` is the profile recorded on generation `e`, and unless `encoderGeneration` equals that profile's pinned value (§11.8) |

PDF is never accepted (AC-01). The server — never the client — authors every value recorded in step 9. Every provider call in steps 2–8 is issued under the credentials of a **live** profile sharing the intent's `backendSha256`, and that profile is the one the DB handed back in step 1 and recorded on generation `e`; the worker never chooses a backend or a profile itself. The only write in the whole pipeline is step 7; it is exact-key and expiry-bounded, and the worker is not the party that decides either bound.

### 11.4 Signed upload URL bounds (`PRESIGNED_PUT` profiles only)

| Bound | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| purpose | writing the staging object of one issued intent; nothing else |
| issuance point | after SO-2 commits, in the M7 business layer, from the committed row, using the credentials of the intent's **own** profile (RP-3) |
| object binding | exactly `stagingObjectKey`, on exactly that intent's backend |
| method | `PUT` only |
| content | signed `Content-Type ∈ {image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp}`; `Content-Length ≤ maxBytes` |
| TTL | provider expiry `≤ uploadExpiresAt`; never later. A replayed SO-2 re-signs the same key with the same absolute ceiling |
| participant / operation association | through the intent row only; the URL carries no participant data |
| one-use | **not provider-enforced**. One-use is a DB property: at most one accepted generation, at most one observation and at most one submission per intent. Repeat PUTs only overwrite staging bytes, which stop mattering once the intent leaves `PROCESSING` |
| post-expiry | provider rejects a request presented after `uploadExpiresAt`; by SP-9 a request accepted just before it either becomes visible by `stagingWriteFenceAt = uploadExpiresAt + providerWriteCompletionWindow + writeFenceSkewAllowance` or is aborted.
