A late staging object, if any, exists only before that instant, is an orphan, and is swept (§17.4) |
| **staging write fence** | no staging delete effect is *executable* before `stagingWriteFenceAt` (SI-5, §11.7). This is why a staging `DELETE` + `HEAD` → `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` is a durable absence claim and not a race with a `PUT` that was accepted a moment earlier |
| revocation | a presigned URL cannot be revoked before expiry. Exposure is bounded to ≤ 300 s and to the staging zone of one backend |
| logging | the URL, its query string and signature are forbidden log fields (RT-16) |
| meaning | **issuing a URL is not an upload; a successful PUT is not canonical evidence.** Canonical evidence exists only as a committed `m7_evidence_submission` whose artifact is `AVAILABLE` on a named backend |

**Byte migration between backends is refused.** No M7 function copies, re-points or rebinds an object from one backend to another. `m7_evidence_artifact.storageProfileId` and `backendSha256` are immutable; `m7.c_retire_storage_backend_v1` drains rather than migrates (§11.1.5). A future artifact wishing to migrate must specify copy → independent read-back verification → rebind → delete-and-confirm-on-source, with its own adversarial suite; V1.1 grants no such path.

### 11.5 Signed download URLs

**None are issued in V1.1.** No M7 operation returns evidence bytes or a URL to any principal. Verification access is a C1 concern (§22); a future C1S that needs reads MUST specify a verifier capability, TTL ≤ 60 s, single key, `GET` only, the backend identity it reads from, audit rows, and invalidation-by-deletion semantics before any download URL exists. Consequently RT-17's *"signed links invalidated, CDN/cache purged"* on withdrawal is satisfied vacuously in V1.1.

### 11.6 External generation fencing (closes `M7V11-AUD-02`)

#### 11.6.1 The failure this replaces

`leaseEpoch` fences the **PostgreSQL** completion but not the **external** side effect. With one fixed canonical key per intent:

```
1. worker W1 claims epoch e
2. W1 processes bytes
3. W1's lease expires
4. worker W2 claims epoch e+1
5. W1 conditional-creates THE canonical key → W1's object now exists
6. W1's DB completion is correctly rejected (M7_STALE_LEASE)
7. W2 conditional-creates THE canonical key → sees it exists, reads it back
8. the object authored by the stale epoch e becomes the canonical object attributed to epoch e+1
```

The DB-side statement *"the stale write is either the same object or an orphan"* is **false** here: W1 and W2 may have decoded, sanitised and re-encoded differently (different `decoderGeneration`/`encoderGeneration`, different sandbox outcome, different staging bytes after a re-PUT). Step 8 is an adoption of un-fenced external work.

#### 11.6.2 The repair: one canonical key per generation

Every claim allocates a **new, globally unique canonical object key bound to exactly one `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)`**:

```text
upload intent I
  ├─ generation (I, e)    → key  <evidencePrefix>I/g{e}/{32 hex}        ← only epoch e may write it
  └─ generation (I, e+1)  → key  <evidencePrefix>I/g{e+1}/{32 hex'}     ← only epoch e+1 may write it
```

| # | Rule | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **GF-1** | A canonical key exists only as a row of `m7_canonical_generation`, allocated inside `m7.w_claim_upload_intent_v1` in the same transaction that advances `leaseEpoch` | `PRIMARY KEY (uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)`, `UNIQUE(canonicalObjectKey)`, insert guard + path |
| **GF-2** | The key embeds the intent id **and** the epoch; the 32-hex suffix is DB-generated and never reused | `CHECK` on shape + `UNIQUE` |
| **GF-3** | A worker holding epoch `e` is told only generation `e`'s key. It has no DB path to any other generation's key | `w_claim_upload_intent_v1` returns exactly one key |
| **GF-4** | An observation must name generation `(intentId, leaseEpoch)`'s key and is refused unless `leaseEpoch` is still the intent's current epoch | composite FK to `m7_canonical_generation` + `m7.t_observation_coherence` + the function's `M7_STALE_LEASE` check |
| **GF-5** | The intent records `acceptedLeaseEpoch` when it reaches `VALIDATED`; it is immutable afterwards | `t_upload_intent_guard` U5 branch |
| **GF-6** | `m7_evidence_artifact` binds `(uploadIntentId, acceptedLeaseEpoch)` and that generation's key by composite FK; no other generation can become the artifact | composite FK + `t_artifact_coherence` |
| **GF-7** | Every generation whose epoch ≠ `acceptedLeaseEpoch` is an **orphan** as soon as the intent leaves `PROCESSING`, and is enqueued for deletion by `m7.w_sweep_superseded_generations_v1` and by reconciliation classification `SUPERSEDED_GENERATION_OBJECT` | worker function + `w_classify_object_key_v1` |
| **GF-8** | Conditional create remains the write mode for a generation key, so a same-epoch retry after a partial failure is idempotent and never overwrites | SP-4 |
| **GF-9** | There is no "latest wins" and no arbitrary overwrite anywhere in the canonical path: a key is written at most once, by one epoch, and adopted only if that epoch was current when the observation was recorded | GF-1…GF-6 |

#### 11.6.3 What the database now proves

| Question | Proof |
| :-- | :-- |
| which generation produced the accepted object? | `m7_evidence_artifact.acceptedLeaseEpoch` → `m7_canonical_generation` row → its unique key, and `m7_storage_observation.leaseEpoch` equals it (composite FK + `UNIQUE(uploadIntentId)` on observations) |
| could a stale epoch's object have become that object? | no: the stale epoch's key is a different row of `m7_canonical_generation` and can never be the artifact's key (GF-6) |
| is the stale object sweepable? | yes, unambiguously: it is a generation row with `epoch ≠ acceptedLeaseEpoch` (GF-7) |
| is crash recovery still possible? | yes: a reclaim at `e+1` re-reads the staging object and writes its own key. The crashed epoch's partial object is an orphan, not a blocker (§17.3 CB-04/CB-05) |
| can two encoder generations collide? | no: they are different profiles, different epochs, different keys; only the accepted epoch's bytes are ever bound |

The cost is explicit and accepted: after a lease expiry the re-encode is redone, and one extra object is written and later deleted. V1.1 prefers a bounded duplicate object over an unfenced adoption.

#### 11.6.4 What §11.6 does **not** prove, and where that is repaired

Per-generation keys prove that **no newer epoch can adopt a stale epoch's bytes**. They do **not** prove that a stale epoch has lost the *ability to write its own key*. With a prefix-wide worker write capability the following remains representable, and it is what `M7V11R2-AUD-01` names:

```
W1 holds epoch e and key K_e        lease expires        epoch e+1 proceeds
K_e is classified superseded        DELETE K_e           HEAD K_e -> absent
outbox -> CONFIRMED                 backend drained/retired
W1 resumes and conditional-creates K_e  -> bytes exist again after a proof of absence
```

`ABSENT_CONFIRMED` would then be a statement about a moment, not a property, and every drain, retirement and deletion-completion claim built on it would be unsound. "Reconciliation will delete it again" is **not** a repair: it concedes that the absence proof was not a proof. §11.7 removes the capability instead.

---

### 11.7 True external write fencing and the sealed capability signer (closes `M7V11R2-AUD-01` and `M7V11R3-AUD-01`)

#### 11.7.0 What the previous candidate got wrong, stated plainly

The round-2 candidate removed the standing prefix-wide `PUT`, introduced the per-generation grant row, `grantExpiresAt`, `writeFenceAt`, XF-DL-1 and the provider write-completion window `W`. **All of those ideas are preserved here.** Its proof, however, rested on this step:

> *exactly one such capability has ever existed for `K_e`*

justified by `PRIMARY KEY (uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)` on `m7_generation_write_grant`. That justification does not hold. The signature or token is produced **outside** PostgreSQL, by a credential that round 2 placed in the storage-worker environment. The primary key proves *exactly one grant **row***; it says nothing about how many physical capabilities were signed against that row. So this remained representable with **no** database mutation at all, and it falsifies the round-2 XF-9 and step (2) of the round-2 theorem:

```text
DB generation e, key K_e, grantExpiresAt = T, one grant row

mint token #1:   key = K_e   validUntil = T
   (later, no DB write of any kind)
mint token #2:   key = K_e   validUntil = T + 1 hour
```

No `PRIMARY KEY`, `CHECK` or trigger observes token #2. V1.1 round 3 therefore **stops claiming physical token uniqueness** and proves a different, implementable property instead.

#### 11.7.1 The property that must be proved

> **XF-GOAL (envelope form).** For every provider capability M7 can ever mint for generation `(I, e)`, the **authorization envelope** is exactly
>
> ```text
> operation   = canonical create only
> objectKey   = generation.canonicalObjectKey     (one exact key)
> backend     = generation.backendSha256          (one storage authority)
> validUntil  = generation.grantExpiresAt         (one absolute instant)
> ```
>
> and **nothing M7 can mint may widen it**: not a broader key or prefix, not a different key, not another generation's key, not a later absolute expiry, not another backend, not another operation.

Two capabilities bearing the **identical** envelope are harmless: they authorize the same single create of the same key on the same backend until the same instant, and conditional create (SP-4) makes the second one either a conflict on an existing object or a byte-identical retry. What must be impossible is a **wider** envelope. That is the property this section proves, and it is the property the arithmetic of `writeFenceAt` actually needs — the fence depends on the **latest absolute expiry any capability for `K_e` may carry**, never on how many were signed.

#### 11.7.2 The three quantities (unchanged from round 2)

| Symbol | Column | Kind | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **G** | `m7_retention_policy."generationWriteGrantTtl"` | policy | provider-enforced validity of one generation's write capability, measured from its allocation |
| **W** | `m7_storage_backend."providerWriteCompletionWindow"` | backend identity (part of `backendSha256`) | SP-9 bound on the time from a write request being *accepted* to its object becoming *visible*; a request exceeding it is aborted without creating the object |
| **Λ** | `m7_retention_policy."writeFenceSkewAllowance"` | policy | allowance for skew between the PostgreSQL clock that computes the fence and the provider clock that enforces expiry |

```text
grantExpiresAt = generation.allocatedAt + G
writeFenceAt   = grantExpiresAt + W + Λ          -- persisted, immutable, per generation
stagingWriteFenceAt = intent.uploadExpiresAt + W + Λ   -- persisted, immutable, per intent
```

> **XF-DL-1 (verified, not assumed).** `G + W + Λ ≤ policy.workerLease`.
> Consequence: `writeFenceAt ≤ leaseExpiresAt`. **The instant a lease expires, that epoch's write fence has already passed.** Because W is a backend field and G, Λ are policy fields, the relation spans two tables and therefore cannot be a single-table `CHECK`: it is verified in `m7.c_activate_manifest_v1` (which binds exactly one policy and one profile, §19.11.2) and re-verified per allocation in `m7.w_claim_upload_intent_v1`, which raises `M7012` if the computed fence would outlive the lease it is issuing.

The trade is explicit: **G, not the lease, is the real write budget.** A worker whose `PUT` is not accepted before `grantExpiresAt` MUST abandon the epoch. It cannot obtain a capability with a later expiry (XF-11) and it cannot obtain any capability at all after that instant (XF-14), so the only way forward is a reclaim at `e+1`, which is safe precisely because `e`'s fence has passed.

#### 11.7.3 The sealed signer edge (the round-3 architectural repair)

The repair is a **capability-topology** change, not another constraint. The envelope is removed from the caller's hands entirely.

```text
storage worker  ──(generationGrantId, an opaque uuid)──▶  capability signer module
                                                              │
                                    m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1(manifestSha256, generationGrantId)
                                                              │
                                          resolves, from immutable rows only:
                                            generationGrantId
                                              → m7_generation_write_grant     ("id" is UNIQUE)
                                              → (uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)
                                              → canonicalObjectKey
                                              → backendSha256
                                              → grantExpiresAt
                                              → capabilityOperation = CANONICAL_CREATE
                                                              │
                                          locks (P1) the intent, (P2) the backend liveness row,
                                          THEN reads the clock (XF-14) and refuses at or after
                                          grantExpiresAt
                                                              │
                                          resolves the SIGNING PROFILE (XF-17): the generation's
                                          executing profile if live, else the live profile of the
                                          same backend and the same capability kind; none -> refuse
                                                              │
                                          returns exactly that envelope plus the signing profile's
                                          credential identity, appends one
                                          m7_generation_capability_mint row (trigger-stamped instant,
                                          one composite FK over grant id + generation + envelope + kind)
                                                              │
                          signer COMMITS, and only then signs THAT envelope with THAT profile's
                          credential (XF-16); the worker never names a credential
```

There is **no** `mintCapability(key, validUntil)` anywhere in M7. The worker never holds an envelope component it could vary; it holds an opaque identifier.

| # | Rule | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **XF-1** | No M7 credential holds a standing write capability over `<evidencePrefix>`. The worker credential is `GET/HEAD/DELETE/LIST` only there | SP-3 + SP-9; deployment condition verified per §18.3 and published as `storage.capabilities.credentialScopes[]`; **IMP-04**, **T-138b** |
| **XF-2** | Canonical bytes are created **only** with a capability whose envelope is the one of XF-GOAL. `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` is the **only** M7 function that returns a capability envelope, and it takes **one** parameter beyond the control-plane digest: an opaque `generationGrantId` | SP-9, SP-10; `m7_generation_write_grant` holds the envelope; `m7_generation_capability_mint` records every mint; exact-set EXECUTE ACL (§19.13.2) |
| **XF-3** | Every generation is fenced **by construction**: `grantExpiresAt` and `writeFenceAt` are `NOT NULL` columns of `m7_canonical_generation`, derived in the claim and immutable | `t_generation_coherence` recomputes both from `allocatedAt`, the bound policy and the backend's `W`; `t_forbid_mutation` forbids any update |
| **XF-4** | A generation is *writable* only while `now < writeFenceAt`; after that instant **no envelope M7 can mint** authorizes creating its key, because every envelope's `validUntil` is `grantExpiresAt` and `grantExpiresAt + W + Λ = writeFenceAt` | XF-1 + XF-11 + XF-14 + SP-9 (proof in §11.7.5) |
| **XF-5** | **No delete effect for an object is executable before that object's fence.** `notBefore` of a canonical effect is at least the generation's `writeFenceAt`; of a staging effect at least the intent's `stagingWriteFenceAt` | `m7.i_enqueue_delete` raises `notBefore` to the fence itself, `m7.t_outbox_coherence` re-verifies it, and `m7.w_lease_outbox_v1` leases nothing with `notBefore > now` |
| **XF-6** | A reclaim to epoch `e+1` requires the previous generation to be fenced (`now ≥ writeFenceAt(e)`) | `m7.w_claim_upload_intent_v1` U3 branch; `M7012 M7_GENERATION_NOT_FENCED`. Implied by XF-DL-1, asserted anyway so no policy value can weaken it silently |
| **XF-7** | A backend is not drained while any of its generations is inside `writeFenceAt` or any of its intents inside `stagingWriteFenceAt`; profile and backend retirement both refuse | `m7.i_backend_is_drained` classes 4 and 5 (§11.9) |
| **XF-8** | No secret, signature, URL or token is stored. The grant row holds the **envelope** — operation, exact key, backend, absolute expiry, capability mode — and the mint row holds the envelope digest, the mint sequence and the minting actor. The signature is computed outside PostgreSQL and is a forbidden log field (RT-16) | DDL (no secret column exists on either table); RT-16 allowlist |
| **XF-9** | **Exactly one grant *row* per generation, ever** — the envelope is allocated once and can never be altered. This is a claim about the **envelope**, not about the number of signatures: §11.7.0 is why the round-2 wording is retired | `PRIMARY KEY ("uploadIntentId","leaseEpoch")` and `UNIQUE("id")` on `m7_generation_write_grant`; `t_forbid_mutation` forbids UPDATE, and DELETE outside `ROW_PURGE` |
| **XF-10** | `W` cannot be lowered under an existing object: it is an identity component of `backendSha256`, so changing it produces a **new backend**, and every fence already computed keeps the `W` it was computed with | `m7.i_backend_digest` covers it; §23.8 |
| **XF-11** | **Envelope immutability and single-grant provenance.** The envelope of a `generationGrantId` is fixed by an immutable row and re-asserted **declaratively on every mint, by one referential edge**: a mint row can exist only if its whole tuple `(grantId, uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch, canonicalObjectKey, backendSha256, grantExpiresAt, capabilityOperation, capabilityMode, envelopeEnforcement)` equals **one** grant row's own. A second mint therefore cannot name a wider key, a different key, another backend, another operation, a later absolute expiry or another capability kind — and it cannot combine grant A's id and envelope with grant B's generation identity, because that nine-component tuple has no referent. Round 3 proved `(grantId + envelope) → one grant` and `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch) → one grant` with two separate foreign keys and nothing tied them to the **same** row (`M7V11R4-AUD-05`); one composite key closes that | `UNIQUE("id","uploadIntentId","leaseEpoch","canonicalObjectKey","backendSha256","grantExpiresAt","capabilityOperation","capabilityMode","envelopeEnforcement")` on the grant + the single composite FK `m7_generation_capability_mint_envelope_fkey` → `23503`, not a trigger judgement (the round-3 `…_generation_fkey` is subsumed and removed); `t_capability_mint_coherence` re-compares generation identity as defence in depth only |
| **XF-12** | **Sealed signer interface.** No M7 function anywhere accepts an object key, a prefix, a backend, an expiry, an interval, an operation, a storage profile or a credential identifier as a parameter of a capability request. The signer's single input is `generationGrantId`; the envelope and the signing profile are **resolved**, never selected (XF-17) | §9.3 forbidden-parameter list extended; the exact signature is pinned by the manifest's `regprocedure` + `prosrc` expectation set (T-135, T-171b) |
| **XF-13** | **Signer topology.** `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` is granted to exactly one role, `pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt`; that role holds EXECUTE on **nothing else**; the storage-worker role does **not** hold EXECUTE on it; and no role holds both. The provider signing credential is loaded by the signer module alone | exact-set EXECUTE comparison (IA-09), **IA-14**, dependency-closure check (IMP-05, IMP-18), T-171b. Classified **E-E** — §11.7.4 |
| **XF-14** | **No capability after expiry, on a clock that cannot be stale.** `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` takes **every** blocking lock it needs first — the intent `FOR UPDATE` (P1, class 4) and the backend liveness row `FOR SHARE` (P2, class 10) — and only **then** reads `clock_timestamp()` and refuses with `M7013 M7_CAPABILITY_REFUSED` when that instant is `>= grant."grantExpiresAt"`, when the grant's epoch is not the intent's current epoch, when the intent is not `PROCESSING`, when the backend is retired, or when no signing profile exists (XF-17). A call that starts before expiry, waits on either lock across `grantExpiresAt`, and wakes afterwards is **refused**; round 3 sampled the clock before the locks and would have minted on the stale instant (`M7V11R4-AUD-04`). The recorded `mintedAt` is not caller- or function-supplied: `t_capability_mint_coherence` **overwrites** it with the trigger's own `clock_timestamp()`, which is at least the function's post-lock instant, and `CHECK ("mintedAt" < "grantExpiresAt")` then makes a mint at or after expiry unrepresentable, even for an owner-class insert that supplies an old instant | post-lock clock in the function + trigger-stamped `mintedAt` + `m7_generation_capability_mint_expiry_ck` (strict); `M7013`; `23514`; **T-170, T-170b** |
| **XF-15** | **Every mint is evidenced.** Each successful mint appends one append-only `m7_generation_capability_mint` row with a monotone `mintSeq`, the envelope digest and the signing profile. Re-minting is therefore *visible* (`mintSeq > 1`) and its envelope digest is provably identical to the first. Concurrent mints of one grant serialize on the P1 intent lock, so they receive consecutive sequence numbers; `UNIQUE("grantId","mintSeq")` is the backstop against an owner-class duplicate | `UNIQUE("grantId","mintSeq")`, `m7.i_capability_envelope_digest`, T-169 |
| **XF-16** | **No signature before a committed mint.** The signer module signs only after the transaction that inserted the mint row has **committed**. A mint whose transaction rolls back, or whose commit outcome is unknown, yields no signature; the signer may call again, which appends a new row with the identical envelope (Corollary 4). Without this rule "every mint is evidenced" would be false for a signature produced against a rolled-back row | signer topology (**E-E**, M7-I126); **T-171d** injects a commit failure after the function returns and asserts that no capability is emitted |
| **XF-17** | **Signer routing without a caller-selected credential.** The credential used for a mint is the signing half of one **signing profile**, resolved by `m7.i_signing_profile(grant)` **after** the liveness lock: the generation's `executingProfileId` if it is still live; otherwise the live profile over the **same** `backendSha256` with the **same** `writeCapabilityMode` and `envelopeEnforcement`, ordered `credentialGeneration DESC, registeredAt DESC, id`; otherwise none, and the mint is refused `M7013`. The envelope is untouched by this choice (the digest excludes it); a credential rotation over the backend changes which credential signs, never what is authorized; a retired profile is never used, because retirement needs the class-10 `FOR UPDATE` the mint's `FOR SHARE` excludes; and neither the worker nor the signer supplies a profile, key, backend, expiry or operation. The mint row records `signingProfileId`, bound by composite FK `(signingProfileId, backendSha256, capabilityMode, envelopeEnforcement)` → `m7_storage_profile (id, backendSha256, writeCapabilityMode, envelopeEnforcement)`, so a mint signed by another backend's or another kind's credential is `23503`; the trigger additionally requires the signing profile to be live | `m7.i_signing_profile`, `m7_generation_capability_mint_signing_profile_fkey`, `m7_storage_profile_id_capability_kind_key`, `t_capability_mint_coherence`; the deployment half — the signer holds signing credentials exactly for the live profiles' `credentialProfileId`s (XC-7) — is **E-E**; **T-171c** |

#### 11.7.4 What each layer actually enforces (no layer is credited with another's work)

| Property | Enforced by | Evidence kind | Class |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| the envelope of a `generationGrantId` is **derived from immutable rows**, and no caller can select any component of it | PostgreSQL: `UNIQUE("id")`, the envelope `UNIQUE`, the mint composite FK, the one-parameter signature, `t_forbid_mutation` | **DB evidence** | E-A |
| **no mint is possible** at or after `grantExpiresAt` (on a clock read after every blocking lock and a trigger-stamped instant), on a retired backend, or for a non-current epoch | PostgreSQL: post-lock function predicate + trigger stamp + strict `CHECK` | **DB evidence** | E-A |
| a mint's grant identity, generation identity, envelope and capability kind all designate **one** grant row, and its signing profile is a live profile of the same backend and kind | PostgreSQL: one nine-component composite FK to the grant; one four-component composite FK to the profile; trigger liveness check | **DB evidence** | E-A |
| the signer signs only after the mint committed, and only with the credential of the signing profile the function returned | deployment capability topology (XF-16, XF-17, XC-7) | **signer / dependency-topology evidence** | **E-E** |
| **every mint is recorded** with an envelope digest, so a re-mint's envelope can be compared byte-for-byte to the first | PostgreSQL: append-only mint table | **DB evidence** | E-A |
| only the signer role can ask for an envelope; the worker role cannot; the signer role can do nothing else | PostgreSQL ACLs, exact-set verified (IA-09, IA-14) | **DB evidence (ACL)** | E-A |
| the **provider** refuses a capability naming a wider key, another key, or carrying a later expiry than the one it was issued with | provider IAM / delegation, **where the provider offers it** — see below | **provider ACL evidence** | E-D |
| the **signer process** signs only the envelope the function returned, holds the only signing credential, and exposes no other signing entry point | deployment capability topology: one module reads the credential, dependency closure proves no other importer, and its only exported function takes `generationGrantId` | **signer / dependency-topology evidence** | **E-E** |
| a stale capability is in fact rejected by the live provider after its expiry, and a near-expiry request is in fact aborted | the real provider | **real-provider behavioural evidence** | E-D |

**On provider IAM.** Where a provider's own delegation system can pin the envelope — a scoped, non-delegatable credential restricted to `create-object` on one exact key with a hard `validUntil` that no derived credential can extend — the backend MUST declare `storage.capabilities.envelopeEnforcement = PROVIDER_IAM`, naming the exact policy document, and the envelope half is then **E-D** (provider-verified). Where the provider offers only a presigned signature over a caller-supplied key and expiry, the envelope is held by **application capability topology** and the backend MUST declare `envelopeEnforcement = SIGNER_TOPOLOGY`, classified **E-E** and carried as residual **M7-R-12**. `envelopeEnforcement` is a component of `profileSha256` (§11.1.2), so the classification cannot drift silently, and §19.13 does **not** claim to verify either one.

**This specification does not collapse those four evidence kinds.** A `PRIMARY KEY` is not evidence that only one external signature exists (§11.7.0). A signer runbook is not an enforcement mechanism. What is claimed is exactly: PostgreSQL enforces envelope *derivation*, mint *refusal* and the *ACL topology*; the provider enforces envelope *validity*; the signer module enforces envelope *fidelity*; and the last of those is **E-E**.

#### 11.7.5 The proof

> **XF-THEOREM (envelope form).** For every generation `(I, e)`, no capability that M7 can mint authorizes creating `K_e` at any instant `t ≥ writeFenceAt(I, e)`. Consequently `K_e` cannot come into existence at or after `writeFenceAt(I, e)` unless an actor holds a provider credential outside M7's issuance (out of scope, §11.7.7).
>
> *Proof.* Let `t ≥ writeFenceAt = grantExpiresAt + W + Λ`.
>
> (1) **Only envelope-bounded capabilities exist.** By **XF-1** no credential M7 hands any worker can create any key under `<evidencePrefix>`, so the only way to create `K_e` is a capability minted for it. By **XF-2** and **XF-12** the sole M7 path producing a capability envelope is `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1`, whose only input is an opaque `generationGrantId`; by **XF-13** only the signer role may call it, and the worker role may not.
>
> (2) **Every such envelope carries the same absolute expiry.** By **XF-11** every mint for a given `generationGrantId` carries `validUntil = grantExpiresAt`, because a mint row naming any other value has no referent on the grant's envelope `UNIQUE` and is `23503`. By **XF-9** and `t_forbid_mutation` the grant's `grantExpiresAt` is immutable. By **XF-14** no mint occurs at or after `grantExpiresAt` at all. Therefore
>
> ```text
> max{ validUntil : any capability M7 mints for K_e } = grantExpiresAt
> ```
>
> **regardless of how many capabilities were signed.** This is the step the round-2 proof got wrong, and it no longer depends on counting tokens.
>
> (3) **No wider key and no other key.** By **XF-11** every envelope names exactly `K_e` on exactly `generation.backendSha256`, with `operation = CANONICAL_CREATE`. By **SP-10** the provider rejects a create for any key the capability does not name — including one differing only in the epoch segment — and rejects a capability naming a prefix. So no capability M7 mints for any other generation, and no capability at all, authorizes creating `K_e` with a later expiry.
>
> (4) **Acceptance is bounded.** By (2) and the provider's enforcement of `validUntil` (SP-9(b)), no request presenting an M7-minted capability for `K_e` can be *accepted* at or after `grantExpiresAt`, up to provider/DB clock skew, which Λ covers.
>
> (5) **Completion is bounded.** By **SP-9**(c) any request accepted strictly before `grantExpiresAt` either becomes visible within `W` of acceptance — hence strictly before `grantExpiresAt + W` — or is aborted by the provider without creating the object.
>
> (4) and (5) exhaust the cases: no acceptance at or after `grantExpiresAt`, and no visibility after `grantExpiresAt + W` for anything accepted earlier. Hence `K_e` cannot come into existence at any `t ≥ grantExpiresAt + W + Λ = writeFenceAt`. ∎
>
> **Premises, named.** (1) rests on XC-1/XC-4 (**provider ACL evidence**, T-138b) and on XF-13 (**signer topology**, **E-E**, T-171b). (2) and (3) rest on database constraints (**E-A**) *and* on SP-10 (**provider ACL evidence**). (5) rests on SP-9(c) (declared, measured, T-142). **The theorem is false if the signer signs an envelope other than the one returned to it** — that is exactly what XF-13 constrains and what §11.7.4 classifies as E-E rather than claiming as enforced.
>
> **Corollary 1 (the audit's scenario is unrepresentable).** By **XF-5** a `DELETE`/`HEAD` on `K_e` is not *executable* before `writeFenceAt`. Every `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` for `K_e` is therefore recorded at some `t ≥ writeFenceAt`, and by the theorem no M7-minted capability authorizes creating `K_e` at or after that instant. `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` for a generation key is thus a statement of **permanent** absence, not of a moment.
>
> **Corollary 2 (reclaim).** A reclaim occurs at `t ≥ leaseExpiresAt ≥ writeFenceAt` (XF-DL-1, XF-6), so epoch `e` is already unable to create `K_e` when epoch `e+1` begins. Combined with §11.6 (epoch `e+1` is told only `K_{e+1}`, and can neither observe nor adopt `K_e`), neither *adoption* nor *late creation* is representable.
>
> **Corollary 3 (drain and retirement).** A mint requires `now < grantExpiresAt < writeFenceAt` (XF-14), so a capability for `K_e` is mintable **only while class 4 of the drain predicate is already blocking** (§11.9). No backend can therefore be in a drained state while one of its keys is still mintable. Combined with the two-sided liveness protocol of §11.10 — which serializes retirement against every path capable of creating new backend-scoped work, minting included — "drained" is a durable property rather than a snapshot, and a retired backend cannot acquire new bytes.
>
> **Corollary 4 (a duplicate envelope is harmless).** If two capabilities with the identical envelope are signed, both authorize the same conditional create of `K_e` on the same backend until the same instant. By SP-4 the second is a conflict on an existing object, never an overwrite, and by (2) it moves no fence. Nothing in §11.6, §11.9, §15.11 or §17.4 depends on the number of signatures — only on the latest absolute expiry, which is fixed.

#### 11.7.6 The six required adversarial cases, executed through the **real** signer and provider path

Each case is driven through `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` and the deployed signer — **not** by inserting a second SQL row — and each names the refusal point explicitly. The full family is §25.18.

| Case | Attempt | Required result | Refusal point | Test |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **A** | mint a second capability for the same generation, same key, `validUntil > grantExpiresAt` | **REFUSED.** The signer has no parameter that can carry a different expiry (XF-12); a forged mint row naming a later expiry is `23503` on the envelope FK (XF-11); and the case asserts that **no** wider token is obtainable through the deployment's only signing path | DB (no parameter; `23503`) **+** signer topology | **T-166** |
| **B** | mint a capability for the same generation naming **another canonical key** | **REFUSED.** No parameter names a key; a forged mint row is `23503` | DB | **T-167** |
| **C** | mint a capability for generation `e` using generation `e+1`'s key — as a second sub-case, `e+1`'s grant id against `e`'s key — and, as a third, an owner-class mint row combining grant A's id and envelope with grant B's `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)` | **REFUSED.** `generationGrantId` resolves exactly one envelope; a cross-generation tuple, and a grant-A/generation-B provenance splice, have no referent on the single nine-component FK (`23503`), and `t_capability_mint_coherence` re-checks epoch currency | DB | **T-168** |
| **D** | re-mint the **same** generation with the exact same key and the same absolute `grantExpiresAt` | **SAFELY ALLOWED**, and provably non-widening: a second `m7_generation_capability_mint` row appears with `mintSeq = 2` and an `envelopeSha256` **identical** to `mintSeq = 1`. The envelope is widened in neither direction (Corollary 4) | permitted by design; envelope equality asserted | **T-169** |
| **E** | request a capability **after** `grantExpiresAt` — including a request that **began before** expiry and **waited** on the intent lock or the liveness lock across it | **REFUSED** with `M7013 M7_CAPABILITY_REFUSED`, because the instant is read after the locks; an owner-class attempt to insert the mint row directly, whatever `mintedAt` it supplies, is `23514` on `m7_generation_capability_mint_expiry_ck` once the trigger has stamped the real instant | DB | **T-170**, **T-170b** |
| **F** | present a **stale** capability to the provider after the fence, after that key's `DELETE` and `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` | **the provider rejects the `PUT`**; `HEAD K_e` remains not-found. A database error alone is **not** a pass | provider | **T-171**, and **T-138** end-to-end |

**T-144 is re-scoped to the external minting boundary.** In round 2 it asserted only that a second SQL row, a fence `UPDATE` and an early reclaim were impossible. Those sub-cases are retained, and T-144 now **additionally** requires cases A, B, C and E to be demonstrated through the real signer entry point, and requires that no *other* entry point capable of signing a write capability exists in the deployment's dependency closure (T-171b). A pass on the SQL sub-cases alone does **not** close `M7V11R3-AUD-01`.

**T-138, T-138b and T-142 keep their real-provider requirement** (IMP-16), unchanged.

**This is not deferred to M7-R-10.** The grant-minting credential is part of M7's own capability topology — round 2 placed it in the storage-worker environment (its XC-3), which is precisely why the defect was reachable without any out-of-band credential. Round 3 moves it into a separate signer module and a separate database role (XF-13, XC-3 rewritten, XC-5, XC-6). The residual it leaves is the **E-E** one of §11.7.7, not M7-R-10.

#### 11.7.7 What this does not claim

- **It does not claim that only one physical token ever existed.** It claims that no envelope M7 can mint is wider than the generation's own, that no mint is possible after that generation's expiry, and that every mint is recorded with its envelope digest. §11.7.0 records why the stronger claim was withdrawn rather than re-asserted.
- **It does not claim PostgreSQL enforces the signer's fidelity.** A signer module that ignored the returned envelope and signed something wider would break the theorem. What the database enforces is that no *M7 interface* offers a wider envelope, that only the signer role may ask for one, that the signer role can do nothing else, and that the worker role cannot ask at all. The remainder is deployment-capability enforcement: invariant **M7-I119**, class **E-E**, residual **M7-R-12**, tested by **T-171b** (dependency closure) and **T-166**. Within one Node process this is an in-process capability model (CCA §45), not a defence against arbitrary code execution — residual **M7-R-02**.
- It does not defend against an actor holding the **object-store credentials themselves** (a provider-console operator, or a compromised deployment secret). That is residual **M7-R-10**, outside M7's threat boundary; the effect of such a write is a `CANONICAL_OBJECT_PRESENT_AFTER_DELETION` reconciliation finding, which with fencing in place can no longer be a tolerated race and is an integrity alarm (§17.4). The object is re-enqueued for deletion, the existing completion record is **not** revoked (append-only), and the finding stands beside it.
- It does not make `W` smaller than the provider makes it. If `W` is large, `G` shrinks to satisfy XF-DL-1, and if no `(G, W, Λ)` fits inside `workerLease`, the manifest **cannot be activated**. Fail-closed, visibly.
- It does not fence anything M7 did not issue: an `UNISSUED_KEY_OBJECT` has no fence, because M7 never authorized a write to it.
- **It does not claim the database proves which credential the signer process actually used.** The database proves which signing profile was *resolved and recorded* for each mint (XF-17), that it was live and of the grant's backend and kind, and that neither caller could choose it. That the signer then used that profile's credential, and only after commit (XF-16), is the same **E-E** topology as M7-I119, stated as M7-I125/M7-I126 and tested by T-171c/T-171d.

### 11.8 Issuance profile versus executing profile (closes `M7V11R2-AUD-02`)

#### 11.8.1 The false provenance this replaces

```
intent issued under profile A1 (encoder E1)      -- stored: intent.storageProfileId = A1
credential + codec rotation on the SAME backend  -- live routable profile becomes A2 (encoder E2)
worker claims the intent after the rotation      -- receives A2's credentials, decoder, encoder
   BUT  m7_canonical_generation.storageProfileId  = A1
        m7_storage_observation.storageProfileId   = A1
        m7_storage_observation.encoderGeneration  = E2   (from A2)
```

The rows then assert that profile A1 produced bytes that profile A2 actually produced, and an observation whose encoder generation belongs to a profile it does not name. The previous candidate made this *worse* than a mislabel by enforcing it: `t_generation_coherence`, `t_observation_coherence` and `t_artifact_coherence` all **required** equality with the intent's profile, so the only representable state was the false one. Retiring A1 then also stranded rows that claimed to have executed under it.

#### 11.8.2 The separation

| Concept | Column | Written by | Meaning, stated exactly |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **issuance** | `m7_evidence_upload_intent."issuanceProfileId"` | SO-2, from the **active** manifest | which profile minted this capability, under which transport, at which capability version. Historical **replay/transport** provenance (RP-3, §9.5). Asserts nothing about execution |
| **execution (generation)** | `m7_canonical_generation."executingProfileId"` | the claim, from `m7.i_require_routable_profile(intent.backendSha256)` | the live profile whose credentials, `decoderGeneration`, `encoderGeneration`, `conditionalCreateMode` and `writeCapabilityMode` this generation is produced with |
| **execution (observation)** | `m7_storage_observation."executingProfileId"` + `"encoderGeneration"` | the observation, copied from the generation | the profile the bytes were written and read back under, and the encoder that actually produced them |
| **execution (artifact)** | `m7_evidence_artifact."acceptedExecutingProfileId"` | SO-3, copied from the **accepted generation** | the profile that produced the live raw object. **Never** copied from the intent |
| **execution (effect)** | `m7_storage_effect_attempt."executingProfileId"` | each attempt | the profile the `DELETE`/`HEAD` ran under (unchanged from V1.1 round 1) |
| **physical home** | `backendSha256` on every one of them | inherited | the one axis that *is* invariant up the chain |

#### 11.8.3 Coherence rules

| # | Rule | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **EP-1** | A generation's `backendSha256` equals its intent's; its `executingProfileId` is a profile **on that backend** and was **live** at allocation | composite FK `(executingProfileId, backendSha256)` → `m7_storage_profile (id, backendSha256)`; `t_generation_coherence` checks `retiredAt IS NULL`; `w_claim_upload_intent_v1` obtains it from `i_require_routable_profile` |
| **EP-2** | A generation's `executingProfileId` **may differ** from `intent.issuanceProfileId`. No trigger, CHECK or FK requires equality | the previously required equality is **removed**; T-118 asserts the difference is representable and recorded |
| **EP-3** | An observation's `executingProfileId` equals **its generation's** | composite FK `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch, executingProfileId)` → `m7_canonical_generation (uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch, executingProfileId)` |
| **EP-4** | An observation's `encoderGeneration` equals **that profile's** pinned `encoderGeneration` — declaratively, not by a trigger | composite FK `(executingProfileId, encoderGeneration)` → `m7_storage_profile (id, encoderGeneration)`, backed by `UNIQUE (id, encoderGeneration)` on the profile. A forged encoder string is `23503`, not a judgement call |
| **EP-5** | The artifact's `acceptedExecutingProfileId` equals the accepted generation's `executingProfileId` | composite FK `(uploadIntentId, acceptedLeaseEpoch, acceptedExecutingProfileId, backendSha256)` → `m7_canonical_generation (uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch, executingProfileId, backendSha256)` |
| **EP-6** | A reconciliation finding's `executingProfileId` is a live profile of the finding's backend at listing time | composite FK + `t_reconciliation_finding_coherence` |
| **EP-7** | Retiring a profile does not strand execution rows: routing needs only a **live profile on the same backend** (SI-3), so a retired executing profile remains a valid *historical* fact and blocks nothing | `i_require_routable_profile`; §11.9 class predicates are backend-scoped, never profile-scoped |
| **EP-8** | SO-2 replay reports **issuance** facts; the trusted-generation projection (§21.3) reports **execution** facts. Neither substitutes for the other | `m7_evidence_submission_receipt."resolvedActiveProfileId"` records what was active for *that operation*; §9.5 RP-2 keeps every control-plane selector out of the request hash |

#### 11.8.4 What the database now proves

| Question | Proof |
| :-- | :-- |
| which profile *issued* this evidence capability? | `intent.issuanceProfileId` — immutable, and still A1 after any rotation |
| which profile *produced* the accepted bytes? | `artifact.acceptedExecutingProfileId` = accepted generation's `executingProfileId` (EP-5), which is A2 when A2 executed |
| is the recorded encoder the executing profile's? | yes, by foreign key (EP-4). No row can name E2 while claiming profile A1 |
| can an artifact silently inherit the issuance profile? | no: the artifact has no column that can hold it, and its only profile column is FK-bound to the accepted generation (EP-5) |
| does retiring A1 invalidate anything? | no: nothing routes through A1; A2 shares the backend (EP-7) |
| can the *backend* silently change across the chain? | no: `backendSha256` equality up the chain is FK-enforced (SI-1) |

**Mandatory end-to-end test (T-118).** Issue an intent on A1/E1; rotate the same backend to A2/E2; retire A1; claim the intent after the rotation; the worker executes with A2/E2; the generation persists A2; the observation persists A2 and E2; the artifact resolves to the accepted A2 generation; SO-2 historical replay still reports A1's issuance facts. Negative halves: an observation naming A1 with E2 fails `23503`; an artifact naming A1 fails `23503`; an observation naming E1 under A2 fails `23503`.

### 11.9 The canonical drain predicate (closes `M7V11R2-AUD-04`)

#### 11.9.1 The failure this replaces

The specification said a profile may be retired when *another live profile exists* **or** *the backend itself is drained*, but `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` implemented only two of the backend predicate's classes (other live profiles, non-`DELETED` artifacts). Two independently written definitions of "drained" had drifted, so the **last** live profile of a backend could be retired while an `ISSUED` or `PROCESSING` intent, staging bytes, or an open or permanently failed outbox effect still existed on it — after which nothing on that backend could be leased, requeued or confirmed, and its bytes were unreachable.

#### 11.9.2 One predicate, seven classes, two callers

`m7.i_backend_is_drained(p_backend_sha256 text) RETURNS text` returns `NULL` when the backend is drained, and otherwise a short reason string naming **the blocking class and its row count**. It is the only definition of drained in this specification.

| Class | Blocks while | Why it implies remaining or future bytes |
| :-- | --: | :-- |
| 1 | an `m7_evidence_artifact` on the backend is not `DELETED` | live raw evidence |
| 2 | an `m7_evidence_upload_intent` on the backend is `ISSUED`, `PROCESSING` or `VALIDATED` | a capability that may still be exercised, and staging bytes that may already exist |
| 3 | an `m7_storage_outbox` row on the backend is not `CONFIRMED` (`PENDING`, `LEASED` **or** `FAILED_PERMANENT`) | an irreversible effect that has not been evidenced as complete |
| 4 | an `m7_canonical_generation` on the backend has `writeFenceAt > now` | XF-7: an authorized write could still land |
| 5 | an `m7_evidence_upload_intent` on the backend has `stagingWriteFenceAt > now` | XF-7, staging zone |
| 6 | an `m7_canonical_generation` on the backend has **no** `CONFIRMED` `DELETE_OBJECT` effect for `(backendSha256, canonicalObjectKey)` | a canonical object M7 wrote there whose absence was never evidenced |
| 7 | an `m7_evidence_upload_intent` on the backend has **no** `CONFIRMED` `DELETE_OBJECT` effect for `(backendSha256, stagingObjectKey)` | a staging object M7 may have written there whose absence was never evidenced |

Classes 6 and 7 are what make §11.1.5's claim — *"every byte M7 ever wrote there is confirmed absent"* — **true** rather than aspirational. Classes 1–3 alone permit a backend with a superseded generation object that was never swept; 6 and 7 do not. Because an authorized `ROW_PURGE` removes an assignment's generations, intents and their effect rows in the **same** transaction (§19.12.5), purged rows contribute to neither side of 6 and 7, so the predicate stays consistent under purge.

| Caller | Use | Failure |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7.c_retire_storage_backend_v1` | always | `M7009 M7_DELETION_PRECONDITION`, `DETAIL` = the reason string |
| `m7.c_retire_storage_profile_v1` | **only when this is the last live profile** of the backend (a non-last retirement is the ordinary credential rotation and stays permitted) | `M7011 M7_STORAGE_ROUTING_MISMATCH`, `DETAIL` = the same reason string |

Both callers evaluate the predicate only after acquiring every lock they take **without waiting**; if any of those locks is held, they raise `M7014 M7_RETIREMENT_BUSY` before the predicate is consulted (§11.10.8), so a busy refusal is never reported as a drain class.

There is no third caller and no second definition. `m7.w_list_storage_scopes_for_sweep_v1`, `m7.w_lease_outbox_v1` and `m7.w_requeue_failed_effect_v1` continue to test **routability** (`i_require_routable_profile`), which is a different question and is deliberately not folded in.

`m7.i_backend_is_drained` contains **no locking clause of any kind** — it is seven pure counting reads. That is a normative property, not an implementation detail: it is what makes the retirement side of §11.10.3 unable to wait on any class 1-9 lock, and therefore what makes the liveness protocol deadlock-free (BL-5, §11.10.5). The source-level check **T-180** asserts it.

#### 11.9.3 Required tests

| Case | Expected |
| :-- | :-- |
| last live profile + `ISSUED` intent | refused, `M7011`, class 2 |
| last live profile + `PROCESSING` intent | refused, `M7011`, class 2 |
| last live profile + `PENDING` outbox row | refused, `M7011`, class 3 |
| last live profile + `FAILED_PERMANENT` outbox row | refused, `M7011`, class 3 |
| last live profile + live artifact | refused, `M7011`, class 1 |
| last live profile + generation inside its write fence | refused, `M7011`, class 4 |
| last live profile + generation with no confirmed delete | refused, `M7011`, class 6 |
| last live profile + fully drained backend | **allowed** |
| non-last profile + another live profile on the same backend | **allowed** (credential rotation) |
| `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` on each of the same blocking states | refused, `M7009`, same class and count |

**T-156…T-162** (§25.21) execute these, and **T-163** asserts the two functions return the **same** blocking class for the same state — the regression test against the two definitions drifting apart again.

**What §11.9 does not settle.** One predicate with two callers removes the *drift*. It does not by itself make retirement **safe**: it says nothing about whether the backend being retired is the one the active control plane routes to, and it says nothing about what may happen between the predicate returning `NULL` and the retirement committing. Those are `M7V11R3-AUD-02` and are repaired in §11.10, which leaves this section's predicate, classes and callers unchanged.

### 11.10 Retirement safety: active-control-plane coherence and the backend liveness protocol (closes `M7V11R3-AUD-02`)

#### 11.10.1 The two defects this replaces

§11.9 gave the drain predicate one definition and two callers. That closed the drift, and it is preserved unchanged. Two things it did **not** close:

**(a) The active control plane could be retired.** `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` refused the **active manifest's profile**. `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` had no equivalent refusal for the **backend the active manifest routes to**, and it retires *every* profile of that backend as part of retiring it. So this was executable:

```text
manifest A active  →  profile A1  →  backend A
A happens to satisfy i_backend_is_drained (no live artifact, no open intent, no open effect, …)

c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)
  → A1 retired
  → A  retired

the active installation still points at manifest A / profile A1
  → i_active_storage_profile(A) now returns a RETIRED profile
  → the next SO-2 binds an intent to a retired profile on a retired backend,
    or fails, depending on which check fires first
```

A drained backend is not an unused backend: "drained" means *no bytes remain*, and a freshly rotated-to backend with no evidence yet is drained by definition. Retiring the active one is therefore not an exotic state, it is the **easiest** state to reach.

**(b) RC-19's serialization proof did not follow.** The round-2 text claimed that taking `FOR UPDATE` on the backend (or profile) row serialized retirement against new issuance and enqueueing. It does not: `p_begin_evidence_upload_v1` reads the active profile, reads the backend and inserts an upload intent **without ever touching that lock**. A lock only serializes parties that take it. The correct statement is that round 2 had a *one-sided* lock and therefore **no** serialization; the window between evaluating `i_backend_is_drained` and committing the retirement was open to every work-creating path.

Both are repaired below. Neither repair weakens §11.9: the drain predicate, its seven classes and its two callers are unchanged.

#### 11.10.2 Active-control-plane coherence (the missing refusal)

| # | Rule | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **RT-1** | `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` refuses the profile of the **active** manifest | unchanged from round 2; `55000` |
| **RT-2** | `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` refuses **any backend referenced by the active manifest's profile**, drained or not, and says so distinctly (`55000`, message `cannot retire the backend of the active manifest`) rather than through the drain predicate. Retiring the active backend is not a drain question; it is a coherence question | `m7.c_retire_storage_backend_v1` joins `m7_control_plane_installation` (active) → `m7_control_plane_manifest` → `m7_storage_profile` and compares `backendSha256`; **T-172** |
| **RT-3** | The only route to retiring a backend is therefore: register the successor backend and a profile over it → `c_activate_manifest_v1` (the active pointer moves) → drain the predecessor → retire it. The order is forced by RT-2, not merely recommended by a runbook | RT-2 + `c_activate_manifest_v1`; **T-177** |
| **RT-4** | Retiring a backend retires every profile over it in the same transaction (unchanged), and RT-2 guarantees none of them is the active manifest's | `c_retire_storage_backend_v1`; CB-16 |
| **RT-5** | Credential rotation on a **live** backend is untouched: retiring a non-last profile while another live profile remains on the same backend consults neither the drain predicate nor RT-2, because the backend keeps routing (EP-7, SI-3) | `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` early branch; **T-178** |

RT-2 and RT-5 together are why the repair does not cost credential rotation: RT-2 constrains **backend** retirement only, and profile retirement of a non-last profile is a different operation with a different precondition.

#### 11.10.3 The backend liveness lock — the exact property, then the mechanism

Round 3 defined the protocol by a syntactic predicate — *"every function that `INSERT`s or `UPDATE`s a row carrying a `backendSha256`"* — and then enumerated a set that did not match its own function bodies (`w_renew_outbox_lease_v1` was listed and took no lock) while forcing locks onto paths that cannot affect retirement. `M7V11R4-AUD-03` asks for the property first. It is:

> **BL-SAFE.** If `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(B)` or `c_retire_storage_profile_v1(P over B, last live)` commits, then (i) at that commit no retirement-blocking obligation exists on `B` — i.e. `m7.i_backend_is_drained(B)` is `NULL` on the committed state — and (ii) no transaction commits a new retirement-blocking obligation on `B`, or mints external write authority for `B`, afterwards.

A **retirement-blocking obligation** is exactly a row satisfying one of the seven drain classes of §11.9. Every write touching a backend-scoped row falls into exactly one of six kinds with respect to that set:

| Kind | Definition over the seven drain classes | Instances in §19 | Liveness lock |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **C — create** | inserts a row that, once committed, satisfies a drain class | `INSERT` into `m7_evidence_upload_intent` (classes 2, 5, 7), `m7_canonical_generation` (4, 6), `m7_evidence_artifact` (1), `m7_storage_outbox` in state `PENDING` (3) | **required** |
| **R — re-open** | moves an existing row from a non-blocking to a blocking state | **none exists**: BL-9 proves it from the guard triggers' transition tables | — (vacuous) |
| **E — extend** | moves the release point of a blocking obligation later | **none exists**: the only time-dependent classes (4, 5) read `writeFenceAt` / `stagingWriteFenceAt`, which are immutable (`t_forbid_mutation`, `t_upload_intent_guard`) | — (vacuous) |
| **M — mint external write authority** | produces a capability able to put bytes on the backend | `INSERT` into `m7_generation_capability_mint` | **required** |
| **U — mutate a blocking obligation** | changes metadata or state of a row that blocks drain before and after the write | outbox `PENDING↔LEASED`, `LEASED→PENDING`, `LEASED→FAILED_PERMANENT`, `FAILED_PERMANENT→PENDING` (requeue), lease renewal; intent `ISSUED→PROCESSING`, `PROCESSING→ISSUED/PROCESSING/VALIDATED`; artifact `AVAILABLE→MISSING`, `→DELETION_SCHEDULED`; attempt, finding, observation, transition, receipt, execution and completion inserts attached to such a row | **none** |
| **D — reduce / remove** | moves a row out of every class, or deletes it | outbox `LEASED→CONFIRMED`; artifact `→DELETED`; intent `→VALIDATED→CONSUMED` (class 2 ends while SO-3 creates class 1 — which is a **C** write in the same transaction), `→EXPIRED`, `→REJECTED_CONTENT`, `→TERMINAL_FAILURE`; every `ROW_PURGE` `DELETE` | **none** |

A transaction must take the liveness lock exactly when it performs a **C** or **M** write. **U** and **D** writes need none, because a retirement cannot commit while the obligation they touch exists (it is visible to the drain predicate as a committed row), and a **D** write can only make a later retirement *possible*, never unsafe.

| # | Rule | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **BL-1** | The lock object is the `m7_storage_backend` row, addressed by `backendSha256`. There is exactly one liveness lock per backend and no other lock is claimed to serve this purpose | §16.2.2 **class 10** |
| **BL-2** | **Exact set.** A function MUST take `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness(B)` (or, for several backends, `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness`) **iff** it — directly or through `m7.i_enqueue_delete` / `m7.i_enqueue_superseded_generations` — performs a **C** or **M** write on `B`. The call is made in phase **P2** (§16.2.5 LG-1): after the function's explicit row locks and **before its first write**. The helper takes `FOR SHARE`, re-reads the row, and raises `M7011 M7_STORAGE_ROUTING_MISMATCH` if `retiredAt IS NOT NULL`. `m7.i_enqueue_delete` keeps an internal call as a fail-safe re-acquisition, which is a no-op for every caller that obeys P2 | `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness`, `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness` (§19.11.1); the set is §11.10.4, published as `database.backendLivenessFunctions[]` (MA-16) and checked in **both** directions by **T-180** |
| **BL-3** | Both retirement functions take the backend row `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` as their **first** lock, before `m7_storage_profile` (also `NOWAIT`), before `i_backend_is_drained`, and before the RT-2 coherence query. **A retirement never waits for any lock** (LG-10): if the backend row is held in any conflicting mode, or a profile row is held, it raises `M7014 M7_RETIREMENT_BUSY` at once, retires nothing, and never becomes a waiter behind which a later `FOR SHARE` could queue (PG-1). *Round 4 took a waiting `FOR UPDATE`; `M7V11R5-AUD-01` shows the cycle that admits* | §19.11.2; **T-173**…**T-176**, **T-190**, **T-193** |
| **BL-4** | A transaction needing liveness on **more than one** backend acquires the locks in ascending `backendSha256 COLLATE "C"` order, through the single helper `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness(text[])`, which sorts and de-duplicates its argument itself. **Five** functions use it: `w_expire_upload_intents_v1`, `w_sweep_superseded_generations_v1`, `w_schedule_withdrawal_deletions_v1`, `w_schedule_retention_deletions_v1`, `w_schedule_authorized_deletion_v1`. Round 3 relied on `ORDER BY` inside a `PERFORM … FROM (…) ORDER BY 1` in the purge, which does not fix the evaluation order of the function calls; that construction is gone | `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness`; **T-179** |
| **BL-5** | `m7.i_backend_is_drained` contains **no locking clause of any kind** and takes no class 1–9 lock. It is a pure read over seven classes | `m7.i_backend_is_drained` source (§19.11.1); **T-180** (iii) |
| **BL-6** | The re-read in BL-2 is **load-bearing**: when retirement commits first, the waiting transaction acquires `FOR SHARE` *after* the update and must observe `retiredAt` | `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness`; **T-173** order 1 |
| **BL-7** | Contention resolves **against the retirement, immediately**: a retirement that meets any holder of the liveness lock raises `M7014` without waiting and without affecting the work transaction, which proceeds and commits normally. The governed rotation pipeline retries under RR-1…RR-7 (§11.10.8). `lock_timeout = '5s'` remains in every `proconfig` (§16.1) but is never the mechanism by which a retirement yields — it bounds only waits that other transactions perform | `NOWAIT`; RR-1…RR-7; **T-176**, **T-193** |
| **BL-8** | Read-only routing checks are deliberately **not** folded in. `m7.i_require_routable_profile` answers "which live profile may address this backend's existing rows"; `m7.w_list_*` functions write nothing and take nothing | §11.9.2's closing paragraph, unchanged |
| **BL-9** | **No re-open and no extension exist.** From the guard triggers of §19.10: no intent transition enters `ISSUED`/`PROCESSING`/`VALIDATED` from a state outside that set; no outbox transition leaves `CONFIRMED`, and every transition into `PENDING`/`LEASED`/`FAILED_PERMANENT` starts inside that set; no artifact transition leaves `DELETED`; generations, grants and mints are immutable; a `CONFIRMED` `DELETE_OBJECT` row disappears only in a `ROW_PURGE` that removes the generation or intent it evidences in the same statement sequence of the same transaction (§11.9.2); and the fences are immutable. Hence **R** and **E** are empty, and a new drain obligation on `B` can only arise through a **C** write | guard-trigger transition tables (§19.10); **T-180** (iv) |
| **BL-10** | **Snapshot soundness of a seven-statement predicate.** `i_backend_is_drained` runs seven `SELECT`s, each on its own READ COMMITTED snapshot. That is sound: by BL-9 the only writes that move an obligation *into* a class are **C** writes, which hold `FOR SHARE` on `B` and therefore cannot commit while the retirement holds `FOR UPDATE`; every other concurrent commit can only move obligations *out of* classes. So no obligation can be missed by being moved from a class not yet evaluated into a class already evaluated | BL-2 + BL-9; **T-184** (b) |

**Derivation rule.** Start from the four **C** tables and the one **M** table of §11.10.3. A function is in the set iff its body contains an `INSERT` into one of them, or calls `m7.i_enqueue_delete` or `m7.i_enqueue_superseded_generations` (the only functions that insert `PENDING` outbox rows). Apply the rule to every `CREATE FUNCTION` in §19.11–§19.13; the result is the table below and nothing else.
