#### 11.10.5 Why there is no deadlock

The class-10 part of the argument is short, and the whole-graph theorem is **LG-THEOREM** (§16.2.8), which this section does not replace. It is stated under the **conservative** PostgreSQL premise PG-1 of §16.2.5: a later compatible row-lock request **may** wait behind an incompatible request already waiting on the same tuple. Nothing below requires the opposite.

1. **A retirement never waits** (BL-3, LG-10). Every row lock it takes is `NOWAIT`, it inserts nothing, its `UPDATE`s touch only rows it already holds, and `i_backend_is_drained` takes no lock (BL-5). A transaction that never waits has no outgoing wait edge, so it lies on no cycle.
2. **No incompatible request ever waits on a backend row.** The only modes ever *requested with waiting* on `m7_storage_backend` are `FOR SHARE` (work in P2; registration and activation) and the implicit `FOR KEY SHARE` of a profile insert, which are mutually compatible; the only conflicting mode, `FOR UPDATE`, is requested only by the two retirements and only `NOWAIT`. Therefore a `FOR SHARE` request on a backend can wait only on a retirement that already **holds** `FOR UPDATE` — case 1 — and can never be queued behind a waiter, whatever PostgreSQL's queueing policy. This is what breaks the round-5 cycle *scheduler → SO-2 → retirement → scheduler*: SO-2's class-10 request has nothing to queue behind.
3. **A backend `FOR SHARE` hold is uncontested.** By 2, no transaction can ever wait on another *because* the latter holds a backend `FOR SHARE`; the round-4 argument that needed a retirement's waiting `FOR UPDATE` to be harmless is no longer needed.
4. **BL-4** still orders every multi-backend acquisition, and **phase discipline (LG-1)** still places every class-10 acquisition of a work transaction after its explicit class 1–8 locks and before its first write; after 1–3 these are no longer load-bearing for class 10, and they are kept because LG-THEOREM's level table (§16.2.8) is computed over them.

Where contention exists it resolves **against the retirement, immediately** (`M7014`, BL-7), and the retirement is retried under the governed contract of §11.10.8.

#### 11.10.6 Why the predicate is now evaluated on a state nothing can extend

> **BL-THEOREM.** If `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(B)` or `c_retire_storage_profile_v1(P)` commits, BL-SAFE holds for `B`.
>
> *Proof.* The retirement holds `B`'s row `FOR UPDATE` from before the predicate call to commit.
> (a) Any **C**/**M** transaction `T` that holds `FOR SHARE` on `B` makes the retirement's `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` fail with `M7014` before the predicate is evaluated, so nothing is retired; a retirement retried after `T` commits sees `T`'s rows under READ COMMITTED, and the predicate refuses.
> (b) Any **C**/**M** transaction `T'` requesting `FOR SHARE` on `B` after the retirement acquired `FOR UPDATE` waits; if the retirement commits, `T'` re-reads `retiredAt IS NOT NULL` (BL-6) and raises before any write (`M7011`, or `M7013` in the signer).
> (c) By **BL-2** and **T-180**, every **C** and **M** write is performed by a function of §11.10.4 in phase P2 order, so there is no third kind of transaction able to add an obligation or mint authority.
> (d) By **BL-9**, no **U** or **D** write moves a row into a drain class, so a transaction outside §11.10.4 cannot add an obligation either; and by **BL-10** the seven separate snapshots of the predicate cannot miss an obligation that a concurrent commit moved between classes.
> (a)–(d) are exhaustive for (i) and (ii) of BL-SAFE. ∎
>
> **Corollary.** `RC-21` has a real serialization point, and it is two-sided **for exactly the transactions that need it**. The round-2 statement — that the retirement side's `FOR UPDATE` alone serialized issuance and enqueueing — remains withdrawn, and the round-3 statement — that every backend-scoped write takes the lock — is withdrawn too, because it was neither true of the bodies nor required by the property.

#### 11.10.7 Required concurrency tests

Every case below uses **two or more real sessions with explicit statement interleaving** (VC-4), runs in **every** order of its lock-acquisition points, and fails on any `40P01`. Full statements in §25.13 and §25.21.

| Case | Interleaving | Expected |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| the active manifest's backend | `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(active)` on a *drained* active backend | **REFUSED** `55000`, message naming the active manifest; nothing retired (**T-172**) |
| retirement vs SO-2 issuance | T1 locks and drains `A`; T2 runs SO-2 targeting `A` | either T2 holds its `FOR SHARE` first and T1 is refused `M7014` at once (and, retried after T2 commits, `M7009 CLASS_2_OPEN_INTENTS=1`), or T1 holds `FOR UPDATE` first, retires, and T2 gets `M7011`. **Never an `ISSUED` intent on a retired backend, and T1 never waits** (**T-173**) |
| retirement vs generation allocation | T2 runs `w_claim_upload_intent_v1` on an intent of `A` | either the generation commits and the retirement is refused (class 4 or 6), or the retirement commits and the claim gets `M7011` (**T-174**) |
| retirement vs outbox enqueue | T2 runs any WC-5…WC-10 function on `A` | either the effect commits and the retirement is refused `CLASS_3_OPEN_EFFECTS=1`, or the retirement commits and T2 gets `M7011` **at its own P2 call, before its first write** (**T-175**) |
| retirement vs reconciliation classification | T2 runs `w_classify_object_key_v1` on an **unissued** key of `A` | safe serialization in both orders; while T2 holds its `FOR SHARE`, the **retirement** fails `M7014` immediately (**T-176**, BL-7) |
| retirement vs requeue, and multi-backend batches | (a) requeue of a `FAILED_PERMANENT` effect on `A`; (b) two sessions running the five BL-4 batch functions over `A` and `B` in opposite arrival order | (a) the retirement is refused in both orders because the row already blocks class 3, and the requeue takes **no** class-10 lock; (b) no `40P01` across 100 interleavings (**T-179**) |
| **capability mint vs retirement** | T2 runs `x_mint_generation_capability_v1` for a live grant on `A`; T1 runs `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)`, and separately `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` of the generation's executing profile while another live profile remains | backend retirement refused in both orders (`M7014` while T2 holds class 10, class 2/4 afterwards); profile retirement serialized at class 10: if it holds `FOR UPDATE` first and commits, the mint records the **other** live profile (XF-17); if the mint holds class 10 first, the retirement raises `M7014` and, retried after the mint commits, succeeds. No `40P01` (**T-182**) |
| **capability mint vs claim / reclaim / observation / release** | T1 holds the intent in `w_claim_upload_intent_v1`, `w_record_validated_observation_v1` or `w_release_upload_intent_v1`; T2 mints for the current grant | the two serialize on the class-4 intent lock; the mint either precedes the state change or is refused `M7013` after it. No mint row for a non-current epoch; no `40P01` (**T-183**) |
| **classification vs retirement and intent state changes** | (a) T2 classifies the staging key and the accepted key of an intent while T1 runs SO-3, U9 expiry or a claim on it; (b) T1's retirement predicate runs while T2 commits a **D** write between two of its seven statements | (a) an owned key is never enqueued in either order; (b) BL-10: no false `NULL` (**T-184**) |
| **the round-5 three-session schedule** | S1 scheduler on artifact of assignment `X` / backend `A` holding `A` `FOR SHARE`; S2 SO-2 on `X` holding `X` `FOR UPDATE`; S3 `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)`; then S2 requests `A` `FOR SHARE` and S1 inserts its execution | S3 raises `M7014` without ever appearing in `pg_locks` as a waiter; S2's `FOR SHARE` is granted; S1 waits on S2 only and then completes. **No `40P01`** (**T-190**) |
| full backend rotation | rotate `A → B`, drain `A`, retire `A` | **succeeds**; RT-3's order is the only one that reaches it (**T-177**) |
| credential rotation preserved | register `A2` over live `A`, activate it, retire `A1` | **succeeds** without consulting the drain predicate (**T-178**, RT-5) |
| BL-2 exactness | source-level check | the set of functions calling the liveness helpers equals §11.10.4 and `database.backendLivenessFunctions[]` in both directions; every call is in P2; `i_backend_is_drained` has no locking clause; BL-9's transition tables hold (**T-180**) |
| governed retry contract | the rotation pipeline meets `M7014` repeatedly | RR-1…RR-7 hold; the work transactions are unaffected (**T-193**) |

#### 11.10.8 Governed retirement retry and failure contract (`M7014`)

A non-waiting retirement moves a question the database used to answer by waiting — *"is anything using this backend right now?"* — into a governed retry. The contract is normative for the control-plane rotation pipeline (TO-7) and is tested by **T-193**.

| # | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| **RR-1** | `M7014 M7_RETIREMENT_BUSY` is raised by `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` and `c_retire_storage_profile_v1`, and only by them, when a `NOWAIT` lock they request is unavailable (`lock_not_available`). `DETAIL` is `BACKEND_LIVENESS_HELD` (the backend row) or `PROFILE_ROW_HELD` (a profile row). It is raised before the RT-1/RT-2 coherence checks and before the drain predicate, the whole transaction rolls back, and **nothing is retired** |
| **RR-2** | `M7014` is a *transient refusal*, never a verdict about drainage or coherence. The pipeline MUST NOT report it as `M7009`, `M7011` or `55000`, and MUST NOT infer from it that the backend holds bytes |
| **RR-3** | The pipeline retries the **same** call with bounded exponential backoff and jitter (initial ≥ 1 s, cap ≤ 5 min, at most `retirementRetryBudget` attempts, a value of the pipeline's reviewed rotation configuration, default 50). A retry is a fresh transaction; no state carries between attempts |
| **RR-4** | The pipeline MUST NOT make progress at the expense of work: it never cancels, terminates or signals another backend process (`pg_cancel_backend`, `pg_terminate_backend`), never raises its own `lock_timeout` or removes `NOWAIT`, never disables a work path, never revokes a work role's EXECUTE, and never uses an owner-class bypass to retire. The only lever it has is time |
| **RR-5** | On exhausting the budget the pipeline stops and records `RETIREMENT_NOT_ACHIEVED` with the last `DETAIL`; the backend and its profiles remain **live** and fully routable. This is the fail-closed direction: an unretired backend strands nothing, whereas a retirement forced through strands obligations (BL-SAFE) |
| **RR-6** | A retry that reaches the predicate reports its real outcome (`M7009` / `M7011` / `55000` / success) and ends the loop; the pipeline does not retry those |
| **RR-7** | Operators MAY schedule retirement inside a low-traffic window, or retire a backend only after RT-3 has moved all new work away from it (a non-active drained backend has no C/M writers except reconciliation of an unissued key, WC-10). No other mechanism is provided, and none is needed for safety. The bounded-progress limitation is residual **M7-R-16** |

---

## 12. Storage state machines

All four machines are finite, have explicit terminal states, and are enforced in PostgreSQL by `BEFORE UPDATE` guard triggers that reject any transition not in the tables below, plus `AFTER` triggers that append one transition-log row per change (`m7_upload_intent_transition`, `m7_evidence_artifact_transition`, `m7_storage_outbox_transition`). Every guarded update also requires `current_user = 'pagamenos_m7_owner'` and the transaction-local write-path marker of the calling function (§18.5). **No transition is chosen by recency; each is a compare-and-set on `(state, stateVersion)` and, where leased, `leaseEpoch`.**

### 12.1 Upload intent

```text
            SO-2
             │
             ▼
   ┌────── ISSUED ◀──── release (U4) ────┐
   │         │ claim (U2) ─ allocates generation(e)
   │         ▼                           │
   │     PROCESSING ── reclaim (U3) ─────┤ (lease expired; allocates generation(e+1))
   │    │    │     │                     │
   │  U6│  U5│   U7│                     │
   │    ▼    ▼     ▼                     │
   │ REJECTED  VALIDATED   TERMINAL_FAILURE
   │ _CONTENT    │  (acceptedLeaseEpoch fixed)
   │             │ SO-3 (U8)
   │             ▼
   │          CONSUMED
   │
   └── expiry/withdrawal (U9) from ISSUED | PROCESSING(lease expired) | VALIDATED ──▶ EXPIRED
```

| ID | From → To | Trigger (function / role) | DB predicate (evaluated under `FOR UPDATE` on the intent row) | Side effects in the same transaction |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| U1 | ∅ → `ISSUED` | `m7.p_begin_evidence_upload_v1` / participant | session valid; assignment locked & owned; binding exists for intent & assignment; no row for `(decisionBindingId, nonce)`; the **active** manifest's storage profile is live | transition log row; `stagingWriteFenceAt` derived (§11.7.2) |
| U2 | `ISSUED` → `PROCESSING` | `m7.w_claim_upload_intent_v1` / worker | `now < intentDeadlineAt`; assignment has no `WITHDRAWN` consent event; a live profile exists over `intent.backendSha256`; XF-DL-1 holds for the fence about to be issued | `leaseEpoch += 1`; `leaseOwner`; `leaseExpiresAt = now + policy.workerLease`; **insert `m7_canonical_generation(intentId, leaseEpoch)`** with a fresh unique key, the **executing** profile (§11.8) and `grantExpiresAt`/`writeFenceAt`; **insert the single `m7_generation_write_grant` row** — the generation's immutable authorization envelope, addressed by an opaque `generationGrantId` which is what the claim returns (XF-2, XF-9, XF-11). The claim does **not** mint a capability and returns no capability material; that is the sealed signer's job (§11.7.3, §19.11.7) |
| U3 | `PROCESSING` → `PROCESSING` | same | `leaseExpiresAt ≤ now < intentDeadlineAt`; no `WITHDRAWN` event; live profile; **`now ≥ writeFenceAt` of the current generation** (XF-6, else `M7012`) | `leaseEpoch += 1`, new owner/expiry, **new generation row + new grant row** with their own fences |
| U4 | `PROCESSING` → `ISSUED` | `m7.w_release_upload_intent_v1` / worker | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch`; `now < uploadExpiresAt` | lease cleared; the released generation becomes superseded and is swept (GF-7) with `notBefore ≥ its writeFenceAt` (XF-5) |
| U5 | `PROCESSING` → `VALIDATED` | `m7.w_record_validated_observation_v1` / worker | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch`; `now < intentDeadlineAt`; no observation exists; the observation names generation `p_epoch`'s key, its **executing profile** and that profile's `encoderGeneration` (EP-3, EP-4) | insert observation; set `acceptedLeaseEpoch = leaseEpoch`; lease cleared; enqueue `DELETE_OBJECT(STAGING)` with `notBefore = stagingWriteFenceAt`; enqueue deletes for every generation ≠ accepted with `notBefore ≥ each one's writeFenceAt` |
| U6 | `PROCESSING` → `REJECTED_CONTENT` | `m7.w_record_content_rejected_v1` / worker | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch` | lease cleared; enqueue staging delete and a delete for **every** generation, each at or after its own fence |
| U7 | `PROCESSING` → `TERMINAL_FAILURE` | `m7.w_record_terminal_failure_v1` / worker | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch` | as U6 |
| U8 | `VALIDATED` → `CONSUMED` | `m7.p_finalize_evidence_submission_v1` / participant | session valid; assignment locked & owned; `intent.assignmentId` matches; `now < intentDeadlineAt`; observation exists on the accepted generation | insert submission, artifact (`AVAILABLE`, bound to the accepted generation and **its executing profile**, EP-5), receipt; `m7_outcome` created if absent |
| U9 | `ISSUED` \| `VALIDATED` \| `PROCESSING` with `leaseExpiresAt ≤ now` → `EXPIRED` | `m7.w_expire_upload_intents_v1` / worker | `now ≥ intentDeadlineAt` **or** assignment has a `WITHDRAWN` consent event | lease cleared; enqueue staging delete (`notBefore = max(now, stagingWriteFenceAt)`) and deletes for **every** generation (`notBefore = max(now, that generation's writeFenceAt)`) |

Terminal: `CONSUMED`, `REJECTED_CONTENT`, `EXPIRED`, `TERMINAL_FAILURE`. **U8 and U9 have mutually exclusive predicates** (`now < intentDeadlineAt` vs `now ≥ intentDeadlineAt`, or U9's withdrawal branch) and both lock the same row, so they cannot both commit (§16.3).

### 12.2 Raw evidence artifact

| ID | From → To | Trigger / role | Predicate | Side effects |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A1 | ∅ → `AVAILABLE` | SO-3 (U8) / participant | as U8; artifact binds `(uploadIntentId, acceptedLeaseEpoch)`, its key, its `acceptedExecutingProfileId` and `backendSha256`, all FK-bound to the accepted **generation** (EP-5) — never copied from the intent | log row |
| A2 | `AVAILABLE` \| `MISSING` → `DELETION_SCHEDULED` | `m7.w_schedule_withdrawal_deletions_v1`, `m7.w_schedule_retention_deletions_v1`, `m7.w_schedule_authorized_deletion_v1` / worker | a verified deletion basis (§15.3) and no existing `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE` execution for the submission | insert `m7_deletion_execution` (with `hardDueAt`, `deadlinePolicyVersion`, §15.11); enqueue `DELETE_OBJECT(CANONICAL)` on the artifact's **own** backend, linked to the execution, with `boundPolicyVersion = execution.deadlinePolicyVersion` (DL-5) and `notBefore ≥` the accepted generation's `writeFenceAt` (XF-5) |
| A3 | `DELETION_SCHEDULED` → `DELETED` | `m7.w_record_effect_attempt_v1` / worker | the linked outbox row reaches `CONFIRMED` under a matching epoch with result `ABSENT_CONFIRMED`, **recorded by an attempt whose `executingBackendSha256` equals the artifact's** | `deletedConfirmedAt = now`; insert `m7_deletion_execution_completion` |
| A4 | `AVAILABLE` → `MISSING` | `m7.w_record_canonical_missing_v1` / worker | a worker `HEAD` on the artifact's own backend observed absence while no deletion was scheduled | insert `m7_evidence_integrity_finding(CANONICAL_OBJECT_MISSING)` |

Terminal: `DELETED`. `MISSING` is not terminal: a later verified deletion basis still produces a deletion record (A2 → A3 confirms absence **on the bound backend**).

### 12.3 Storage outbox effect

| ID | From → To | Trigger / role | Predicate | Side effects |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| O1 | ∅ → `PENDING` | any enqueueing function (U5–U7, U9, A2, reconciliation, generation sweep) | `UNIQUE(effectKind, backendSha256, objectKey) WHERE state IN ('PENDING','LEASED')` — an existing open effect for that key **on that backend** is reused (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` + re-select); `boundPolicyVersion` derived per family (DL-5); `notBefore` raised to the object's fence (XF-5) | log row |
| O2 | `PENDING` → `LEASED` | `m7.w_lease_outbox_v1` / worker | `nextAttemptAt ≤ now`, `notBefore ≤ now`, **a live profile exists over `backendSha256`**; selected `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` | `leaseEpoch += 1`, owner, `leaseExpiresAt = now + `**`boundPolicy`**`.workerLease` (DL-5) |
| O3 | `LEASED` → `LEASED` | `m7.w_lease_outbox_v1` | `leaseExpiresAt ≤ now`; live profile | `leaseEpoch += 1` (fences the previous holder); expiry from the **bound** policy |
| O4 | `LEASED` → `LEASED` | `m7.w_renew_outbox_lease_v1` | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch`, `leaseExpiresAt > now` | extend `leaseExpiresAt` by the **bound** policy's `workerLease` (heartbeat) |
| O5 | `LEASED` → `PENDING` | `m7.w_record_effect_attempt_v1` | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch`; attempt backend matches; result `PROVIDER_ERROR_RETRYABLE` or `STILL_PRESENT`; `attempts + 1 − attemptBudgetBase < `**`boundPolicy`**`.outboxMaxAttempts` | `attempts += 1`; `nextAttemptAt = now + least(2^(attempts − attemptBudgetBase) s, `**`boundPolicy`**`.outboxBackoffCap)`; attempt row |
| O6 | `LEASED` → `CONFIRMED` | `m7.w_record_effect_attempt_v1` | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch`; result `ABSENT_CONFIRMED`; **the attempt row's `executingBackendSha256` equals the outbox row's `backendSha256`** | attempt row; `confirmedAt`; A3 if linked to an artifact deletion; the completion row records `withinCompletionBudget` / `withinHardDeadline` (DL-7) |
| O7 | `LEASED` → `FAILED_PERMANENT` | `m7.w_record_effect_attempt_v1` | `leaseEpoch = p_epoch`; result `PROVIDER_ERROR_PERMANENT` or the **bound** policy's attempt window exhausted | attempt row; appears in `m7.v_deletion_sla_critical`; a linked deletion execution gets an `m7_deletion_sla_failure` row (DL-8) |
| O8 | `FAILED_PERMANENT` → `PENDING` | `m7.w_requeue_failed_effect_v1` / worker (operator-invoked) | state is `FAILED_PERMANENT`; live profile over the backend | **`attempts` is NOT reset**: it stays the lifetime count and `attemptBudgetBase` is set to it, opening a new, explicitly recorded window. One `m7_outbox_requeue_record` row per requeue records `session_user`, the lifetime attempts, and whether the bound budget and hard deadline were already exceeded; if they were, an `m7_deletion_sla_failure` row is asserted (DL-6) |

Terminal: `CONFIRMED`. **`ABSENT_CONFIRMED` means the worker issued `DELETE` and then observed `HEAD` → not-found for that key, on the backend the row is bound to.** A provider `DELETE` success response alone is not confirmation (§17.2), and absence observed on any other backend is not confirmation at all (SI-3).

### 12.4 Canonical generation

A generation row is **append-only**; it has no mutable state column. Its lifecycle is entirely relational:

| Stage | Condition | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| allocated | inserted by U2/U3 | epoch `e` may write exactly this key, under exactly this **executing** profile, using a capability whose envelope is this generation's own and whose `validUntil` is exactly `grantExpiresAt`. The generation's write grant is allocated in the same transaction (CB-21) and is addressed thereafter only by its opaque `generationGrantId` |
| writable | `now < writeFenceAt` | the only interval in which this key can come into existence (XF-4) |
| fenced | `now ≥ writeFenceAt` | no M7-issued capability can create or re-create this key, ever (XF-THEOREM). Only now may its delete effect execute (XF-5) |
| candidate | `intent.state = 'PROCESSING'` and `e = intent.leaseEpoch` | the current epoch's target; never swept |
| accepted | `e = intent.acceptedLeaseEpoch` | the observation and, after U8, the artifact bind it |
| superseded | `intent.state <> 'PROCESSING'` (or `e <> intent.leaseEpoch` while processing) **and** `e <> intent.acceptedLeaseEpoch` | an orphan; `m7.w_sweep_superseded_generations_v1` enqueues its delete; reconciliation classifies a found object as `SUPERSEDED_GENERATION_OBJECT` |

**No generation is ever re-pointed, re-used, promoted or demoted.** `acceptedLeaseEpoch` is written exactly once (U5) and is immutable (guard). A generation row is deleted only by an authorized `ROW_PURGE`, which removes its write-grant row in the same transaction.

**A generation's fence columns are append-only facts, not schedule hints.** `grantExpiresAt` and `writeFenceAt` are set at allocation, recomputed and verified by `t_generation_coherence`, and immutable thereafter; no function may extend either, because extending a fence would retroactively invalidate every absence proof taken against it.

## 13. Outcome model

### 13.1 Definition

> **`Outcome` is the M7 root attached to exactly one accepted `Decision`** (FINAL §21, §30; RT-09 as disambiguated by JBA §23). It carries no authored content. **Outcome assertions** are immutable participant-authored facts about what followed that `Decision`.

`Outcome` is not a `PurchaseOccasion`, not proof of a purchase, not an A2 artifact, not writable by B, and not a verification (JBA §7.1, §7.7, BI-01, BI-21).

### 13.2 Root creation

`m7_outcome` is created **only** inside `m7.p_record_outcome_assertion_v1` (SO-1) or `m7.p_finalize_evidence_submission_v1` (SO-3), atomically with the first participant fact for that `Decision`, via `INSERT … ON CONFLICT ("decisionBindingId") DO NOTHING` followed by `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. The assignment lock is already held (§16.2), so for one participant the two operations serialize; `UNIQUE(decisionBindingId)` makes the root unique regardless (E-A).

An A2 `PurchaseIntentInvalidation` of the intent does **not** prevent an `Outcome`: the `Decision` exists and remains a real historical artifact (A2 §22.1, §44). M7 records what the participant asserts about it; B/C read the invalidation lineage under their own rules (RAT P-04).

### 13.3 Assertion content

| Column | Values | Rule (DB CHECK unless stated) |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `assertionKind` | `ORIGINAL`, `CORRECTION`, `RETRACTION` | `supersedesAssertionId IS NULL ⇔ ORIGINAL` |
| `statusLabel` | §6.4 | `NOT NULL ⇔ kind ≠ RETRACTION` (unless redacted, §15.4) |
| `occurrenceAssertion` | `NONE`, `ATTEMPTED_PURCHASE`, `REALIZED_PURCHASE` | same nullability as `statusLabel`. **Independent of `statusLabel`**: no CHECK ties a label to an occurrence value, because labels are undefined upstream (JBA §7.3) |
| `merchantAssertionKind` + `merchantVocabularyVersion` + `merchantRef` | §13.4 | kind `NOT_ASSERTED` unless `occurrenceAssertion ≠ NONE`. `merchantVocabularyVersion` is a **CP** fact (§9.5.1): it is resolved at insert, never supplied and never hashed |
| `eventTimeAssertionKind` + `assertedEventAt TIMESTAMPTZ(6)` + `assertedEventLimaDate DATE` | §13.5 | kind `NOT_ASSERTED` unless `occurrenceAssertion ≠ NONE` |
| `capturedAt` | CCA collection instant | within `policy.captureSkewTolerance` (≤ 120 s) of `clock_timestamp()` at insert (function check) |
| `recordedAt` | `clock_timestamp()` | DB knowledge time |

**Not carried**, deliberately: saving amounts, paid amounts, counterfactuals, baseline, verification verdict, free text, any copy of an A2 value (intended merchant, amount, `intendedTransactionAt`), any participant/assignment/intent/decision identifier column. Value fields belong to a future C1S (§22); A2 context is decision input, not a real-world claim (A2 §44; JBA R-B-07).

### 13.4 Merchant assertion without a fixed merchant universe (closes V1 AUD-01)

| Kind | Stored | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `NOT_ASSERTED` | nothing | the participant did not name a merchant |
| `VOCABULARY_MERCHANT` | `(merchantVocabularyVersion, merchantRef)` — composite FK to `m7_merchant_vocabulary_entry` | the participant selected a merchant from the vocabulary in force when they asserted |
| `UNLISTED_MERCHANT` | nothing | the participant asserted a merchant not in the vocabulary; no free text is stored (FINAL §33 minimization) |

The **merchant vocabulary** is versioned control-plane data, not schema:

- a vocabulary version is registered with the control-plane manifest (§23), binds a `corpusId` from the accepted corpus release ledger (A2 §33.10), and lists that release's merchant identifiers;
- `m7.c_register_merchant_vocabulary_v1` recomputes `entriesSha256` **and** the whole-row `vocabularySha256` **in PostgreSQL** over the installed rows and refuses registration on any mismatch, including a reused version whose `corpusId` differs (§23.8, R-B-14 principle);
- the assertion guard requires `merchantVocabularyVersion` = the vocabulary bound to the **active** manifest at insert time (a CP resolution, never caller input);
- a new study merchant set is a **new vocabulary version** under a reviewed manifest rotation; historical assertions keep their version by FK; no `CHECK (… IN (…))` on merchants exists anywhere;
- **RP-5**: a `merchantRef` is a stable corpus identifier and MUST NOT be re-bound to a different merchant in a later vocabulary version. This is what makes the vocabulary-free request hash of §9.5 sound, and it is a rotation obligation (MA-4).

```
FIXED 14-MERCHANT CHECK OR EQUIVALENT PERMANENT DOMAIN RESTRICTION: ABSENT
MERCHANT VOCABULARY VERSION IN THE REQUEST HASH: ABSENT (§9.5 RP-1)
```

### 13.5 Asserted event time

`INSTANT` is passed to PostgreSQL as **text** and parsed there (`::timestamptz`) after a regex requiring an explicit offset and ≤ 6 fractional digits, so no JavaScript `Date` truncation occurs on the write path (RAT P-08; JBA BI-12). Reads that must preserve precision use `to_char(…, 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')` text, never a `Date`. `LIMA_DATE` is a calendar date (FINAL §13 Lima semantics); a coarse assertion is never widened into a fake instant. **No timestamp is identity** (§7.1).

### 13.6 No current status, no latest-wins, no VS level

M7 stores and projects **no** current status, latest assertion, effective assertion, highest VS level, or "is corrected" flag. §14.2 defines the only resolution M7 performs: explicit supersession edges. Nothing is ever selected by `recordedAt`, `capturedAt`, `assertionSeq` magnitude, label rank or ladder position.

### 13.7 Cardinality

| Pair | Cardinality | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `Decision` binding ↔ `m7_outcome` | 1 : 0..1 | `UNIQUE(decisionBindingId)` |
| `m7_outcome` ↔ assertion | 1 : 0..N | FK |
| `m7_outcome` ↔ `m7_evidence_submission` | 1 : 0..N | FK |
| upload intent ↔ canonical generation | 1 : 0..N | PK `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)` |
| upload intent ↔ **accepted** generation | 1 : 0..1 | `acceptedLeaseEpoch` nullable, written once |
| `Outcome` ↔ purchase-shaped assertions / B candidates / occasions | **not fixed by M7** | JBA §7.2, AM-4 |

## 14. Correction and adjudication (append-only)

### 14.1 Principles

| # | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| CR-1 | A historical row is never updated into a new meaning. The only in-place change M7 ever makes to a fact row is authorized **redaction** (§15.4), which removes content and adds none |
| CR-2 | A correction is a new row with its own identity, its own capture time, its own receipt, and an explicit FK to exactly one target |
| CR-3 | Resolution uses explicit edges only. **No latest-wins, first-wins, or highest-wins** (RAT P-14 principle) |
| CR-4 | No maximum correction depth exists; termination follows from strictly decreasing allocation order along edges |

### 14.2 Outcome assertion correction

| Aspect | Specification |
| :-- | :-- |
| original identity | `m7_outcome_assertion.id` of the `ORIGINAL` row |
| correction identity | the new row's `id` (`CORRECTION` or `RETRACTION`) |
| target relation | `supersedesAssertionId`; composite FK `("outcomeId","supersedesAssertionId") → ("outcomeId","id")` ⇒ **same `Outcome`, DB-enforced** |
| reason | the kind: `CORRECTION` replaces content; `RETRACTION` withdraws it. No free-text reason (minimization) |
| actor / authority | the participant, through SO-1 under the Outcome consent policy; `participantSessionId` records the session; `generationPath = 'M7_RECORD_OUTCOME_ASSERTION_V1'` |
| event time | `capturedAt` (CCA instant) and `recordedAt` (DB) |
| ordering | `assertionSeq` allocated under the root lock as `max + 1`; trigger requires `target.assertionSeq < NEW.assertionSeq` |
| competing corrections | `UNIQUE("supersedesAssertionId") WHERE NOT NULL` ⇒ **at most one successor per row**. A second correction of the same target fails (SQLSTATE `23505`, mapped to `M7_CORRECTION_TARGET_ALREADY_SUPERSEDED`); the participant must re-read and target the current unsuperseded member. No conflict is auto-resolved |
| chain / cycle prevention | single successor + strictly increasing seq ⇒ each lineage is a finite simple path; a cycle would require a row to precede itself |
| corrections of corrections | **allowed**: a `CORRECTION` may target a `CORRECTION` |
| corrections of retractions | **refused**: trigger rejects any row targeting a `RETRACTION` (terminal) |
| across a vocabulary rotation | a `CORRECTION` written after rotation carries the **new** vocabulary version; its target keeps the old one. Neither is re-interpreted, and the correction is not a replay (its caller material differs by `clientCaptureKey`) |
| canonical resolution | lineage `L(r)` = the path from an `ORIGINAL` row through successors. Its **resolution** is its unique member with no successor: `ACTIVE_CONTENT` if that member is `ORIGINAL`/`CORRECTION`, `RETRACTED` if it is `RETRACTION`. Different `ORIGINAL` rows are different lineages and are **never** merged or ranked. `m7.v_outcome_assertion_resolution` computes this with a recursive CTE; it is a **reproducible, non-authoritative projection** of the rows (JBA §16.1 principle) |

### 14.3 Evidence correction (participant replacement)

| Aspect | Specification |
| :-- | :-- |
| original identity | `m7_evidence_submission.id` |
| correction identity | a new submission created by SO-3 with `supersedesEvidenceId` |
| target relation | composite FK `("outcomeId","supersedesEvidenceId") → ("outcomeId","id")` (same `Outcome`) |
| ordering | `evidenceSeq` under the root lock; trigger requires `target.evidenceSeq < NEW.evidenceSeq` |
| competing replacements | `UNIQUE("supersedesEvidenceId") WHERE NOT NULL` |
| cycles | impossible (as §14.2) |
| retraction | **no participant evidence-retraction operation exists.** Removal of evidence is a privacy act (§15), never a collection act, so it remains available after withdrawal |
| effect on storage | none. A superseded submission's artifact follows the ordinary retention/withdrawal rules on its **own** backend; replacement is not deletion, and a replacement created after a storage-profile rotation does not move or re-address the replaced artifact |

### 14.4 System integrity adjudication

`m7_evidence_integrity_finding` records a storage-integrity observation about one submission:

| Kind | Meaning | Author |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `CANONICAL_OBJECT_MISSING` | the worker observed `HEAD` → not-found, **on the artifact's bound backend**, for an `AVAILABLE` artifact with no scheduled deletion | `pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt` via `m7.w_record_canonical_missing_v1` |
| `CANONICAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH` | the worker read the canonical object from the bound backend and its SHA-256 differs from the bound observation | via `m7.w_record_canonical_digest_mismatch_v1` |

`UNIQUE(submissionId, findingKind)`; append-only; not itself correctable (it records what was observed at `observedAt`). **A finding is never a verification verdict** and never asserts anything about a purchase. A finding raised while the worker was addressing the wrong backend is impossible: both functions require a routable profile for the artifact's own `backendSha256`.

### 14.5 Evidence standing — independent axes, no precedence

| Axis | Source row(s) | Values |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| participant supersession | existence of a successor submission | superseded / not |
| integrity | set of findings | ∅ / {MISSING} / {MISMATCH} / both |
| raw artifact | `m7_evidence_artifact.state` | `AVAILABLE` / `DELETION_SCHEDULED` / `DELETED` / `MISSING` |
| redaction | `m7_storage_observation.redactedAt` | redacted / not |
| storage reachability | whether a live profile exists over the artifact's `backendSha256` | routable / unroutable (operational, never a domain judgement) |

Consumers read every axis. M7 defines **no** combined "valid evidence" status; any such judgement is verification (C1).

### 14.6 Direct-SQL invariants for correction

These rows restate register entries (§26) in the correction context; **§26 is the canonical register.**

| ID | Invariant | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| M7-I20 | a correction targets a row of the same `Outcome` | composite FK (E-A) |
| M7-I21 | at most one successor per assertion / submission | partial unique index (E-A) |
| M7-I22 | successor has strictly greater seq; target is not a `RETRACTION` | `BEFORE INSERT` trigger (E-A) |
| M7-I23 | no row is updated into new content | `BEFORE UPDATE` guard allowing only the redaction column pattern under the redaction path (E-A) |
| M7-I02 | no correction row can be inserted outside SO-1 / SO-3 | insert guard: `current_user` + path marker; no table privilege to any login role (E-A) |

---

## 15. Withdrawal and deletion

### 15.1 Two different acts

| | **Withdrawal** | **Deletion** |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| what it is | an A1 `StudyConsentEvent(action = WITHDRAWN)` appended by A1 (A1 §8) | a removal of stored content by an authorized mechanism |
| who performs it | the participant through A1 | M7 storage worker, under a verified basis (§15.2) |
| what it changes in M7 | (1) every later SO-1/SO-2/SO-3 is refused by CCA; (2) open upload intents expire (U9); (3) raw evidence deletion is scheduled for every artifact of that assignment (RT-17) | stored bytes (`RAW_OBJECT_DELETE`), row content (`ROW_REDACT`), or rows (`ROW_PURGE`) |
| what it does not change | existing assertions, submissions, observations, receipts, sessions, storage bindings; it mutates no historical fact | consent state; it is never a withdrawal |
| implies the other? | implies **raw-evidence deletion only** (RT-17). It does **not** by itself imply redaction or purge of assertions or submission metadata (AC-03) | **never** implies withdrawal |
| study eligibility | not decided by M7 (C2; Rev2 §6.E sensitivity) | not decided by M7; C2 treats resulting missingness conservatively (JBA §16.6.2) |
| immutable domain facts | preserved as pre-withdrawal facts | changed only as the authorized mechanism requires; P-05 purpose limitation applies (§15.9) |

### 15.2 Deletion bases and their authority sources

| Basis | Authority source (DB row) | Mechanisms permitted | Target | Who schedules |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `CONSENT_WITHDRAWAL` | `public.study_consent_event` row with `action = 'WITHDRAWN'` for the target's assignment (A1 fact; RT-17) | `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE` | one `EVIDENCE_SUBMISSION` | worker, `m7.w_schedule_withdrawal_deletions_v1` |
| `RETENTION_EXPIRY` | the submission's **own** bound `m7_retention_policy` and its stored `rawDeleteScheduleByAt` (§15.11) | `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE` | one `EVIDENCE_SUBMISSION` | worker, `m7.w_schedule_retention_deletions_v1` |
| `LEGAL_PRIVACY_OBLIGATION` | `m7_deletion_authorization` row minted by `pagamenos_m7_deletion_authority_rt` | `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE`, `ROW_REDACT`, `ROW_PURGE` | `EVIDENCE_SUBMISSION` or `ASSIGNMENT_M7_DATA` | worker, `m7.w_schedule_authorized_deletion_v1` |

RT-17's *"≤ 7 days after a verification decision"* has **no basis in V1.1** because no verification decision can exist (C1 unauthorized); every artifact therefore falls under the never-verified window or withdrawal. A future C1S MUST add that basis by instantiating the deadline model of §15.11 — a fourth basis with its own hard deadline, schedule deadline and budget — never by mutating an existing one (C1-OB-5).

**Upload-intent leftovers, superseded generations and orphan objects** are not participant data deletions; they are storage hygiene and are enqueued directly against the intent, the generation or the reconciliation finding (§17.4), never through `m7_deletion_execution`.

### 15.3 Verifiable authorization predicate

`m7.t_deletion_execution_verify` (`BEFORE INSERT` on `m7_deletion_execution`) recomputes the predicate from database facts. **No caller-supplied reference is accepted as proof.**

| Basis | Predicate (all must hold) |
| :-- | :-- |
| `CONSENT_WITHDRAWAL` | `consentEventId` resolves; `action = 'WITHDRAWN'`; `consentEvent.assignmentId = NEW.assignmentId`; `NEW.assignmentId` = derived assignment of `targetSubmissionId`; mechanism `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE`; `authorizationId IS NULL`; `NEW.hardDueAt = consentEvent.recordedAt + policy.rawDeleteHardDeadlineWithdrawal` where `policy` is the **submission's own** bound policy |
| `RETENTION_EXPIRY` | `retentionPolicyVersion = submission.retentionPolicyVersion`; `submission.rawDeleteScheduleByAt <= clock_timestamp()`; assignment coherence as above; mechanism `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE`; `NEW.hardDueAt = submission.rawDeleteHardDueAt` |
| `LEGAL_PRIVACY_OBLIGATION` | `authorizationId` resolves to a row whose `generationPath = 'M7_MINT_DELETION_AUTHORIZATION_V1'`; `authorization.assignmentId = NEW.assignmentId`; mechanism equals the authorization's mechanism, **or** is `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE` scheduled as a prerequisite of the authorization's `ROW_PURGE`/`ROW_REDACT`; if `targetKind = EVIDENCE_SUBMISSION`, the submission's derived assignment equals `NEW.assignmentId` and, when the authorization names a submission, it is that submission; `NEW.hardDueAt = authorization.authorizedAt + policy.authorizedDeletionHardDeadline` |
| all | `current_user = 'pagamenos_m7_owner'`, path `M7_WORKER_DELETION_V1`; `NEW.completionBudgetDueAt = NEW.scheduledAt + policy.effectCompletionBudget`; `NEW.budgetSatisfied = (NEW.completionBudgetDueAt <= NEW.hardDueAt)`; uniqueness indexes of §19.9 (one raw delete per submission ever; one row-mechanism execution per authorization) |

**What makes a `LEGAL_PRIVACY_OBLIGATION` authorization verifiable rather than opaque:** (1) it can only exist if inserted by `m7.a_mint_deletion_authorization_v1`, whose EXECUTE ACL is exactly `pagamenos_m7_deletion_authority_rt` (guard: owner + path, E-A against non-owner actors); (2) its subject (`assignmentId`), optional erasure request (composite FK to the same assignment) and optional submission (trigger-verified to that assignment) are coherence-checked at mint; (3) its mechanism/target pair is CHECK-constrained; (4) execution re-verifies scope at schedule time and again at row execution. `decisionRecordSha256` (digest of the privacy authority's decision document) is **provenance, not proof**; M7 asserts no legal sufficiency (JBA §16.4).

**`budgetSatisfied = false` is never a refusal.** The execution is still created — the obligation to delete does not weaken because the system is late — but the row is flagged and surfaces in `m7.v_deletion_sla_critical` (§15.11). Refusing would trade a *visible* SLA problem for a *silent* retention of data.

### 15.4 Mechanisms

| Mechanism | Effect | Rows touched | Precondition |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `RAW_OBJECT_DELETE` | canonical object deleted **on its own bound backend** and absence confirmed there; artifact `DELETED` | `m7_evidence_artifact` (state), outbox, attempts, completion | basis verified; a live profile exists over the artifact's `backendSha256` |
| `ROW_REDACT` | participant-authored content removed in place: assertion `statusLabel`, `occurrenceAssertion`, merchant and event-time columns set to NULL; observation `byteSize`, `contentSha256`, `mediaType`, `encoderGeneration`, `providerEtag` set to NULL; `redactedAt`, `redactionExecutionId` set once | `m7_outcome_assertion`, `m7_storage_observation` | legal authorization; every artifact in scope `DELETED` (raw bytes first) |
| `ROW_PURGE` | all M7 rows of the assignment deleted in FK-safe order (generations included); sessions of the participant deleted where no longer referenced; if `retainDeletionHistory = false`, deletion executions, completions, outbox and attempt rows for the assignment **and the authorization itself** are deleted last in the same transaction | every participant-scoped M7 table (§20) | legal authorization; every artifact in scope `DELETED`; every intent terminal; every related outbox row `CONFIRMED` |

Redaction is permitted only by the two redaction guards `m7.t_assertion_redaction_guard` and `m7.t_observation_redaction_guard`, only under path `M7_ROW_REDACTION_V1`, only from non-redacted to redacted, only nulling the listed columns. Purge `DELETE` is permitted by `m7.t_forbid_mutation` only under path `M7_ROW_PURGE_V1`. `TRUNCATE` is always refused. **Control-plane tables — backends, profiles, manifests, installations, policies, vocabularies and the catalog expectation set — are never purgeable**, because they are not participant data.

### 15.5 Execution identity and separation

| Capability | Role | Cannot |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| mint legal authorization | `pagamenos_m7_deletion_authority_rt` | schedule, execute, write any M7 fact, call any `m7.w_*`, `m7.p_*` or `m7.c_*` |
| schedule and execute deletion | `pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt` | mint an authorization; write participant facts; register or retire a storage backend/profile |
| request erasure (participant) | `pagamenos_m7_privacy_request_rt` | authorize or execute anything |
| register/retire control-plane identities | owner-class only (`m7.c_*`, no login grantee) | be reached by any login role |

`PR-1…PR-4` (JBA §16.8) are realized by: no login role owns an M7 object; no login role can disable triggers (not owner, not superuser — asserted at install); no login role is a member of another M7 role; the authority role has no EXECUTE on any mutating function. **A deployed role holding both authority and execution capability must not exist** (install assertion `IA-06`, §18.4).

### 15.6 Participant erasure request

`m7.r_record_erasure_request_v1(secret, participantId, assignmentId, clientRequestKey)` records `m7_participant_erasure_request` after session validation and relational re-proof that the participant owns the assignment. It is **not consent-conditioned** (it must work after withdrawal), **not an authorization**, and **executes nothing**. It is an input the privacy authority may reference with basis `GRANTED_PARTICIPANT_ERASURE_REQUEST`. Idempotent on `UNIQUE(assignmentId, clientRequestKey)`.

### 15.7 Asynchronous lifecycle, evidence, retries, partial failure

```text
basis verified ─▶ m7_deletion_execution (immutable; hardDueAt, completionBudgetDueAt, budgetSatisfied)
   ─▶ artifact DELETION_SCHEDULED ─▶ outbox PENDING (bound to the artifact's backendSha256)
   ─▶ LEASED(epoch e, under a live profile over THAT backend)
   ─▶ worker DELETE + HEAD on THAT backend
   ─▶ attempt(e, ABSENT_CONFIRMED, executingBackendSha256 = outbox.backendSha256)
   ─▶ outbox CONFIRMED ─▶ artifact DELETED ─▶ m7_deletion_execution_completion
```

| Question | Answer |
| :-- | :-- |
| evidence that deletion occurred | an attempt row with result `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` **whose executing backend equals the bound backend**, under the lease epoch that confirmed the outbox, plus the completion row. **Scheduling is never evidence; absence on any other backend is never evidence** |
| retries | O5 with capped exponential backoff, bounded by `policy.outboxMaxAttempts` and `policy.outboxBackoffCap` |
| permanent failure | O7 → `FAILED_PERMANENT`; the artifact stays `DELETION_SCHEDULED`; the execution appears in `m7.v_deletion_sla_critical`; operator requeue O8 |
| no routable profile | the outbox row is **not leased** (O2/O3 require a live profile over its backend) and appears in `m7.v_deletion_sla_critical` as `UNROUTABLE_BACKEND`. It never becomes `CONFIRMED` by default |
| partial failure across many artifacts | each artifact has its own execution and outbox row; row mechanisms (`ROW_REDACT`/`ROW_PURGE`) refuse to run until **every** artifact in scope is `DELETED` |
| replay / idempotency | one raw-delete execution per submission ever; one row-mechanism execution per authorization; schedule functions skip already-scheduled targets. **Row mechanisms are replay-safe under the exact contract of §15.7.1**, which is different for redaction, for a purge that keeps deletion history and for a purge that forbids residue; no sentence in this document claims more |
| reconciliation | §17.4 sweeps: `DELETED` artifacts are re-`HEAD`ed on a sample **on their own backends**; a present object re-enqueues a delete and records `CANONICAL_OBJECT_PRESENT_AFTER_DELETION` in `m7_reconciliation_finding` |
| audit record | executions, completions, outbox transitions, attempts; subject to purge when the authority forbids residue (§15.8) |

#### 15.7.1 Row-mechanism replay contract (closes `M7V11R5-AUD-02`)

The round-4 text said *"row mechanisms are idempotent on replay"* and tested only redaction. That sentence was false in three ways: `w_execute_row_purge_v1` had **no** replay check, so a replay with `retainDeletionHistory = true` reached its completion `INSERT` again and failed `23505` on `UNIQUE("executionId")`; redaction's check ran only **before** the assignment lock, so a *concurrent* duplicate passed it, waited, and failed the same way; and a purge with `retainDeletionHistory = false` removes, by design, the very execution identity and count a replay would need. The contract below replaces the sentence.

| # | Rule | Enforcement |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **RM-1** | **Replay check, twice.** Each row mechanism reads its execution and its completion before the class-1 lock, and **re-reads both after it**. Every writer of a completion for an execution of assignment `X` holds `X` `FOR UPDATE` (LO-1, IW-5 guarded by class 1), so after the lock the re-read sees either a committed completion or none, never an uncommitted one | §19.12.5 bodies; **T-61** (c) |
| **RM-2** | **Redaction.** If the completion exists, the function returns its stored `affectedRowCount`, updates nothing and inserts nothing | `w_execute_row_redaction_v1`; **T-61** (a), (c) |
| **RM-3** | **Purge, `retainDeletionHistory = true`.** Identical to RM-2: the stored `affectedRowCount` is returned; no `DELETE`, no second completion, no `23505` | `w_execute_row_purge_v1`; **T-61** (b), (c) |
| **RM-4** | **Purge, `retainDeletionHistory = false`.** A committed purge deletes the authorization, every execution, completion, SLA-failure, outbox, attempt and erasure-request row of the assignment and writes no marker (§15.8, JBA §16.6.1 Case 2). The execution identity therefore **intentionally no longer exists**. A later call naming it — sequential, or concurrent and woken after the first commits — finds no execution (before or after the lock) and raises `M7009 M7_DELETION_PRECONDITION` with `DETAIL = 'EXECUTION_ABSENT'`. It deletes nothing, inserts nothing, returns no count, and recreates no row | `w_execute_row_purge_v1`; **T-61** (d), (e) |
| **RM-5** | **Absence is indistinguishable, deliberately.** `EXECUTION_ABSENT` is also the response for an execution id that never existed. The database MUST NOT distinguish *"purged without residue"* from *"unknown"*, because distinguishing them would itself be residue. No stored count is ever pretended: the count of a residue-prohibited purge exists only in the return value of the call that performed it | §15.8; **T-61** (d) |
| **RM-6** | **Worker handling.** The storage worker treats `EXECUTION_ABSENT` on a `ROW_PURGE` retry as terminal *nothing to do*. It does not record, log or export the execution id, the assignment id or any count for that outcome, and it discards its in-memory retry state for that id (RT-16 allowlist, IMP-12). A lost response of a residue-prohibited purge is therefore unrecoverable *as a count*, and that is the intended consequence of Case 2 (residual **M7-R-17**) | worker module; IMP-12; **T-61** (e) |
| **RM-7** | **Rolled-back runs leave nothing.** A mechanism that raised (`M7009`, `ROW_MECHANISM_TARGET_BUSY`, timeout, crash) committed nothing, so its re-run is a first run under RM-1 | transaction atomicity; CB-24 |

| Mechanism | State at replay | Replay outcome | Rows written by the replay |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `ROW_REDACT` | completion present | stored `affectedRowCount` | none |
| `ROW_REDACT` | concurrent duplicate, first commits while second waits on the assignment | second returns the first's stored count | none |
| `ROW_PURGE`, `retainDeletionHistory = true` | completion present | stored `affectedRowCount` | none |
| `ROW_PURGE`, `retainDeletionHistory = true` | concurrent duplicate | second returns the first's stored count | none |
| `ROW_PURGE`, `retainDeletionHistory = false` | first purge committed | `M7009 EXECUTION_ABSENT` | none; no marker, no count |
| `ROW_PURGE`, `retainDeletionHistory = false` | concurrent duplicate | second, after waking, `M7009 EXECUTION_ABSENT` | none |
| either mechanism | previous run rolled back | executes as a first run | as a first run |

### 15.8 Residue (JBA §16.5–§16.6)

`retainDeletionHistory = true`: executions, completions, outbox and attempt rows survive the purge (Case 1: typed deletion history). `retainDeletionHistory = false`: they are deleted and the authorization row is deleted last, in the same transaction; no marker, count or log row is written (Case 2: ordinary absence). M7 MUST NOT reconstruct purged residue from logs, backups, identifier gaps or joins (JBA BI-31, AT-22a), and a replay of a residue-prohibited purge MUST NOT recreate residue or report a count (RM-4…RM-6). **Backup retention is outside M7's technical guarantee** and is recorded as residual **M7-R-05**.

### 15.9 Purpose limitation

No M7 function selects deletion targets by any scientific attribute (label, occurrence value, merchant, time, evidence standing). Scheduling predicates use only the basis facts of §15.3 and the deadline fields of §15.11. Nor does any function select targets by storage profile or backend: routing is a *consequence* of the target, never a *criterion* for choosing it. This realizes RAT P-05 (purpose, not consequence) and P-05a (retention never overrides a controlling deletion obligation).

### 15.10 RT-17 windows

| Window | Clock start | Hard deadline | Scheduling | Measured completion |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| withdrawal ≤ 24 h | `study_consent_event.recordedAt` of the `WITHDRAWN` event | `+ policy.rawDeleteHardDeadlineWithdrawal` (≤ 24 h) | as soon as the event is visible; worker cadence ≤ `policy.schedulerWorstCaseLag` | `m7_deletion_execution_completion.completedAt` |
| never verified ≤ 30 days | `m7_evidence_submission.recordedAt` | `+ policy.rawDeleteHardDeadlineNeverVerified` (≤ 30 d), stored as `rawDeleteHardDueAt` | at `rawDeleteScheduleByAt` (§15.11) | same |
| legally authorized | `m7_deletion_authorization.authorizedAt` | `+ policy.authorizedDeletionHardDeadline` (≤ 30 d) | immediately on `w_schedule_authorized_deletion_v1` | same |
| after verification decision ≤ 7 days | — | — | **not applicable in V1.1**; C1S instantiates §15.11 | — |

RT-17 states these defaults are to be confirmed at Wave-0 sign-off; a stricter confirmed value is a new policy version (§23), and because every row carries its own bound policy, a later change never applies retroactively.

### 15.11 The deletion deadline model (closes `M7V11-AUD-04`)

#### 15.11.1 The failure this replaces

Treating the RT-17 number as a *scheduling* offset makes the normative SLA unachievable at its own boundary value:

```
policy.rawDeleteAfterNeverVerified = 30 days
selection predicate: recordedAt + 30 days <= now
⇒ the execution is created at T+30d at the earliest
⇒ outbox lease, provider DELETE, HEAD, retries all occur AFTER T+30d
⇒ completion is necessarily later than the RT-17 completion bound
```

A breach detector does not satisfy an SLA; it reports failing it. The repair is to make the decomposition explicit, machine-readable and CHECK-enforced.

#### 15.11.2 The three quantities, and the relation between them

| Symbol | Policy column | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **H** | `rawDeleteHardDeadlineNeverVerified` / `rawDeleteHardDeadlineWithdrawal` / `authorizedDeletionHardDeadline` | the RT-17 **completion** bound measured from the basis clock start |
| **S** | `rawDeleteScheduleAfterNeverVerified` / `rawDeleteScheduleAfterWithdrawal` / `authorizedDeletionScheduleAfter` | the offset from the clock start by which the execution MUST exist |
| **L** | `schedulerWorstCaseLag` | the maximum time a scheduler may take to notice an eligible row (a deployment commitment, IMP-08) |
| **B** | `effectCompletionBudget` | the maximum time from execution creation to confirmed absence, covering lease acquisition, provider call, read-back and **all** retries |

> **DL-1 (CHECK, per policy row, per basis).** `S + L + B ≤ H`.
> **DL-2 (CHECK).** `H ≤` the RT-17 constant for that basis (24 h / 30 d / 30 d).
> **DL-3 (CHECK).** `S > 0` for the retention basis; `S ≥ 0` for withdrawal and authorized deletion.
> **DL-4 (verified at registration).** `B ≥ worstCaseRetrySpan(outboxMaxAttempts, outboxBackoffCap, workerLease)`, where
> `worstCaseRetrySpan = Σ_{n=1..maxAttempts} min(2^n s, backoffCap) + maxAttempts × workerLease`.
> `m7.c_register_retention_policy_v1` recomputes this sum in SQL and raises `55000` if `B` is smaller.
> **All four terms are read from the same policy row** — and §15.11.6 makes the *runtime* read them from that same row for every effect that policy's budget covers. Without §15.11.6 this inequality relates one policy's `B` to another policy's retry schedule, which proves nothing.

DL-4 is what makes the budget honest: the budget must actually dominate the retry schedule the outbox will really execute, not an optimistic guess.

#### 15.11.3 Per-row due dates

| Row | Column | Value | Verified by |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7_evidence_submission` | `rawDeleteScheduleByAt` | `recordedAt + policy.rawDeleteScheduleAfterNeverVerified` | `t_submission_coherence` |
| `m7_evidence_submission` | `rawDeleteHardDueAt` | `recordedAt + policy.rawDeleteHardDeadlineNeverVerified` | `t_submission_coherence` |
| `m7_deletion_execution` | `hardDueAt` | per basis (§15.3) | `t_deletion_execution_verify` |
| `m7_deletion_execution` | `completionBudgetDueAt` | `scheduledAt + policy.effectCompletionBudget` | `t_deletion_execution_verify` |
| `m7_deletion_execution` | `budgetSatisfied` | `completionBudgetDueAt <= hardDueAt` | `t_deletion_execution_verify` |
| `m7_storage_outbox` | `boundPolicyVersion` | resolved from the row's own family (§15.11.6 DL-5) | `t_outbox_coherence` |
| `m7_deletion_execution_completion` | `withinCompletionBudget`, `withinHardDeadline` | `completedAt <= execution.completionBudgetDueAt` / `<= execution.hardDueAt` | `t_completion_coherence` (DL-7) |

The policy used for a submission is the submission's own bound policy; for an authorized deletion it is the policy bound to the target's submission, or — for an assignment-wide authorization — the policy of the active manifest at mint time, recorded on the authorization row as `retentionPolicyVersion`. A rotation therefore never shortens or lengthens an existing row's deadlines.

#### 15.11.4 The three monitoring projections

| View | Reports | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7.v_deletion_schedule_lag` | live artifacts past their `rawDeleteScheduleByAt` (or past a visible withdrawal event) with **no** execution | the scheduler is behind. This is the **early** signal, and it fires well before any SLA is breached |
| `m7.v_deletion_sla_critical` | executions with `budgetSatisfied = false`; executions whose outbox row is `FAILED_PERMANENT`; executions whose outbox row cannot be leased because no live profile exists over its backend; executions past `completionBudgetDueAt` and not complete | the deletion is at risk of missing, or has already missed, the completion budget. **A permanent failure lands here rather than silently reporting compliance** |
| `m7.v_deletion_sla_breach` | executions past `hardDueAt` without a completion row | the RT-17 completion bound has actually been missed |

All three are owner-only views, read by the worker through `m7.w_list_deletion_sla_v1`. None of them changes data: monitoring never deletes and never marks anything complete.

#### 15.11.5 Why this satisfies RT-17 rather than restating it

- The normative obligation is a **completion** bound (`H`), and `H` is a CHECK-bounded column, not a comment.
- The schedule deadline `S` is strictly earlier than `H` by at least `L + B` (DL-1), so a system that meets its own declared cadence and retry budget **completes** inside `H`.
- `B` is not a guess: DL-4 forces it to dominate the real retry schedule.
- Missing `S` is visible (`v_deletion_schedule_lag`) before `H` is at risk.
- Exhausting `B`, or exhausting retries, or losing routability, produces an **SLA-critical** state — never a `DELETED` artifact and never a `CONFIRMED` outbox row.
- Nothing here reduces a constant arbitrarily: the RT-17 constants remain the ceilings on `H`.

#### 15.11.6 Bound-policy resolution for every outbox family (closes `M7V11R2-AUD-03`)

##### The failure this replaces

The deletion **execution** correctly persisted `deadlinePolicyVersion`, so its `hardDueAt` and `completionBudgetDueAt` survived a rotation. But the **runtime** did not:

| Function | Read from | Consequence after a rotation to a materially different policy |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `w_lease_outbox_v1` | active manifest's policy → `workerLease` | leases are shorter or longer than the budget assumed |
| `w_renew_outbox_lease_v1` | same | heartbeat window changes mid-execution |
| `w_record_effect_attempt_v1` | active manifest's policy → `outboxMaxAttempts`, `outboxBackoffCap` | the real retry schedule is the **new** policy's, while `B` was checked against the **old** policy's |

So DL-4 — *"`B` dominates the retry schedule the outbox will really execute"* — became false at the first rotation: it compared P1's budget with P2's schedule. A deletion could exhaust its attempts long before, or long after, the budget it is being judged against.

##### DL-5: every effect resolves exactly one bound policy, deterministically

`m7_storage_outbox` carries `boundPolicyVersion TEXT NOT NULL` (FK to `m7_retention_policy`) and `policyBinding m7."M7OutboxPolicyBinding"`. The derivation is **total** over the three families the `basis_ck` constraint already partitions, and is verified by `t_outbox_coherence` at insert:

| `policyBinding` | Family | `boundPolicyVersion` MUST equal |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `DELETION_EXECUTION` | `deletionExecutionId IS NOT NULL` | `deletionExecution.deadlinePolicyVersion` — i.e. `outbox → deletionExecution → retention policy`, **never** the active manifest |
| `UPLOAD_INTENT` | `uploadIntentId IS NOT NULL` (staging hygiene, generation sweeps) | `uploadIntent.retentionPolicyVersion` — the intent's own bound policy, already immutable |
| `RECONCILIATION_RUN` | `reconciliationFindingId IS NOT NULL` | `reconciliationFinding.boundPolicyVersion`, recorded on the finding from the installation active **at listing time** and immutable afterwards |

> **DL-5 (normative).** For every `m7_storage_outbox` row, *every* timing and retry parameter used by its execution — lease duration, lease renewal, attempt ceiling, retry backoff cap — is read from `m7.i_outbox_bound_policy(row)`, which resolves **only** through `boundPolicyVersion`. No outbox-execution function reads `m7.i_policy(m7.i_manifest(installation))`. Housekeeping families are not exempt: they have their own explicitly named bound policy, chosen for the same reason (an effect must be judged by the budget that was in force when it was created), not silently inherited from the active manifest.

Mechanically: `i_assert_control_plane` is still called by every worker entry point (a drifted deployment still cannot write, §23.6), but its returned installation is no longer the source of any outbox timing value. `w_lease_outbox_v1` resolves the bound policy **per row inside its loop**, so a batch spanning two policies leases each row under its own.

##### DL-6: a manual requeue is recovery, not continued compliance

`w_requeue_failed_effect_v1` previously set `attempts = 0`, which silently restored an exhausted DL-4 budget. V1.1:

| Change | Effect |
| :-- | :-- |
| `attempts` is never reset | it remains the **lifetime** attempt count and stays auditable |
| `attemptBudgetBase INTEGER NOT NULL` added to the outbox | the ceiling test is `attempts − attemptBudgetBase < boundPolicy.outboxMaxAttempts`; a requeue sets `attemptBudgetBase = attempts`, opening a **new, visible** window |
| one `m7_outbox_requeue_record` row per requeue | records `session_user`, `requeueSeq`, `attemptsAtRequeue`, `budgetExhausted`, `pastHardDueAt`, and a `justificationSha256` |
| if the effect is deletion-linked and `budgetExhausted` or `pastHardDueAt` | an `m7_deletion_sla_failure` row is asserted for the execution |

> **DL-6 (normative).** A requeue never restores the original DL-4 guarantee. After a requeue past the bound budget, the execution is represented as **recovery after an SLA failure**: its `m7_deletion_sla_failure` row is permanent and append-only, and its eventual completion row carries `withinCompletionBudget = false`.

##### DL-7 / DL-8: completion tells the truth about lateness

> **DL-7 (normative).** `m7_deletion_execution_completion` carries `withinCompletionBudget` and `withinHardDeadline`, both derived by `t_completion_coherence` from the execution's own `completionBudgetDueAt` / `hardDueAt` against `completedAt`, and CHECK-paired so they cannot be forged. A completion is never *refused* for being late — refusing it would leave the system claiming the object still exists — but it can never be mistaken for a timely one.
>
> **DL-8 (normative).** `m7_deletion_sla_failure` holds one append-only row per execution that (a) had a linked effect reach `FAILED_PERMANENT`, (b) passed `completionBudgetDueAt` with no completion, or (c) was requeued after budget exhaustion. It is asserted by the function that observes the condition, is never deleted except by an authorized `ROW_PURGE` that removes the execution itself, and is what `m7.v_deletion_sla_critical` reports as a **durable** fact rather than a recomputed view predicate.

##### Mandatory test (T-151)

Schedule a deletion under P1; record its `hardDueAt`, `completionBudgetDueAt` and `deadlinePolicyVersion`; rotate to a materially different P2 (different `workerLease`, `outboxMaxAttempts`, `outboxBackoffCap`, `effectCompletionBudget`); then run the full lease / renew / retry / permanent-failure / requeue path and prove by direct SQL that **every** observed lease duration, renewal window, attempt ceiling and backoff interval equals P1's value, and that `hardDueAt` is still P1's. **T-152** does the same for an `UPLOAD_INTENT`-family effect, **T-153** for a `RECONCILIATION_RUN`-family effect, **T-154** covers the requeue honesty rules (no counter reset, a requeue record, an SLA-failure row, `withinCompletionBudget = false` on the eventual completion), and **T-155** asserts that no outbox-execution function's source text references `i_manifest` or `i_policy` — a source-level check over the function digests the catalog verifier already pins. The full family is §25.20.

## 16. Transaction and concurrency model

### 16.1 Isolation and clocks

- Every M7 transaction runs at PostgreSQL **READ COMMITTED** (A2 §4.1, CCA §4). Correctness never relies on SERIALIZABLE; it relies on explicit row locks, unique constraints and compare-and-set predicates evaluated after locking.
- **Control-plane time** (`issuedAt`, `expiresAt`, deadlines, leases, `recordedAt`, `observedAt`, `authorizedAt`, `confirmedAt`, `allocatedAt`) is `pg_catalog.clock_timestamp()` inside the function. **Collection time** (`capturedAt`) is the A1 service-clock sample carried through CCA (millisecond origin, stored exactly). **Participant-asserted event time** is parsed from text in PostgreSQL. **Storage time** reported by the provider is not stored. **Audit time** is the `recordedAt` of log rows. No two are substituted for each other.
- Every M7 function sets `lock_timeout = '5s'` in its `proconfig`, which bounds every lock wait inside the function; a timeout raises and the whole transaction rolls back (CCA §49). `statement_timeout` is **not** placed in `proconfig`, because a function-level setting does not bound the already-running top-level statement; the CCA engine and the worker instead issue `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '30s'` at transaction start (an operational bound, not a security invariant).

### 16.2 Canonical lock order, transaction owners and the lock graph (closes `M7V11-AUD-07`, `M7V11R4-AUD-01`, `M7V11R4-AUD-02`)

#### 16.2.1 The contradictions being repaired

The round-1 candidate asserted both *"Worker functions never lock `experiment_assignment`"* and *"`w_execute_row_purge_v1` and `w_execute_row_redaction_v1` take `experiment_assignment` first"*. CCA §33 class C permits a future accepted authority artifact to add new transaction owners, so the correct repair was **enumeration**, not a blanket prohibition, and that repair is kept.

The round-3 candidate then stated a lock order its own SQL did not follow (`M7V11R4-AUD-02`):

| Function (round 3) | Actual acquisition sequence | Declared rule it broke |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `x_mint_generation_capability_v1` | backend `FOR SHARE` (class 10) → intent `FOR UPDATE` (class 4) | "class 10 last among its locks" |
| `w_classify_object_key_v1` | backend `FOR SHARE` (class 10) → intent `FOR UPDATE` (class 4) | same |
| `c_activate_manifest_v1` | manifest → profile `FOR SHARE` → backend `FOR SHARE` | "class-0 internal order `backend ≺ profile`", which `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` obeyed (backend `FOR UPDATE` → profile `FOR UPDATE`) — an executable profile↔backend inversion between two governed transactions |
| six loop functions | class 10 for row *n* held while locking the class 4/7/8 row of row *n+1* | "no class 1–9 lock while holding class 10 for a different backend" |
| every function inserting a row with a foreign key | implicit `FOR KEY SHARE` on the referenced row, never modelled | "every M7 function acquires locks in ascending class order" |

It also enumerated seven transaction owners and omitted the one it had just created, the capability signer (`M7V11R4-AUD-01`). Both are repaired below **from the SQL outward**: §16.2.5 states the model, §16.2.6 lists what every function body actually does, §16.2.7 lists every implicit wait, and §16.2.8 derives the theorem from those tables rather than from a sentence about them.

The round-4 candidate then derived its theorem from a **false PostgreSQL premise** (`M7V11R5-AUD-01`). Its PG-1 said a `FOR SHARE` or `FOR KEY SHARE` request compatible with the current holders is granted even when a conflicting `FOR UPDATE` is already queued, and its theorem's step 3 used that clause to conclude that a class-10 `FOR SHARE` could wait only on a retirement already *holding* `FOR UPDATE`. PostgreSQL's tuple-lock arbitration does not guarantee that — it exists to stop incoming share lockers starving a waiting exclusive locker — and with a waiting retirement the schedule *scheduler (holds backend `FOR SHARE`, waits on the assignment) → SO-2 (holds the assignment, requests the backend `FOR SHARE` behind the waiting retirement) → retirement (waits on the scheduler's `FOR SHARE`)* is a real cycle. Round 5 therefore (1) replaces PG-1 by a conservative premise under which a compatible request **may** wait behind an incompatible waiter, (2) re-derives every wait under that premise through Lemma Q and the contention table, (3) removes the waiting exclusive requests that made the premise matter — both retirements and the session revocation become non-waiting (LG-10) — and orders the one family of implicit waits whose order was unconstrained (LG-8), and (4) replaces the sink argument by a finite level function (§16.2.8, table LV). Two further cycles of the same kind, not named by the audit, were found by that re-derivation and are closed by (3): the erasure-request / participant-operation / revocation cycle and the two-scheduler cycle (§16.2.8 Corollaries 2 and 3).

#### 16.2.2 Lock classes

```text
class 1  public.experiment_assignment            FOR UPDATE (TO-1 first; TO-5 first); A1 and A2 accepted owners
class 2  m7.m7_participant_session (+revocation)  FOR SHARE (validation) / FOR UPDATE NOWAIT (revocation quiescence probe; TO-5)
class 3  m7.m7_outcome                           root upsert + FOR UPDATE (TO-1); TO-5 NOWAIT
class 4  m7.m7_evidence_upload_intent            FOR UPDATE (TO-1 SO-3, TO-4, TO-8); SKIP LOCKED in batches; TO-5 NOWAIT
class 5  m7.m7_canonical_generation ≺ m7.m7_generation_write_grant
                                                 created by TO-4 (claim); locked only by TO-5 NOWAIT
class 6  m7.m7_outcome_assertion / m7.m7_evidence_submission / m7.m7_storage_observation
                                                 created by TO-1 / TO-4; locked only by TO-5 NOWAIT
class 7  m7.m7_evidence_artifact                 FOR UPDATE (TO-4 scheduling, attempt, integrity); TO-5 NOWAIT
class 8  m7.m7_storage_outbox                    FOR UPDATE / SKIP LOCKED (TO-4); TO-5 NOWAIT
class 9  append-only records: receipts, transitions, attempts, findings, executions, authorizations,
         erasure requests, completions, requeue records, SLA-failure records, capability mints
                                                 created by their writers; locked only by TO-5 NOWAIT
class 10 m7.m7_storage_backend                   BACKEND LIVENESS LOCK
           work transactions (§11.10.4 set) : FOR SHARE, phase P2, ascending "backendSha256" COLLATE "C"
           c_register_* / c_activate        : FOR SHARE, first control-plane lock
           c_retire_*                       : FOR UPDATE NOWAIT, first control-plane lock (M7014 if held; LG-10)
class 0  control-plane identity rows other than the backend, in this internal order:
           m7_storage_profile ≺ m7_retention_policy ≺ m7_merchant_vocabulary ≺ m7_merchant_vocabulary_entry
         ≺ m7_control_plane_manifest ≺ m7_expected_* ≺ m7_control_plane_installation
                                                 explicit locks: c_* only, and only after class 10; retirements lock profiles NOWAIT
```

Round 3 filed `m7_storage_backend` both as the first class-0 element and as class 10. It is now **only** class 10, in every role and every mode; class 0 is the remainder of the control-plane identity. The class numbers are labels. The **acquisition orders** are LG-2 (work transactions) and LG-4 (control-plane transactions), and they are the normative content.

This table is normative, is **complete**, and replaces every universal statement about worker or signer locking. §18.6 is its `DatabaseExecutionContext` view and must list exactly the same eight rows; `database.transactionOwners[]` (MA-17) publishes it; **T-189** checks all three against each other and against the role EXECUTE sets.
