**Why TO-8 is not a sub-case of TO-4.** The signer's separation from the worker is the security property of §11.7: disjoint roles, disjoint EXECUTE sets, disjoint credentials and disjoint processes, so that no single compromised principal can both choose storage work and obtain a write capability. Folding it into the worker's owner row would re-merge in the transaction model what §18.2 and IA-14 separate in the catalog. Its lock profile is also different: it is the only owner that holds a class-4 lock without ever writing the row it locks.

> **LO-1 (normative).** Exactly two M7 functions outside the CCA engine may take an **explicit** lock on `public.experiment_assignment`: `m7.w_execute_row_redaction_v1` and `m7.w_execute_row_purge_v1`. Both take it as their **first** lock. Every other `m7.w_*`, `m7.s_*`, `m7.r_*`, `m7.a_*`, `m7.c_*` and `m7.x_*` function MUST NOT issue `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, `FOR SHARE` or `FOR KEY SHARE` against it.
>
> **LO-2 (normative).** Reading `public.study_consent_event` or `public.experiment_assignment` **without** a locking clause is permitted anywhere. The implicit `FOR KEY SHARE` that PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check takes when an M7 row referencing an assignment is inserted is **not** a direct lock in the sense of CCA §37 or LO-1: it is enumerated as IW-1 (§16.2.7) and is the only form of assignment access TO-3, TO-4's schedulers and TO-6 have. *Round 3's T-107 said no non-listed function "blocks" behind an assignment lock; that was false for exactly these functions, whose foreign-key check waits on a concurrent `FOR UPDATE`. It is corrected, not hidden (T-107, T-107b).*
>
> **LO-3 (verification).** `database.assignmentLockingFunctions[]` equals exactly the LO-1 pair and `database.implicitAssignmentReferenceFunctions[]` equals exactly the IW-1 takers; capability CI (IMP-05) fails on any difference with the migration source, and T-107/T-107b execute both.
>
> **LO-4 (normative, class 10).** Transaction owners TO-1, TO-4 and TO-8 take the backend liveness lock `FOR SHARE`, in phase P2, through `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness` / `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness` and nowhere else, **exactly** in the functions of §11.10.4. TO-7 takes the same row `FOR SHARE` in registration and activation and `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` in `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` / `c_retire_storage_profile_v1`, always as its first lock, so no retirement is ever a waiter on it (LG-10). TO-2, TO-3, TO-5 and TO-6 take it not at all. `database.backendLivenessFunctions[]` publishes the work set (MA-16) and **T-180** checks it both ways.
>
> **LO-5 (normative, all owners).** Every M7 function obeys the phase discipline and orders of §16.2.5, and its lock profile is published as a row of `database.lockProfiles[]` (MA-18). **T-181** checks each function body against its row.

#### 16.2.4 No cycle with A1 or A2

The round-4 argument (*"A1 and A2 transactions can appear in an M7 wait chain only as its last element"*) relied on PG-1's no-queueing clause at the assignment row. It is re-derived here from four implementation facts of the baseline (§1.2 item 12 — verified facts, not design authority), without that clause:

| # | Premise | Verified at the baseline by |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **PA-1** | accepted A1 and A2 code issues explicit row locks only on `public.experiment_assignment` (`FOR UPDATE`, as the first lock of its transaction) and `public.purchase_intent` (`FOR UPDATE`; the A2 Case-C decision freeze takes it **without** the assignment) | full-text search of `src/` for locking clauses |
| **PA-2** | every A1/A2 insert whose foreign key references `experiment_assignment` is performed by a transaction that already holds that assignment `FOR UPDATE` or inserted it; the Case-C freeze inserts no row referencing an assignment | the foreign keys onto `experiment_assignment` in the three accepted migrations and the repositories that write those tables |
| **PA-3** | no accepted path updates or deletes a row of `study_participant`, `study_consent_event` or `purchase_intent_decision_binding` | the A1/A2 immutability triggers; only negative tests attempt it |
| **PA-4** | A1 and A2 neither reference nor lock any `m7` row | schema and source |

Consequences. **(a)** An M7 implicit `FOR KEY SHARE` on `study_participant`, `study_consent_event` or `purchase_intent_decision_binding` (IW-2) has no possible conflicting holder and no possible conflicting waiter (PA-1, PA-3), so it never waits. **(b)** An A1/A2 transaction that holds any lock can wait only on A1/A2 transactions: its explicit waits are on `purchase_intent` (held only by A2) and its implicit waits are on rows it holds, on A2-held `purchase_intent` rows, or on A1/A2 unique keys (PA-1, PA-2, PA-4). **(c)** An M7 transaction can wait on an A1/A2 transaction only through a request on `experiment_assignment` (IW-1, or TO-1's/TO-5's first lock). By (b), no wait path leaves an A1/A2 transaction that holds a lock and reaches an M7 transaction; an A1/A2 transaction that holds no lock (waiting for its first lock) can be waited on by nobody. **Therefore no wait cycle contains both an M7 and an A1/A2 transaction**, under either queueing behaviour of PG-1. Cycles among A1/A2 transactions alone are governed by their accepted disciplines (A1 §8.10, A2 §4); M7 adds no edge between two of them, because such an edge would need an M7 transaction to wait, while holding a lock an A1/A2 transaction wants, on an A1/A2 holder — and the only such lock is an assignment, whose M7 holders never wait on A1/A2 (§16.2.8, table LV).

#### 16.2.5 The lock model: premises and rules

**Premises about PostgreSQL ≥ 15.** Round 4's PG-1 said that a request compatible with every current holder is granted without waiting *even when a conflicting request is already queued*. That is **not** a property this design may rely on (`M7V11R5-AUD-01`): PostgreSQL arbitrates a contended tuple through its heavyweight tuple lock precisely so that a stream of incoming share lockers does not starve an exclusive locker that is already waiting, and a later share locker can therefore wait behind that waiter. The premise is replaced by a **conservative** one that admits both behaviours, and the proof of §16.2.8 is valid under either. Nothing in this document asserts which behaviour a given server exhibits in a given schedule.

| # | Premise | Verified by |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **PG-1** | **Conservative queueing.** A waiting row-lock request of transaction `T` on tuple `t` in mode `m` — explicit, or implicit per PG-2 — may be blocked by **(a)** any other transaction that holds a lock on `t` in a mode conflicting with `m`, **and (b)** any other transaction whose request on `t`, in a mode conflicting with `m`, is already waiting — **even when `m` is compatible with every current holder**. The specification neither assumes that (b) happens nor that it does not. Conflict matrix (PostgreSQL's documented one): `FOR KEY SHARE` conflicts only with `FOR UPDATE`; `FOR SHARE` with `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` and `FOR UPDATE`; `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` with `FOR SHARE`, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` and `FOR UPDATE`; `FOR UPDATE` with all four. A request by a transaction that already holds `t` in an equal or stronger mode is granted without waiting | **T-188** (i), (vi); **T-190**, **T-191**, **T-192** |
| **PG-2** | Implicit locks: an `INSERT` whose foreign key references row *r* takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on *r*; an `UPDATE` that changes no column of a non-partial, non-expression unique index takes `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`; a `DELETE` takes `FOR UPDATE`; an `INSERT` that conflicts on a unique index with an uncommitted insertion waits for that inserting transaction's transaction lock, on which every waiter requests the same shared mode, so such waiters never queue behind one another. A row a transaction inserted is invisible to, and so unlockable by, every other transaction until commit | **T-188** (ii), (iii), (vii) |
| **PG-3** | `SELECT … SKIP LOCKED` and `SELECT … NOWAIT` never wait **and never leave a waiting request behind**: a `NOWAIT` request that cannot be granted raises `55P03` (`lock_not_available`) without joining any queue, so no later request can be blocked by it (PG-1 (b) cannot refer to it). Under READ COMMITTED a locking `SELECT` that waited re-evaluates its `WHERE` on the newest row version and skips a row that no longer qualifies | **T-188** (iv), (v), (vi); T-187 |

Every `retiredAt`/`retiredBy` update in §19 changes no unique-index column, so it takes `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, which does not conflict with `FOR KEY SHARE`; the only unique index involving `retiredAt` (`m7_control_plane_installation_one_active`) is an expression partial index and therefore not a key index (PG-2).

**Lemma Q (queue collapse).** For a relation `R`, let `𝒲(R)` be the set of modes that any M7, A1 or A2 transaction can request **with waiting** on rows of `R` (§16.2.7, table C; `NOWAIT` and `SKIP LOCKED` requests are excluded by PG-3). For a mode `m`, let `C(m)` be the set of modes conflicting with `m`, and let `Reach_R(m)` be the least set satisfying `Reach_R(m) = C(m) ∪ ⋃ { Reach_R(m′) : m′ ∈ 𝒲(R) ∩ C(m) }` — the modes held by a transaction that a request of mode `m` can reach through any chain of waiters on the same tuple. *Claim:* if `T` waits on tuple `t ∈ R` in mode `m`, then every transaction `T` can be blocked by — directly, or through a chain of PG-1 (b) edges — is either a waiter on `t` or a **holder of `t` in a mode of `Reach_R(m)`**. *Proof.* By LG-9 no waiter on `t` holds `t`. A PG-1 (b) edge from a waiter of mode `m₁` goes to a waiter of a mode `m₂ ∈ 𝒲(R)` conflicting with `m₁`, which is itself blocked only by holders conflicting with `m₂` or by waiters conflicting with `m₂`; the chain visits only waiters on `t`, is finite, and each holder it reaches holds a mode in `Reach_R(m)`. ∎ *Consequence:* every cycle of the PG-1 wait graph contains, after deleting the intermediate waiters on each tuple, a cycle of the **holder graph** `H*`, whose edges are `T → H` with `H` holding a lock `T`'s request can reach under `Reach`. LG-THEOREM is proved over `H*`, which over-approximates both PostgreSQL behaviours.

**Rules** (normative for every M7 function; T-181 checks them at source level):

| # | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| **LG-1** | **Three phases.** Every M7 function body is P1 → P2 → P3. **P1**: explicit row locks only (locking `SELECT`s, including `SKIP LOCKED` / `NOWAIT` batches), plus — for TO-1 only — the class-3 root *upsert* (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` immediately followed by `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` of that root), whose insertion wait is guarded by class 1 (IW-5). **P2**: the class-10 liveness call(s), present exactly for the §11.10.4 set. **P3**: writes, and only writes; **no waiting** explicit locking clause appears after the first P3 write. The one locking clause after a P3 write anywhere in §19 is the revocation's quiescence probe `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` (§8.2 RV-3), which by PG-3 is not a wait. The root upsert is a P1 acquisition, not a P3 write. Plain reads may appear in any phase |
| **LG-2** | **Work order.** P1 acquisitions ascend in class `1 ≺ 2 ≺ 3 ≺ 4 ≺ 5 ≺ 6 ≺ 7 ≺ 8 ≺ 9`. Within one class, a function that *waits* for more than one row locks them in one declared key order. Exactly one function takes multiple waiting locks within a class: `w_schedule_authorized_deletion_v1` (artifacts by `backendSha256 COLLATE "C"`, `submissionId`); every other multi-row P1 acquisition is `SKIP LOCKED` (TO-4 batches) or `NOWAIT` (TO-5) |
| **LG-3** | **Liveness order.** P2 takes class 10 `FOR SHARE` for the transaction's backends in ascending `backendSha256 COLLATE "C"` order, via `i_hold_backends_liveness` whenever there can be more than one (BL-4) |
| **LG-4** | **Control-plane order.** A `c_*` function acquires `class 10 ≺ m7_storage_profile ≺ m7_retention_policy ≺ m7_merchant_vocabulary ≺ m7_merchant_vocabulary_entry ≺ m7_control_plane_manifest ≺ m7_expected_* ≺ m7_control_plane_installation`, locks several profile rows only `ORDER BY "id"`, resolves any row it must reach through a later element **without a lock first** and then locks in this order, and takes no class 1–9 lock, explicit or implicit. Registration probes use `FOR SHARE`; activation's installation lock is `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`; only retirements use `FOR UPDATE`, and **only `NOWAIT`** (LG-10) |
| **LG-5** | **Row mechanisms do not wait after the assignment.** After its class-1 `FOR UPDATE`, TO-5 locks every row it will update or delete with `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`, in class order 2 → 9, and then writes only rows it holds. A `55P03` is re-raised as `M7009 M7_DELETION_PRECONDITION` with `DETAIL = 'ROW_MECHANISM_TARGET_BUSY'`; the mechanism is retried later. TO-5 takes no class-10 lock |
| **LG-6** | **Never-waiting states.** A transaction in one of the following states performs no further waiting request, so it has no outgoing edge and lies on no cycle: **N1** `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` and `c_retire_storage_profile_v1`, at every point (every lock `NOWAIT`, no insert, updates only of held rows, a lock-free predicate); **N2** TO-5 after its class-1 lock (LG-5; its completion insert is guarded by class 1, its foreign-key checks name rows only TO-5 of the same assignment could hold in `FOR UPDATE`); **N3** `s_revoke_participant_session_v1` after its revocation insert (only the `NOWAIT` probe follows); **N4** `c_load_catalog_expectations_v1` after its manifest lock (inserts guarded by it); **N5** `w_lease_outbox_v1` after its `SKIP LOCKED` batch and `w_renew_outbox_lease_v1` after its outbox lock (only IW-4 follows); **N6** every function after its last possible wait. *Round 4's LG-6 called transactions "sinks" if they waited only on sinks and placed a retirement holding `FOR UPDATE` among them; under PG-1 a retirement that is **waiting** for `FOR UPDATE` is not a sink but a queue head, which is the defect `M7V11R5-AUD-01` exhibits. The level table of §16.2.8 replaces the sink argument* |
| **LG-7** | **Publication.** Each function's P1 sequence, P2 kind, P3 implicit-wait identifiers and `NOWAIT` requests are published in `database.lockProfiles[]` (MA-18) exactly as §16.2.6 lists them |
| **LG-8** | **Ascending assignment references.** A transaction whose P3 can insert rows referencing **more than one** assignment inserts them in ascending `"assignmentId"` order, so its implicit assignment `FOR KEY SHARE` locks (IW-1) ascend. Exactly two functions can: `w_schedule_withdrawal_deletions_v1` and `w_schedule_retention_deletions_v1`, whose P3 loops are ordered `"assignmentId", "submissionId"`. Every other IW-1 taker references exactly one assignment per transaction (`r_record_erasure_request_v1`, `a_mint_deletion_authorization_v1`, `w_schedule_authorized_deletion_v1`) |
| **LG-9** | **No waiting upgrade.** No function issues a *waiting* request — explicit or implicit — on a tuple it already holds in a strictly weaker mode. (The one upgrade in §19 is the revocation's `NOWAIT` probe over the `FOR KEY SHARE` its own insert took, which is not a wait.) This keeps PostgreSQL's lock-queue re-ordering for requesters that already hold a conflicting lock out of every schedule the proof considers |
| **LG-10** | **No exclusive waiter on a shared-held control or session row.** Every request for `FOR UPDATE` or `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on `m7_storage_backend`, `m7_storage_profile` or `m7_participant_session` is `NOWAIT`: both retirements (backend, then profiles), the revocation's quiescence probe (session), and TO-5 (session). Therefore `𝒲` of these three relations contains only `FOR SHARE` and `FOR KEY SHARE`, which are mutually compatible, and **no request on them can ever be queued behind a waiter** (PG-3). This is the architectural repair of `M7V11R5-AUD-01` |

#### 16.2.8 LG-THEOREM — no deadlock cycle exists among M7, A1 and A2 transactions

> **LG-THEOREM.** Under PG-1…PG-3 — in particular whether or not PostgreSQL queues a compatible row-lock request behind an incompatible waiter — and for function bodies satisfying LG-1…LG-10, the tables of §16.2.6–§16.2.7 and the premises PA-1…PA-4, the wait graph of any set of concurrent M7, A1 and A2 transactions is acyclic.

**Table LV — wait levels.** For a waiting request `q` of transaction `T`, `λ(q) = 0` if `q` has no possible target (it never waits); otherwise `λ(q) = 1 + max μ(H)` over the holders `H` it can reach (tables IW and C), where `μ(H)` is the largest `λ` among the waiting requests `H` can still issue **while holding** the lock through which `T` reaches it (`μ = 0` for the never-waiting states N1…N6 of LG-6). Every wait in the §16.2.6 matrix is an instance of exactly one row; T-181 checks the mapping.

| # | Waiting request | Holders it can reach, and what each can still wait on while holding | `μ` of targets | `λ` |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | --: | --: |
| **LV-1** | backend `FOR SHARE` (P2 of WC-1…WC-10; `c_register_*`; activation); profile `FOR SHARE` (activation; profile registration); IW-0 on a backend or profile | the retirements (N1) | 0 | **1** |

| **LV-3** | IW-0 on a policy, vocabulary, manifest or installation; policy and vocabulary `FOR SHARE`; IW-2; IW-4; guarded IW-5 | none | — | **0** |
| **LV-4** | IW-5 single: registration keys, session handle, revocation key, digest-mismatch finding, first activation's installation keys | the competing inserter after its insert: a registration (IW-0, LV-1/LV-3), `s_issue` (IW-2, IW-0: LV-3), a revocation (N3), the digest-mismatch job (nothing), an activation (nothing) | ≤ 1 | **2** |
| **LV-5** | IW-5 single: classification's `(finding, outbox)` pair | the competing classification after its finding insert: its outbox insert (cannot wait on a third classification, which would have inserted the finding first), IW-0 (LV-1) | 1 | **2** |

| **LV-7** | intent `FOR UPDATE` (SO-3 holding classes 1–3; TO-4 single-intent functions; TO-8) | TO-4 single-intent functions and TO-8 holding the intent (P2 LV-1; IW-0 LV-1; IW-3 LV-2; guarded IW-5; classification LV-5); SO-3 holding it (P2 LV-1; IW-0/2/3 ≤ 1); expiry and sweep holding it (P2 LV-1; IW-3 LV-2); TO-5 (N2) | 2 | **3** |
| **LV-8** | installation `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (activation) | activation after its installation lock (first-activation IW-5, LV-4) | 2 | **3** |
| **LV-9** | manifest `FOR SHARE` (activation; manifest registration); manifest `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (catalog load) | load after its lock (N4); activation holding the manifest (installation, LV-8); registration holding its probe (IW-0 LV-1/LV-3; IW-5 LV-4) | 3 | **4** |

| **LV-11** | IW-1 on assignment `X`; the first-lock `FOR UPDATE` on `X` by TO-1 or TO-5 | TO-1 holding `X` (LV-10); TO-5 (N2); TO-3 after its insert (IW-4 only: N6); TO-6 after its insert (IW-3 LV-2; IW-0 LV-1/LV-3); a scheduler holding `X` `FOR KEY SHARE`, which can still wait only on IW-1 for an assignment **strictly greater than `X`** (LG-8), on IW-0/2/3 (≤ 1), and on IW-5 keys that cannot conflict while it holds `X` (raw-delete keys are guarded by class 7; the authorized scheduler holds `X` before its row-mechanism insert only if it inserted raw-delete executions, and then every competitor for the same authorization is still waiting in P1 on the in-scope artifacts it holds, so no competing row-mechanism insertion exists); A1/A2 holding `X` (never lead back to M7, §16.2.4) | ≤ max(3, `λ` of IW-1 on the next greater referenced assignment) | **finite**, by induction on `assignmentId` from the greatest: `λ(X) = 1 + max(3, max{λ(Y) : Y > X})` |
| **LV-12** | IW-5 single: erasure-request key; authorized row-mechanism execution key | a competing TO-3 after its insert (IW-1, LV-11); a competing authorized scheduler after its insert (IW-1 on its one assignment, LV-11; IW-3 LV-2). The waiter itself holds no lock anyone can reach: a TO-3 holds only its session `FOR SHARE` (unreachable, table C), and an authorized scheduler that reaches this wait holds no assignment lock (see LV-11) | finite (LV-11) | **finite** |
| **LV-13** | artifact `FOR UPDATE` (authorized scheduler holding lower-keyed artifacts; attempt; canonical-missing) | an attempt holding the artifact (outbox LV-6); canonical-missing (IW-3 LV-2); a scheduler holding it (artifact `FOR UPDATE` on a **strictly greater** `(backendSha256, submissionId)` key — authorized scheduler only, LG-2 —, P2 LV-1, IW-1 LV-11, IW-0/2/3 ≤ 1); TO-5 (N2) | finite | **finite**, by induction on the artifact key from the greatest |
| **LV-14** | IW-5 ordered (SLA-failure assertion) | a competing assertion job holding a strictly smaller key (further IW-5 on greater keys; IW-3 LV-2) | finite | **finite**, by induction on `(completionBudgetDueAt, id)` from the greatest |

> *Proof of LG-THEOREM.*
>
> (1) **Reduction.** By Lemma Q (§16.2.5), every cycle of the PG-1 wait graph — including cycles that exist only because a compatible request queued behind an incompatible waiter — induces a cycle of the holder graph `H*`. It suffices to show `H*` acyclic.
>
> (2) **A1/A2.** By §16.2.4, no cycle contains both an M7 and an A1/A2 transaction, and M7 adds no edge between A1/A2 transactions. It remains to exclude cycles of M7 transactions.
>
> (3) **Targets.** For every waiting request of every M7 function, table C and Lemma Q give the complete set of reachable holders, and table IW and the rows of table LV enumerate them. The decisive entries are the three LG-10 relations: on `m7_storage_backend`, `m7_storage_profile` and `m7_participant_session` no exclusive request ever waits, so a `FOR SHARE` or `FOR KEY SHARE` holder of those rows is **never** a target, and their exclusive holders (N1, N2, N3) never wait.
>
> (4) **Levels.** Let `T → H` be an edge of `H*`, with `T` blocked on request `q` and `H` blocked on request `q_H` while holding the lock `q` reaches. By construction `λ(q_H) ≤ μ(H) < λ(q)`. Every `λ` in table LV is finite: the non-inductive rows directly, and LV-11, LV-13 and LV-14 by well-founded induction on a total order that the only self-referential step strictly increases (LG-8, LG-2, IW-5 ordered). So `λ` strictly decreases along every edge of `H*` and takes values in the natural numbers; no cycle exists. ∎
>
> **Corollary 1 (the round-5 audit schedule is unrepresentable).** Let `T_sched` be a deletion scheduler for assignment `X` on backend `A`, `T_SO2` an SO-2 on `X` / `A`, and `T_retire` = `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)`.
>
> ```text
> ROUND 4 (waiting retirement), under PG-1 (b):
>   T_sched  holds A FOR SHARE (P2);  waits FOR KEY SHARE on X (P3 execution INSERT)   → T_SO2   (holds X FOR UPDATE)
>   T_SO2    holds X FOR UPDATE;       waits FOR SHARE on A (P2), queued behind         → T_retire (waiting FOR UPDATE on A)
>   T_retire holds nothing on A;       waits FOR UPDATE on A                            → T_sched (holds A FOR SHARE)
>   CYCLE: T_sched → T_SO2 → T_retire → T_sched
>
> ROUND 5, same interleaving:
>   T_retire requests A FOR UPDATE NOWAIT → 55P03 → M7014 M7_RETIREMENT_BUSY; no waiter is left behind (PG-3)
>   T_SO2    requests A FOR SHARE: no holder in {NO KEY UPDATE, UPDATE}, no waiter in 𝒲 ∩ C(SHARE) = ∅ → granted
>   T_sched  waits FOR KEY SHARE on X → T_SO2 (LV-11); T_SO2 has no outgoing edge; T_SO2 commits; T_sched proceeds
>   GRAPH: T_sched → T_SO2.   ACYCLIC.   T_retire, retried under RR-3, then reports its real outcome.
> ```
>
> **Corollary 2 (the revocation schedule is unrepresentable).** Let `T_priv` be `r_record_erasure_request_v1` for participant `P`'s assignment `X` using session `s`, `T_SO` an SO-1/2/3 on `X` using session `s`, and `T_rev` a revocation of `s`.
>
> ```text
> ROUND 4 (waiting revocation), under PG-1 (b):
>   T_priv holds s FOR SHARE;   waits FOR KEY SHARE on X (erasure-request INSERT)   → T_SO   (holds X FOR UPDATE)
>   T_SO   holds X FOR UPDATE;  waits FOR SHARE on s, queued behind                 → T_rev  (waiting FOR UPDATE on s)
>   T_rev  holds nothing;       waits FOR UPDATE on s                               → T_priv (holds s FOR SHARE)
>   CYCLE: T_priv → T_SO → T_rev → T_priv
>
> ROUND 5, same interleaving:
>   T_rev  INSERTs the revocation (FOR KEY SHARE on s: no FOR UPDATE holder) → probe FOR UPDATE NOWAIT fails → DRAINING; commits
>   T_SO   requests s FOR SHARE → granted (LG-10); its revocation check sees the committed row → 28000; rolls back, releasing X
>   T_priv waits on X only while T_SO holds it; then commits (RV-2: it validated before the revocation committed)
>   GRAPH: T_priv → T_SO.   ACYCLIC.   A later probe by the session module returns QUIESCENT (RV-3, RV-4).
> ```
>
> **Corollary 3 (the two-scheduler schedule is unrepresentable).** Round 4 ordered a batch scheduler's P3 loop by `(backendSha256, …)`, so scheduler `S_a` could reference `X` then `Y` while `S_b` referenced `Y` then `X`. With A1 withdrawals `W_X`, `W_Y` waiting on `X` and `Y`: `S_a (holds X KS) → W_Y → S_b (holds Y KS) → W_X → S_a`. Under LG-8 both reference the smaller of `X`, `Y` first, so no scheduler holds the greater while waiting on the smaller, and LV-11's induction applies.
>
> **Corollary 4 (round 4's three inversions stay unrepresentable).** The signer and classification take class 4 in P1 and class 10 in P2; activation takes backend before profile, like both retirements; loop functions finish their P1 batch before P2. Each is a row of §16.2.6, and T-181 rejects a body that contradicts its row.
>
> **What the theorem does not claim.** It does not claim freedom from *waiting*: work transactions still wait, bounded by `lock_timeout = '5s'`; retirements (`M7014`), revocation probes (`DRAINING`) and row mechanisms (`ROW_MECHANISM_TARGET_BUSY`) refuse instead of waiting and are retried. It does not depend on PostgreSQL's queueing policy for compatible requests — that is exactly what PG-1 no longer fixes. It does depend on the conflict matrix, the implicit lock modes of PG-2 and the no-residue property of `NOWAIT` in PG-3, which T-188 checks on the deployed major version (residual **M7-R-14**). PostgreSQL's deadlock detector remains a backstop, and the suite treats any `40P01` as a failure, never as recovery.

| manifest activation vs backend retirement | **T-186** |

| multi-backend batch functions, all five, in opposite arrival orders | **T-179** (b) |

| the PostgreSQL premises the theorem rests on — recorded, not demanded, for PG-1 (b) | **T-188** |

### 16.3 Race matrix

**Twenty-nine distinct normative races, `RC-01` … `RC-29`, listed in ascending order, one meaning per identifier.** The round-2 candidate carried two different `RC-17` rows and two different `RC-18` rows, so three of its references were ambiguous; §16.3.1 reconciles the identifiers and records exactly what moved (`M7V11R3-AUD-03`). Round 4 **appends** `RC-22` … `RC-25` for the races `M7V11R4-AUD-01`, `-02` and `-04` exposed, and **rewrites** `RC-16` and `RC-21` onto the exact liveness set of §11.10.4. Round 5 **appends** `RC-26` … `RC-29` for the three conservative-queueing schedules of §16.2.8 and the concurrent row-mechanism duplicate of §15.7.1, and **amends** `RC-10`, `RC-21`, `RC-22` and `RC-25` onto the non-waiting retirement and revocation protocol (their meanings are unchanged).

| # | Race | Serialization point | Outcome |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| RC-01 | SO-1 vs A1 withdrawal | `experiment_assignment FOR UPDATE` | either the assertion commits before withdrawal, or CCA reads the withdrawal and refuses (A2 §4.3 two-serialization proof, unchanged) |
| RC-02 | SO-3 vs A1 withdrawal | same | same; a refused SO-3 leaves the intent `VALIDATED`; U9 later expires it and deletes its staging object and **every** generation |
| RC-03 | two SO-1 corrections of one target | root lock, then `UNIQUE(supersedesAssertionId)` | one commits; the other gets `M7_CORRECTION_TARGET_ALREADY_SUPERSEDED` |

| **RC-06** | **stale worker (epoch `e`) completes externally and/or in the DB after reclaim (epoch `e+1`)** | per-generation canonical keys (GF-1…GF-6) + `leaseEpoch = p_epoch` on U5–U7 + the write fence (XF-4, XF-6) | epoch `e` can write **only** its own key `K_e`, and only while `now < writeFenceAt(e)`; the reclaim itself cannot occur before that instant (XF-DL-1, XF-6), so by the time `e+1` exists no envelope M7 can mint authorizes `K_e` at all. `e`'s DB completion is rejected `M7_STALE_LEASE`. `e+1` **cannot** observe, adopt or read `K_e`: it is told only `K_{e+1}`, and `m7.w_record_validated_observation_v1` refuses any object key other than generation `p_epoch`'s. `K_e`, if it exists, is a superseded generation and is swept at or after its fence (GF-7, XF-5). **Neither adoption nor late creation is representable** |
| RC-07 | U8 finalize vs U9 expiry | intent `FOR UPDATE`; `now < deadline` vs `now ≥ deadline` | exactly one; a late SO-3 gets `M7_UPLOAD_INTENT_NOT_CONSUMABLE` |

| RC-09 | duplicate SO-3 with **different** transport key, same intent | `UNIQUE(uploadIntentId)` + reload-and-prove in function | alias receipt `SUBMISSION_ALIAS` if RQ equal, else `M7_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`/`M7_DOMAIN_CONFLICT` |

The session module reports completion only after `QUIESCENT` (RV-4) |
| RC-11 | two workers lease one outbox row | `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; epoch | one lease; stale attempt rejected `M7_STALE_LEASE` |

| **RC-21** | **backend or last-profile retirement races a transaction that creates a drain obligation or mints external write authority** — issuance (WC-1), generation allocation (WC-2), capability minting (WC-3), artifact creation (WC-4), outbox enqueue (WC-5…WC-9), reconciliation classification (WC-10) *(round-2 `RC-19`, whose serialization proof did not follow and is withdrawn; round-3 text, which named requeue, lease, renewal and attempt writes that need no lock, is withdrawn too)* | the **two-sided backend liveness lock** for exactly the set of §11.10.4: those functions take the `m7_storage_backend` row `FOR SHARE` in phase P2 and re-read `retiredAt` before their first write (BL-2, BL-6); both retirement functions acquire it `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` — never waiting, `M7014` when held — and hold it across the RT-2 coherence check, the drain predicate and the update (BL-3, LG-10); multi-backend transactions acquire through `i_hold_backends_liveness` in ascending order (BL-4); `m7.i_backend_is_drained` takes no lock (BL-5); every other backend-scoped write is a **U** or **D** write that cannot move a row into a drain class (BL-9, BL-10) | exactly one safe ordering in every interleaving, proved by the **BL-THEOREM** (§11.10.6): either the work holds class 10 first and the retirement raises `M7014` at once (and, retried after the work commits, is refused with its blocking class), or the retirement holds class 10 first, commits, and the work raises (`M7011`, or `M7013` in the signer) before any write. #### 16.3.1 Race-identifier reconciliation (`M7V11R3-AUD-03`)

The round-2 candidate assigned three identifiers twice. Round-1 identities are preserved where the audit required; the round-2 races were re-identified into fresh, contiguous slots.

| Round-2 identifier | Round-2 meaning | Round-3 identifier | Why |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `RC-17` (first occurrence, §16.3) | stale epoch's external `PUT` versus delete-and-confirm of its own key | **`RC-19`** | round-2 race; yields the identifier to the pre-existing round-1 meaning |
| `RC-17` (second occurrence, §16.3) | two claims racing to allocate a generation | **`RC-17`** (unchanged) | round-1 identity, preserved as the brief requires |
| `RC-18` (first occurrence, §16.3) | policy rotation versus an in-flight outbox effect | **`RC-20`** | round-2 race; yields the identifier |
| `RC-18` (second occurrence, §16.3) | observation recorded while a new epoch is claiming | **`RC-18`** (unchanged) | round-1 identity, preserved as the brief requires |
| `RC-19` | last-profile retirement versus issuance or enqueue | **`RC-21`**, **restated** | round-2 race; and its serialization claim was unsupported, so the row is rewritten onto the mechanism actually specified (§11.10.3), not merely renumbered |
| — | — | `RC-16` **amended** | its serialization point named only the retirement side; it now names the two-sided lock |

```
DISTINCT NORMATIVE RACES                 : 29
IDENTIFIERS IN USE                       : RC-01 .. RC-29
DUPLICATE IDENTIFIERS                    : 0
GAPS                                     : 0
IDENTIFIERS WITH MORE THAN ONE MEANING   : 0
ROUND-1 IDENTITIES CHANGED               : 0
ROUND-2 IDENTIFIERS REASSIGNED           : 3 (RC-17 -> RC-19, RC-18 -> RC-20, RC-19 -> RC-21)
ROWS REWRITTEN RATHER THAN RENUMBERED    : 2 (RC-21, RC-16) in round 3; the same 2 again in round 4
ROUND-4 IDENTIFIERS APPENDED             : 4 (RC-22, RC-23, RC-24, RC-25)
ROUND-3 IDENTIFIERS REASSIGNED IN ROUND 4: 0
ROUND-5 IDENTIFIERS APPENDED             : 4 (RC-26, RC-27, RC-28, RC-29)
ROUND-5 ROWS AMENDED, MEANING UNCHANGED   : 5 (RC-10, RC-16, RC-21, RC-22, RC-25)
IDENTIFIERS REASSIGNED IN ROUND 5        : 0
```

**Every transitive reference is updated**, not only §16.3: the closure matrices of §27.2 and §27.4, the invariant register §26, the verification families §25.18, §25.20 and §25.21, the coverage map §25.22, the crash-boundary matrix §17.3, the deadline model §15.11.6, §11.7, §11.10, Appendix A.0, A.1, A.2 and A.3 check 12, and every prose count of the number of races. A reference to a round-2 identifier survives nowhere in this candidate.

### 16.4 Idempotency domains

| Domain | Key | Replay | Different key, same domain identity | Same key, different material |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| SO-1 transport | `(M7_OUTCOME_ASSERTION_RECORD_V1, assignmentId, idempotencyKey)` | return receipt | — | `M7_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` |
| SO-1 domain | `(outcomeId, clientCaptureKey)` | — | new receipt `CAPTURE_ALIAS` if RQ equal, else `M7_DOMAIN_CONFLICT` | — |
| SO-2 | `(decisionBindingId, clientCorrelationNonce)` | return existing intent (any state), with **its own** profile and transport | — | — (issuance carries no other RQ material; A2 §14.1) |
| SO-3 transport | `(M7_EVIDENCE_SUBMISSION_V1, assignmentId, idempotencyKey)` | return receipt | — | `M7_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` |
| SO-3 domain | `uploadIntentId` (and `(outcomeId, clientCaptureKey)`) | — | `SUBMISSION_ALIAS` if RQ equal, else `M7_DOMAIN_CONFLICT` | — |
| worker claim | `(uploadIntentId, leaseEpoch)` — also the generation identity | — | — | — |
| outbox | `(effectKind, backendSha256, objectKey)` while open | reuse open row | — | — |
| deletion | one raw delete per submission; one row mechanism per authorization | skip | — | — |
| row-mechanism run | `executionId` | redaction and purge with `retainDeletionHistory = true`: stored `affectedRowCount`; purge with `retainDeletionHistory = false`: `M7009 EXECUTION_ABSENT`, no count (§15.7.1) | — | — |
| erasure request | `(assignmentId, clientRequestKey)` | return row | — | — |
| control-plane identity | `policyVersion`, `vocabularyVersion`, `storageProfileVersion`, `backendSha256`, `manifestVersion` | re-register with **identical** content succeeds and is a no-op | — | `55000` (§23.8) |

**Request hashes are computed inside PostgreSQL** by `m7.i_request_hash(jsonb)` = `'sha256:' ‖ hex(sha256(convert_to(p::text,'UTF8')))` over a `jsonb_build_array` of the function's own typed **RQ** material only (§9.5 RP-1), with timestamps rendered by `to_char(… AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')`. The hash is an internal comparator, not a cross-system identity. A runtime-role actor cannot store a hash that disagrees with the stored material.

## 17. Outbox, recovery and reconciliation

### 17.1 Why an outbox, and why writes are object-first

- **Irreversible storage effects caused by DB state (deletes)** use a transactional outbox: the intent to delete is committed atomically with the state change that requires it, **carrying the backend identity of the object it must address**; the effect is performed later by a fenced worker; success is recorded only after an observed absence on that backend.
- **Object creation** is *object-first, DB-second*: the worker writes the canonical object of its own generation before any DB row claims it exists, and a committed DB row always refers to an object the worker already read back. A crash therefore leaves at worst an **ownerless object** (swept), never a **DB claim of a non-existent object** — except through later external loss, which reconciliation detects (§17.4).
- A two-phase commit across PostgreSQL and the object store is not available and not assumed.

### 17.2 The DB never claims an effect merely because it was requested

| State | Claims |
| :-- | :-- |
| `m7_evidence_upload_intent` `ISSUED` | an upload is **permitted**, not that one occurred |
| `m7_canonical_generation` row | a key is **reserved** for one epoch, not that an object exists |
| observation row | the worker **read back** these bytes at that generation's key **on that profile** |
| `acceptedLeaseEpoch` | which generation the observation belongs to |
| outbox `PENDING`/`LEASED` | a delete is **requested** against a named backend |
| attempt `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` | the worker issued `DELETE` and **then observed not-found**, **on the backend the row is bound to** |
| artifact `DELETED` | the linked outbox row is `CONFIRMED` by such an attempt |

### 17.3 Crash-boundary matrix

| # | Crash / failure point | Durable state after crash | Recovery |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| CB-01 | after SO-2 commit, before URL returned | intent `ISSUED` with its profile | client retries SO-2 with the same nonce → same intent, URL re-signed on the **same** profile with the same ceiling |
| CB-02 | client PUT succeeds, client never calls SO-3 | staging object; intent `ISSUED` | U9 at deadline → staging + every generation enqueued for deletion on the intent's backend |
| CB-03 | worker crashes after claim | `PROCESSING`, lease live, generation `e` allocated (possibly no object) | lease expires; U3 reclaim allocates generation `e+1`; generation `e` becomes superseded and is swept, whether or not it has an object |
| **CB-04** | **worker crashes after writing generation `e`'s canonical object, before the observation** | object `K_e` exists; intent `PROCESSING` | reclaim at `e+1` allocates `K_{e+1}`, re-reads the staging object, re-decodes and re-encodes, writes `K_{e+1}`, reads it back, records the observation. **`K_e` is never read, adopted or bound**; it is a superseded generation and is deleted (GF-7). If the intent is never reclaimed, U9 enqueues deletes for `K_e` and the staging object |
| **CB-05** | worker's observation call fails (DB error) after writing `K_e` | as CB-04 | as CB-04. The previous candidate's "read back the existing object" recovery is deliberately **removed**: re-reading a prior generation's object is exactly the adoption `M7V11-AUD-02` forbids |
| **CB-19** | **worker crashes holding an unexpired write grant, then resumes after its lease expired** | `K_e` may or may not exist; intent reclaimed at `e+1` | the resumed worker's grant is provider-expired (`grantExpiresAt < leaseExpiresAt ≤ now`, XF-DL-1), so its `PUT` is **rejected by the provider**, not merely ignored by the DB. It cannot mint another grant (XF-9). Recovery is only through a reclaim, which allocates a new key and a new grant |
| **CB-20** | **write request accepted just before `grantExpiresAt`, still streaming when the DB reclaims** | the provider either completes it before `grantExpiresAt + W` or aborts it (SP-9) | the reclaim happens at `leaseExpiresAt ≥ grantExpiresAt + W + Λ`, so the outcome is already settled when `e+1` starts; whichever way it settled, `K_e` is a superseded generation and `K_{e+1}` is the only candidate |
| **CB-21** | **crash between the generation row and the write-grant row** | impossible to half-commit: both are inserted in the claim's single transaction, and the grant's composite FK requires the generation's fence values | full rollback; the intent keeps its previous epoch and is reclaimable |
| CB-06 | SO-3 transaction rolls back (consent refused, lock timeout, crash) | intent `VALIDATED`, accepted generation's object exists, no submission | participant may retry before deadline; otherwise U9 → deletes for the accepted and every other generation |
| CB-07 | SO-3 commits, response lost | submission + receipt | pre-CCA replay lookup returns it (RS from the historical rows) |
| CB-08 | outbox delete performed, crash before attempt recorded | object absent; outbox `LEASED` | lease expires → O3 re-lease → `DELETE` (idempotent) + `HEAD` on the **same** backend → `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` |
| CB-09 | attempt recorded `ABSENT_CONFIRMED`, same transaction fails to update artifact | impossible to half-commit: O6 and A3 are one transaction | — |
| CB-10 | worker issues `DELETE`, provider returns success, `HEAD` shows present | `STILL_PRESENT` attempt | O5 retry; SP-7 makes this a provider defect, surfaced by `v_deletion_sla_critical` |
| CB-11 | stale worker (epoch `e`) finishes a delete after `e+1` leased | `e+1` holder proceeds | `e`'s attempt call rejected; `e+1` observes absence and confirms |
| CB-12 | DB references a canonical object that no longer exists (external loss) | artifact `AVAILABLE` | reconciliation `HEAD` on the artifact's own backend → `m7.w_record_canonical_missing_v1` → `MISSING` + integrity finding (§14.4) |
| CB-13 | object exists with no valid DB owner | object only | reconciliation classification → `m7_reconciliation_finding` + outbox delete on that backend (§17.4) |
| CB-14 | expired authorization arrives late (late SO-3, late worker observation) | intent terminal | function predicate fails; typed error; nothing written |
| CB-15 | duplicate provider event / callback | — | M7 consumes **no** provider callbacks; all storage facts come from worker reads. Any future callback MUST be treated as a hint that schedules a worker read |
| **CB-16** | **control-plane rotation crashes mid-transaction** | the whole `c_*` call is one transaction | full rollback: no half-registered profile, no manifest without its bindings, no two active installations |
| **CB-17** | **worker crashes between allocating generation `e+1` and writing its object, repeatedly** | many superseded generations, no object | each is swept; the intent still expires at `intentDeadlineAt`; generation rows are bounded by `intentDeadlineAt / workerLease`, an explicit and small bound |
| **CB-18** | **the backend becomes unreachable while effects are pending** | outbox rows `PENDING`, unleasable or failing | `v_deletion_sla_critical` lists them; nothing is confirmed; no artifact becomes `DELETED` |
| **CB-22** | **the signer crashes between the capability mint and the `PUT`, or the `PUT` response is lost** | one `m7_generation_capability_mint` row exists; `K_e` may or may not exist | the worker may ask the signer again: the re-mint appends `mintSeq = 2` with an **identical** `envelopeSha256` (XF-15, Corollary 4), so the second capability authorizes exactly the same conditional create until exactly the same instant, and by SP-4 it is a conflict on an existing object rather than an overwrite. If `grantExpiresAt` has passed, the signer refuses (`M7013`) and the only way forward is a reclaim at `e+1`. **A lost mint is never a reason to widen an envelope**, and no path exists to do so |
| **CB-23** | **the mint function returned an envelope, but the signer's transaction failed to commit, or its commit outcome is unknown** | either no `m7_generation_capability_mint` row (rolled back) or one committed row the signer cannot confirm | the signer **does not sign** (XF-16). It may call again: a rolled-back mint leaves the sequence unchanged, a committed one yields `mintSeq + 1` with the identical `envelopeSha256`. No capability ever exists without a committed mint row naming its envelope and signing profile (T-171d) |
| **CB-24** | **a row mechanism commits, and its response is lost** | redaction or purge with `retainDeletionHistory = true`: its completion row; purge with `retainDeletionHistory = false`: nothing of the assignment's M7 data, authorization or execution | the worker re-runs the execution: the first two return the stored `affectedRowCount` (RM-2, RM-3); the third raises `M7009 EXECUTION_ABSENT`, which the worker treats as terminal without logging or persisting the id or a count (RM-4…RM-6). A mechanism that rolled back is simply re-run (RM-7) |

### 17.4 Reconciliation sweeps (storage worker)

Every sweep is executed **per storage profile**, over the prefixes of that profile's backend, using that profile's credentials. A sweep never lists a backend it is not currently entitled to, and a finding always records the backend it was observed on.

| Sweep | Input | Classification (`m7.w_classify_object_key_v1`, which locks the intent row `FOR UPDATE` when one exists) | Action |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| staging listing | `<stagingPrefix>` of one backend | intent absent → `UNISSUED_KEY_OBJECT`; intent's `backendSha256` ≠ the listed backend → `UNISSUED_KEY_OBJECT`; intent `ISSUED`/`PROCESSING` → owned; any other state → `ORPHAN_STAGING_OBJECT`; key ≠ intent's `stagingObjectKey` → `UNISSUED_KEY_OBJECT` | finding + outbox delete on that backend with `notBefore = max(now, intent.stagingWriteFenceAt, now + policy.orphanGrace for unissued)` (XF-5) |
| canonical listing | `<evidencePrefix>` of one backend | no generation row for the key, or the generation's backend ≠ the listed backend → `UNISSUED_KEY_OBJECT`; generation epoch = `intent.leaseEpoch` and intent `PROCESSING` → owned; generation epoch = `intent.acceptedLeaseEpoch` and intent `VALIDATED` → owned; epoch = accepted and intent `CONSUMED` and artifact not `DELETED` → owned; epoch = accepted and artifact `DELETED` → `CANONICAL_OBJECT_PRESENT_AFTER_DELETION`; **epoch ≠ accepted and ≠ current** → `SUPERSEDED_GENERATION_OBJECT`; intent terminal with no accepted epoch → `ORPHAN_CANONICAL_OBJECT` | finding + outbox delete on that backend |
| superseded-generation sweep | `m7.w_sweep_superseded_generations_v1` over generation rows | epoch ≠ `acceptedLeaseEpoch` and (intent not `PROCESSING` or epoch ≠ `leaseEpoch`) | enqueue delete for that generation's key on its own backend with `notBefore ≥ writeFenceAt` (XF-5); no listing required |
| artifact audit | `AVAILABLE` artifacts listed by `m7.w_list_artifacts_for_audit_v1`, grouped by `backendSha256` | `HEAD` not-found → CB-12; sampled `GET` digest ≠ observation → `CANONICAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH` | integrity finding |
| deletion SLA | `m7.w_list_deletion_sla_v1` over the three views of §15.11.4 | — | alert; no automatic data change |

**Orphan adoption is impossible:** no function turns a found object into an intent, a generation, an observation or a submission. Ownership exists only by the key having been allocated to a canonical generation of a live intent on that backend, and bound to a consumed intent.

**`CANONICAL_OBJECT_PRESENT_AFTER_DELETION` changes meaning under fencing.** Before §11.7 it could be a tolerated race with a stale epoch. With XF-1…XF-10 in force it cannot be: by the XF-THEOREM no M7-issued capability can create a fenced key, and every confirmed delete happened at or after the fence. The finding is therefore **necessarily** an out-of-band write — a provider-console action or a compromised object-store credential — and is an integrity alarm at the same tier as `CANONICAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH`. Handling: the object is enqueued for deletion again; the existing `m7_deletion_execution_completion` row is **not** revoked (append-only, §14.1); the finding stands permanently beside it, so the record says "absence was evidenced, then something outside M7 wrote here" rather than quietly re-reporting compliance. This residual is **M7-R-10** (§28.3).

**No sweep may delete an object before that object's fence.** `w_classify_object_key_v1` returns the fence instant with the classification, and `m7.i_enqueue_delete` raises `notBefore` to it regardless, so a sweep that mis-computes it cannot produce an early effect (XF-5, defence in depth).

## 18. PostgreSQL role and security model

### 18.1 Principles

| # | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| RS-1 | All M7 objects live in schema `m7`, owned by `pagamenos_m7_owner` (NOLOGIN). No login role owns any M7 object |
| RS-2 | No login role has any table, column or sequence privilege on any M7 relation. **All M7 data access is through `SECURITY DEFINER` functions** with explicit per-role EXECUTE grants |
| RS-3 | Every M7 function has EXECUTE revoked from `PUBLIC`; default privileges for the owner in `m7` revoke EXECUTE from `PUBLIC` |
| RS-4 | Every guarded M7 table's insert/update/delete trigger requires `current_user = 'pagamenos_m7_owner'` and the function-specific transaction-local write path (`pagamenos.m7.write_path`). A mistaken future table grant to a login role therefore still cannot write |
| RS-5 | Grants on accepted A1/A2 relations go to `pagamenos_m7_owner` only, are additive, and are the minimum listed in §19.2 |
| RS-6 | Role provisioning is separate from migration and **fails closed**: the M7 migration asserts, and aborts on any mismatch (§18.4) |
| RS-7 | Runtime credentials are separated per capability and per transaction owner (§16.2.3): the CCA-private participant credential (TO-1), the session issuer credential (TO-2), the privacy request credential (TO-3), the storage worker credential (TO-4, TO-5), the deletion authority credential (TO-6) and the capability signer credential (TO-8) are distinct `DATABASE_URL`s, each loaded only by its owning module; the owner-class rotation credential (TO-7) is never present in an application deployment (§18.3) |
| RS-8 | Control-plane identity registration and retirement (`m7.c_*`) has **no login grantee at all**: it is reachable only by an owner-class actor running the governed rotation script |

### 18.2 Roles

| Role | LOGIN | Owns | Schema USAGE | Table / sequence privileges | EXECUTE | Forbidden (asserted) |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `pagamenos_m7_owner` | **NO** | schema `m7` and every object in it | `m7` (owner); `public` | on M7: owner. On accepted tables: `SELECT` on `study_participant`, `experiment_assignment`, `study_consent_event`, `purchase_intent_capture_token`, `purchase_intent`, `purchase_intent_decision_request`, `purchase_intent_decision_binding`; `REFERENCES` on `study_participant(id)`, `experiment_assignment(id)`, `study_consent_event(id)`, `purchase_intent_decision_binding(id)`; `UPDATE("id")` on `experiment_assignment` (required by `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`; every actual UPDATE is still rejected by the accepted A1 trigger) | all M7 functions (owner) | SUPERUSER, CREATEDB, CREATEROLE, REPLICATION, BYPASSRLS; any member other than the migration role(s) named in the manifest |
| `pagamenos_m7_participant_rt` | YES | nothing | `m7` | **none** | `m7.p_lock_and_prove_assignment_v1`, `m7.p_lookup_outcome_receipt_v1`, `m7.p_record_outcome_assertion_v1`, `m7.p_begin_evidence_upload_v1`, `m7.p_lookup_evidence_receipt_v1`, `m7.p_finalize_evidence_submission_v1` | any privilege on `public` tables; membership in any role; attributes as owner |
| `pagamenos_m7_session_issuer_rt` | YES | nothing | `m7` | none | `m7.s_issue_participant_session_v1`, `m7.s_revoke_participant_session_v1` | as above |
| `pagamenos_m7_privacy_request_rt` | YES | nothing | `m7` | none | `m7.r_record_erasure_request_v1` | as above |
| `pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt` | YES | nothing | `m7` | none | every `m7.w_*` function (§19.12) | `m7.a_*`, `m7.p_*`, `m7.s_*`, `m7.r_*`, `m7.c_*` |
| `pagamenos_m7_deletion_authority_rt` | YES | nothing | `m7` | none | `m7.a_mint_deletion_authorization_v1` | every other M7 function |
| **`pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt`** | YES | nothing | `m7` | none | **`m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` — and nothing else** | every other M7 function, and in particular **every `m7.w_*`**: the signer cannot claim an intent, record an observation, lease an effect, list, sweep or schedule. Conversely `pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt` holds **no** EXECUTE on `m7.x_*` (XF-13, IA-14). The role is used only by transaction owner **TO-8**, in its own process (§16.2.3) |

The **sealed signer edge** is this role plus one function. Its whole purpose is that the party able to obtain a capability envelope and the party able to do storage work are different principals with disjoint EXECUTE sets, so that no single compromised credential can both choose work and widen a write capability (§11.7.3). The database can and does prove the disjointness (IA-09, IA-14, exact-set comparison); it cannot prove what the signer process then signs, which is §11.7.4's E-E row.

Every login role: `NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS NOINHERIT`, `CONNECTION LIMIT` set, no role memberships, `rolvaliduntil` per operations policy. **None of them is granted to or granted any other role.** The pre-existing application runtime role(s) named in the manifest (`legacyRuntimeRoles`) MUST hold no privilege in schema `m7` and no membership in any M7 role. **No login role holds EXECUTE on any `m7.c_*` function** (RS-8).

### 18.3 Credential scoping (deployment conditions, verified)

| Credential | Loaded only by | Verified by |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `M7_PARTICIPANT_DATABASE_URL` → `pagamenos_m7_participant_rt` | the private CCA engine's hidden Prisma client | CCA §42–§43 capability CI extended: the env key is read in exactly one module; dependency closure check |
| `M7_SESSION_ISSUER_DATABASE_URL` | the M7 session module | same |
| `M7_PRIVACY_REQUEST_DATABASE_URL` | the M7 privacy-request service | same |
| `M7_STORAGE_WORKER_DATABASE_URL` | the M7 storage worker entry point (cron/job), not a request handler | same; deployment manifest names the job |
| `M7_DELETION_AUTHORITY_DATABASE_URL` | an operator tool outside the web deployment | not present in the web deployment's environment (deployment check) |
| **`M7_CAPABILITY_SIGNER_DATABASE_URL`** → `pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt` | the M7 **capability signer** module (TO-8), running as **its own process**, and nothing else | dependency-closure check: the env key is read in exactly one module, that module exports exactly one function whose only argument is a `generationGrantId`, it does not import the CCA engine, and no other module imports the provider signing SDK (IMP-05, IMP-18, T-171b); process separation from the storage worker (IMP-20, T-189) |
| **the provider write-signing credentials** (the signing half of each live profile's `credentialProfileId`) | the same capability-signer process, keyed by `credentialProfileId` and selected **only** by the `signing_credential_profile_id` the mint function returns (XF-17) | absent from the storage worker's environment and from every request handler (XC-5); the set present equals the live profiles' `credentialProfileId`s of every live backend, published as `deployment.capabilitySigner.credentialProfileIds[]` (XC-7, MA-15); a retired profile's signing credential is removed after its retirement commits |
| the control-plane rotation credential (owner-class) | the governed rotation script, run manually or by a gated pipeline | never present in any application deployment (deployment check) |
| per-storage-profile object-store credentials, keyed by `credentialProfileId` | the storage worker and the presigning path, selected **by the live profile the DB hands the worker for the row being acted on** (SI-3, SI-4) | the manifest's `storage.credentialScopes[]`; §19.13 does not and cannot verify object-store ACLs, so this is an operational prerequisite (IMP-04) |

#### 18.3.0 Object-store write capability, narrowed (XF-1)

`M7V11R2-AUD-01` turns on a credential fact, so it is stated here as a verified deployment condition rather than only in §11.7:

| # | Condition on the object-store ACLs of every registered backend | Verified by |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| XC-1 | the **worker** credential (`credentialProfileId` of any profile) has `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE`, `LIST` under `<stagingPrefix>` and `<evidencePrefix>`, and **no** `PUT`/`POST`/`COPY`/multipart-initiate or any other create or overwrite right under `<evidencePrefix>` | provider ACL export compared against `storage.capabilities.credentialScopes[]`; IMP-04, re-verified per rotation |
| XC-2 | the **staging** credential may only create exact keys under `<stagingPrefix>`, never a prefix-wide right, and never anything under `<evidencePrefix>` | same |
| XC-3 | the **capability-signing** credential can only *sign or mint* an exact-key, expiry-bounded write capability (SP-9/SP-10); it is never used to issue a write directly; and it is present in **exactly one** environment — the capability-signer module's. **Round 3 changes this condition**: round 2 placed it in the storage worker's environment, which is precisely what made `M7V11R3-AUD-01` reachable without any out-of-band credential | same + deployment check + dependency closure (IMP-18) |
| XC-4 | a positive test proves XC-1: with the worker credential alone, a `PUT` to a fresh key under `<evidencePrefix>` is **rejected by the provider** (T-138b) | adversarial suite, **STORE** tier |
| **XC-5** | the **storage worker's** environment contains no credential able to sign a write capability, and the **signer's** environment contains no credential able to `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` or `LIST` any M7 prefix. Neither can do the other's job with its own secrets | deployment check; T-171b |
| **XC-6** | the signer module exposes **one** entry point, whose only argument is an opaque `generationGrantId`; it exports no function accepting a key, prefix, expiry, interval, operation or **credential/profile identifier**, and no other module in the deployment's dependency closure imports the provider signing SDK | dependency-closure check (IMP-05, IMP-18); **T-171b**; the database half is the one-parameter signature pinned by the expectation set (T-135) |
| **XC-7** | **signer routing.** The signer signs with exactly the credential named by the `signing_credential_profile_id` the mint function returned for that call, and with no other; if its environment has no credential for that identifier it signs nothing and reports a deployment defect (it never falls back to another credential). It signs only after the mint transaction committed (XF-16). Its credential set equals the live profiles' `credentialProfileId`s, so a credential rotation is deployed to the signer **before** the new profile is registered (a registered profile is live, and `i_signing_profile` may select it once the executing profile is retired) and removed **after** the old profile is retired | deployment check against `deployment.capabilitySigner.credentialProfileIds[]` (MA-15); **T-171c**, **T-171d** |

XC-1…XC-7 are the reason the XF-THEOREM's steps (1) and (3) hold, and XC-7 is the reason a credential rotation cannot silently change which authority signs. They are ACL, environment and dependency-topology statements, **not** database constraints, and the specification says so plainly: PostgreSQL cannot verify any of them, `m7.w_verify_control_plane_catalog_v1` does not claim to, T-138b is the only thing that demonstrates XC-1 on a real provider, and T-171b is the only thing that demonstrates XC-5 and XC-6 on a real deployment. A deployment that cannot demonstrate XC-4 has **not** closed `M7V11R2-AUD-01`, and one that cannot demonstrate XC-5 and XC-6 has **not** closed `M7V11R3-AUD-01`, whatever the database contains.

**What the database *can* prove about the same boundary, and does:** that `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` is the only function returning an envelope; that its signature admits no envelope component; that its EXECUTE grantee set is exactly `{pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt}`; that that role's whole EXECUTE set is exactly that one function; that `pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt` is not in the grantee set; and that no role holds both (IA-09, **IA-14**, T-132, T-171b). Those are E-A facts and are verified in both directions by the exact-set comparison. The gap between them and XC-5/XC-6 is exactly the **E-E** row of §11.7.4, and it is not papered over.

Within one Node process these separations are an **in-process capability model** (CCA §45), not a defence against arbitrary code execution. That limit is residual **M7-R-02**.

#### 18.3.1 Strengthening M7-R-01 without a second consent algorithm

`M7V11-AUD-05`'s companion instruction is explicit: **M7-R-01 must not be "solved" by duplicating A1 consent semantics in PostgreSQL.** V1.1 therefore keeps the residual explicit (§9.6, §28.3) and strengthens only the *topology* and its *verification*:

| # | Strengthening | Why it is not a second consent algorithm |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| CS-1 | `M7_PARTICIPANT_DATABASE_URL` is read in exactly one module (the private CCA engine), proved by a dependency-closure check, and that module exports no client, no transaction and no raw-query capability | it constrains *who may reach the credential*, not *what consent means* |
| CS-2 | The participant role's EXECUTE set is exactly the six `p_*` functions and nothing else; the catalog verifier proves the set is exact in both directions (§19.13) | an ACL statement, not a predicate |
| CS-3 | The participant credential is absent from every worker, job, operator and rotation environment (deployment check, IMP-03) | deployment scoping |
| CS-4 | `m7.p_lock_and_prove_assignment_v1` is a separate function from every write function, so the CCA engine's lock step cannot be skipped by calling a write function "the same way" — the write functions re-take the lock and re-validate the session themselves | duplication of *locking*, not of consent |
| CS-5 | The residual is an executed test (T-23), not a footnote: the suite asserts that a direct call **succeeds**, so nobody can mistake the topology for a database consent guarantee | honesty requirement |

What V1.1 deliberately does **not** do: read `study_consent_event` to decide whether a participant write may proceed; compute `consentSeq`; evaluate `optionalEvidenceConsent`; or gate any `p_*` function on a consent state. The only consent-event read anywhere in M7 is `m7.i_withdrawal_event`, used solely as the RT-17 **deletion/expiry trigger** (AC-06, §15.2), never as collection authorization.

### 18.4 Fail-closed provisioning

Roles are created by a separately governed provisioning step (passwords are secrets and are never in a migration). The M7 migration **only asserts and grants**:

| ID | Install assertion (migration aborts with `RAISE EXCEPTION` if false) |
| :-- | :-- |
| IA-01 | every role of §18.2 exists |
| IA-02 | `pagamenos_m7_owner`: `rolcanlogin = false`, not superuser/createdb/createrole/replication/bypassrls |
| IA-03 | every M7 login role: `rolcanlogin = true`, not superuser/createdb/createrole/replication/bypassrls, `rolinherit = false` |
| IA-04 | no M7 login role is a member of any role, and no role is a member of an M7 login role |
| IA-05 | the members of `pagamenos_m7_owner` are exactly `{session_user}` of the migration (the migration role) |
| IA-06 | no role holds EXECUTE on both `m7.a_mint_deletion_authorization_v1` and any `m7.w_*` function (checked after grants) |
| **IA-14** | after grants: no role holds EXECUTE on both `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` and any `m7.w_*`, `m7.p_*`, `m7.s_*`, `m7.r_*` or `m7.a_*` function; the grantee set of `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` is exactly `{pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt}`; and that role's total EXECUTE set in schema `m7` has cardinality **1**. This is the database half of the sealed signer edge (XF-13) and the migration aborts if any part of it is false |
| IA-07 | schema `m7` does not pre-exist (fresh install); rotation is §23.7 and never re-runs this script |
| IA-08 | server version `≥ 150000` (`current_setting('server_version_num')`) |
| IA-09 | after all DDL and grants: the **exact set** of functions in `m7` equals the manifest's expectation set, each with the declared `prosecdef`, `proconfig`, owner, source digest and **exact** EXECUTE grantee set (missing *and* extra grants are violations) |
| IA-10 | after all DDL: no M7 relation, column or sequence grants any privilege to any role other than the owner, and the schema ACL is exactly `{owner: ALL} ∪ {each login role: USAGE}` |
| IA-11 | the **exact set** of triggers, constraints and indexes in `m7` equals the manifest's expectation set, and every trigger is `tgenabled = 'O'` |
| IA-12 | the **exact set** of roles and role memberships relevant to M7 equals the manifest's expectation set |
| IA-13 | exactly one active control-plane installation exists, its manifest is registered, its digest matches, and its storage profile and backend are live |

A failed `GRANT`/`REVOKE` raises and aborts the single migration transaction (PostgreSQL semantics). **There is no fallback path**: the application's M7 modules refuse to start unless the control-plane check of §23.6 passes, so a missing role or grant cannot silently route M7 work through a more privileged connection.

### 18.5 `SECURITY DEFINER` hardening — rules for every definer function

| # | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| SD-1 | owner `pagamenos_m7_owner`; allowed executors exactly as §18.2 (and, for `c_*`, none) |
| SD-2 | `SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp` in `proconfig`. `pg_temp` is listed **last** explicitly, because an unlisted `pg_temp` is searched **first** and would let a caller shadow objects with temporary tables or functions |
| SD-3 | every relation, type and M7 function referenced is schema-qualified (`m7.…`, `public.…`); every built-in function is `pg_catalog.`-qualified in security-relevant expressions |
| SD-4 | no dynamic SQL (`EXECUTE`), no `format()` of identifiers, no `COPY`, no `dblink`/extension calls — except inside the install-time `DO` blocks of §19.2, §19.10.1 and §19.13, which run as the migration role before any grant exists |
| SD-5 | `REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION … FROM PUBLIC` then explicit `GRANT EXECUTE … TO <role>` |
| SD-6 | the function sets its write-path marker with `pg_catalog.set_config('pagamenos.m7.write_path', '<PATH>', true)` as its first statement and resets it to `''` before every normal return |
| SD-7 | the function validates the control-plane digest parameter (`m7.i_assert_control_plane`) before any other read or write |
| SD-8 | parameters are typed; free text is length- and pattern-checked before use |
| SD-9 | `lock_timeout = '5s'` set in `proconfig` (§16.1) |
| SD-10 | internal helpers (`m7.i_*`) and trigger functions are `SECURITY INVOKER`, carry the same `search_path`, and have EXECUTE revoked from `PUBLIC` with no grants; they run only as the owner inside definer functions or as triggers |
| SD-11 | any function that acts on an existing object resolves its storage profile from the row and calls `m7.i_require_routable_profile` before issuing any routing-relevant value to its caller (SI-3) |
| **SD-12** | a function calls `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness` (or `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness`) **iff** it creates a drain obligation or mints external write authority on that backend (BL-2's kinds **C** and **M**), and it does so in phase P2 — after its explicit row locks, before its first write. §11.10.4 enumerates exactly those functions, and NW-1…NW-6 the backend-scoped writers that must **not** take it; **T-180** checks both directions against the `prosrc` digests the manifest pins |
| **SD-14** | every definer function follows the phase discipline and orders of §16.2.5 (LG-1…LG-10) and matches its row of `database.lockProfiles[]`; in particular every `FOR UPDATE` / `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on `m7_storage_backend`, `m7_storage_profile` and `m7_participant_session` is `NOWAIT` (LG-10) and every multi-assignment P3 loop is ordered by `"assignmentId"` (LG-8); **T-181** checks it at source level |
| **SD-13** | no function signature anywhere in schema `m7` accepts an object key, a key prefix, a `backendSha256`, a capability expiry, an interval used as a capability validity, or a capability operation **as a parameter of a capability request** (XF-12). The one capability function takes `(manifestSha256, generationGrantId)`; the expectation set pins its `regprocedure` so an added overload is `FN-EXTRA` (T-135) |

**Why a caller-set write-path marker cannot forge generation.** Custom settings are settable by any role, but a login role has no table privilege, so setting the marker grants nothing. A definer function always overwrites the marker with its own value before writing. Trigger checks require both the marker and `current_user = 'pagamenos_m7_owner'`.

### 18.6 `DatabaseExecutionContext` and transaction owners (CCA §29, §33–§36)

The complete, enumerated set. It is the `DatabaseExecutionContext` view of §16.2.3 and lists **exactly** the same eight owners; neither table may be extended without the other (T-189).

| # | Transaction owner | CCA class | Registration | Nesting | Explicit class-1 lock? | Class 10 |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| TO-1 | private CCA engine (SO-1/2/3) | B (accepted) | unchanged (CCA §29) | CCA rejects re-entry | yes (first) | `FOR SHARE` (SO-2, SO-3) |
| TO-2 | M7 session module (issue/revoke) | **new C-class owner proposed by this candidate** | registers in `DatabaseExecutionContext` | CCA rejects if it is active | no | — |
| TO-3 | M7 privacy-request service | **new, proposed** | same | same | no | — |
| TO-4 | M7 storage worker — pipeline, outbox, reconciliation, scheduling | **new, proposed** | same; runs in a job process, never inside a request transaction | same | no | `FOR SHARE` (§11.10.4 subset) |
| TO-5 | M7 storage worker — row mechanisms (`w_execute_row_redaction_v1`, `w_execute_row_purge_v1`) | **new, proposed** | same job process; declared separately because of LO-1 | same | **yes (first)** | — |
| TO-6 | deletion authority tool | **new, proposed** | outside the web deployment | same | no | — |
| TO-7 | control-plane rotation script | **new, proposed** | outside the web deployment; class 10 and class 0 only | same | no | `FOR SHARE` / `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` (first; `M7014`, RR-1…RR-7) |
| **TO-8** | **M7 capability signer** (`x_mint_generation_capability_v1`) | **new, proposed** | **its own process and its own owner kind**; registers every transaction it opens; refuses to open one while any registered transaction is active | CCA rejects if a TO-8 transaction is active; the signer never imports the CCA engine | **no** (and no implicit assignment reference) | `FOR SHARE` (WC-3) |

These additions become permitted only if this candidate is accepted (CCA §33 class C: *"unless a future accepted authority artifact explicitly adds them"*). Only TO-1 (accepted) and TO-5 access `experiment_assignment` with an explicit lock, and TO-5 only from inside PostgreSQL, as its first lock. TO-3, TO-4's schedulers and TO-6 reach it only through the implicit referential-integrity `FOR KEY SHARE` of IW-1, which is not a direct assignment lock under CCA §37 and is enumerated rather than denied (LO-2, J-30).

## 19. Complete normative DDL

### 19.1 Status and conventions of this section

- This section is **normative specification text** for a future migration. It is not executed by this candidate. The implementation migration MUST be byte-equivalent in semantics; its source digest is bound by the control-plane manifest (§23).
- Target: PostgreSQL ≥ 15. No extension is required (`gen_random_uuid`, `sha256` are core).
- **Prisma.** All M7 objects live in schema `m7`, outside the Prisma-managed schema set. Prisma cannot express roles, grants, `SECURITY DEFINER`, triggers, partial unique indexes, composite self-references with `MATCH SIMPLE` semantics, or the guard pattern; **this SQL, not a Prisma model, is the authority for every invariant here.** The implementation MUST NOT add M7 models to `schema.prisma` that would let Prisma client code address M7 tables, and `db:migrate:check` MUST be extended to (a) prove Prisma's diff is unaffected by schema `m7`, and (b) run the catalog verification of §19.13 against a real database.
- Identifiers: schema `m7`; tables lowercase; columns quoted camelCase (accepted project convention).
- The script runs in **one transaction**; any failure leaves no partial M7 schema.
- Section order: §19.2 preamble · §19.3 enums · §19.4 control-plane identity (storage backend/profile, policy, vocabulary, manifest, installation) · §19.5 catalog expectation set · §19.6 session · §19.7 outcome · §19.8 evidence, generations, storage · §19.9 privacy, deletion, outbox · §19.10 triggers · §19.11–§19.12 functions · §19.13 catalog verification and grants · §19.14 inventory.

### 19.2 Preamble — install assertions, schema, accepted-table grants

```sql
BEGIN;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- IA-01 .. IA-08 : fail-closed provisioning assertions (§18.4)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DO $install$
DECLARE
    v_login  CONSTANT text[] := ARRAY[
        'pagamenos_m7_participant_rt', 'pagamenos_m7_session_issuer_rt',
        'pagamenos_m7_privacy_request_rt', 'pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt',
        'pagamenos_m7_deletion_authority_rt', 'pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt'];
    v_role text;
BEGIN
    IF pg_catalog.current_setting('server_version_num')::integer < 150000 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL IA-08: PostgreSQL >= 15 required';
    END IF;

    FOREACH v_role IN ARRAY (v_login || ARRAY['pagamenos_m7_owner']) LOOP
        IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = v_role) THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL IA-01: role % does not exist', v_role;
        END IF;
    END LOOP;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles
               WHERE rolname = 'pagamenos_m7_owner'
                 AND (rolcanlogin OR rolsuper OR rolcreatedb OR rolcreaterole
                      OR rolreplication OR rolbypassrls)) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL IA-02: pagamenos_m7_owner attributes invalid';
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles
               WHERE rolname = ANY (v_login)
                 AND (NOT rolcanlogin OR rolsuper OR rolcreatedb OR rolcreaterole
                      OR rolreplication OR rolbypassrls OR rolinherit)) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL IA-03: M7 login role attributes invalid';
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1
               FROM pg_catalog.pg_auth_members m
               JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid
               JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles u ON u.oid = m.member
               WHERE g.rolname = ANY (v_login) OR u.rolname = ANY (v_login)) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL IA-04: M7 login roles must have no memberships';
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1
               FROM pg_catalog.pg_auth_members m
               JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid
               JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles u ON u.oid = m.member
               WHERE g.rolname = 'pagamenos_m7_owner' AND u.rolname <> session_user)
       OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1
               FROM pg_catalog.pg_auth_members m
               JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid
               JOIN pg_catalog.pg_roles u ON u.oid = m.member
               WHERE g.rolname = 'pagamenos_m7_owner' AND u.rolname = session_user) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL IA-05: members of pagamenos_m7_owner must be exactly the migration role';
    END IF;

    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace WHERE nspname = 'm7') THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL IA-07: schema m7 already exists; re-install refused (rotation is §23.7)';
    END IF;
END
$install$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Schema and the minimum additive grants on accepted A1/A2 relations (RS-5).
-- Executed by the migration role, which owns the accepted relations.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE SCHEMA m7 AUTHORIZATION pagamenos_m7_owner;
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA m7 FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA m7 TO pagamenos_m7_participant_rt, pagamenos_m7_session_issuer_rt,
    pagamenos_m7_privacy_request_rt, pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt, pagamenos_m7_deletion_authority_rt,
    pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt;

GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO pagamenos_m7_owner;
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE
    public.study_participant, public.experiment_assignment, public.study_consent_event,
    public.purchase_intent_capture_token, public.purchase_intent,
    public.purchase_intent_decision_request, public.purchase_intent_decision_binding
  TO pagamenos_m7_owner;
GRANT REFERENCES ("id") ON TABLE public.study_participant                TO pagamenos_m7_owner;
GRANT REFERENCES ("id") ON TABLE public.experiment_assignment            TO pagamenos_m7_owner;
GRANT REFERENCES ("id") ON TABLE public.study_consent_event              TO pagamenos_m7_owner;
GRANT REFERENCES ("id") ON TABLE public.purchase_intent_decision_binding TO pagamenos_m7_owner;
-- Required only so that SELECT ... FOR UPDATE may lock the assignment row (PostgreSQL requires
-- UPDATE privilege on at least one column for row-locking clauses). Every actual UPDATE remains
-- rejected by the accepted A1 trigger "experiment_assignment_no_update".
GRANT UPDATE ("id") ON TABLE public.experiment_assignment TO pagamenos_m7_owner;

-- Everything below is created by, and owned by, pagamenos_m7_owner.
SET LOCAL ROLE pagamenos_m7_owner;

ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA m7 REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA m7 REVOKE ALL ON TABLES FROM PUBLIC;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA m7 REVOKE ALL ON SEQUENCES FROM PUBLIC;
```

### 19.3 Enumerated types

```sql
CREATE TYPE m7."M7OutcomeStatusLabel"      AS ENUM ('INTENDED','ATTEMPTED','SELF_REPORTED','FAILED','ABANDONED');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7AssertionKind"           AS ENUM ('ORIGINAL','CORRECTION','RETRACTION');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7OccurrenceAssertion"     AS ENUM ('NONE','ATTEMPTED_PURCHASE','REALIZED_PURCHASE');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7MerchantAssertionKind"   AS ENUM ('NOT_ASSERTED','VOCABULARY_MERCHANT','UNLISTED_MERCHANT');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7EventTimeAssertionKind"  AS ENUM ('NOT_ASSERTED','INSTANT','LIMA_DATE');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7OutcomeResultKind"       AS ENUM ('RECORDED','CAPTURE_ALIAS');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7EvidenceResultKind"      AS ENUM ('SUBMITTED','SUBMISSION_ALIAS');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7UploadIntentState"       AS ENUM ('ISSUED','PROCESSING','VALIDATED','CONSUMED',
                                                    'REJECTED_CONTENT','EXPIRED','TERMINAL_FAILURE');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7ContentRejectionReason"  AS ENUM ('SIZE_EXCEEDED','MAGIC_BYTES_MISMATCH','DECODE_FAILED',
                                                    'PIXEL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED','REENCODE_FAILED');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7TerminalFailureReason"   AS ENUM ('CANONICAL_KEY_CONFLICT','READBACK_FAILED','PROVIDER_PERMANENT_ERROR');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7ArtifactState"           AS ENUM ('AVAILABLE','DELETION_SCHEDULED','DELETED','MISSING');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7ObjectZone"              AS ENUM ('STAGING','CANONICAL');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7StorageEffectKind"       AS ENUM ('DELETE_OBJECT');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7OutboxState"             AS ENUM ('PENDING','LEASED','CONFIRMED','FAILED_PERMANENT');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7EffectAttemptResult"     AS ENUM ('ABSENT_CONFIRMED','STILL_PRESENT',
                                                    'PROVIDER_ERROR_RETRYABLE','PROVIDER_ERROR_PERMANENT');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7IntegrityFindingKind"    AS ENUM ('CANONICAL_OBJECT_MISSING','CANONICAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7ReconciliationFindingKind" AS ENUM ('UNISSUED_KEY_OBJECT','ORPHAN_STAGING_OBJECT',
                                                    'ORPHAN_CANONICAL_OBJECT','SUPERSEDED_GENERATION_OBJECT',
                                                    'CANONICAL_OBJECT_PRESENT_AFTER_DELETION');
CREATE TYPE m7."M7SessionRevocationReason" AS ENUM ('LOGOUT','ROTATED','REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED','ADMINISTRATIVE');
