-- whose literal arguments equal the reviewed manifest's "database.controlPlaneInstall" object. Its values
-- are NOT asserted by this document.
--   SELECT m7.c_register_storage_backend_v1(...);           -- returns backendSha256
--   SELECT m7.c_register_storage_profile_v1(...);
--   SELECT m7.c_register_retention_policy_v1(...);
--   SELECT m7.c_register_merchant_vocabulary_v1(...);
--   SELECT m7.c_register_manifest_v1(<manifestVersion>, <manifestSha256>, ...);
--   SELECT m7.c_load_catalog_expectations_v1(<manifestVersion>, ...);
--   SELECT m7.c_activate_manifest_v1(<manifestVersion>, <manifestSha256>);

-- IA-06, IA-09..IA-13: final fail-closed catalog assertion, against the manifest just activated.
DO $final$
DECLARE v text; v_mv text;
BEGIN
    SELECT i."manifestVersion" INTO v_mv FROM m7.m7_control_plane_installation i WHERE i."retiredAt" IS NULL;
    IF v_mv IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL: no active control-plane installation';
    END IF;
    FOR v IN SELECT * FROM m7.i_catalog_violations(v_mv) LOOP
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'M7_INSTALL catalog violation: %', v;
    END LOOP;
END
$final$;

RESET ROLE;
COMMIT;
```

## 20. Persisted-class accounting

Every normative persisted class M7 introduces is listed below. There is **no hidden assertion unit**: the only rows carrying a participant's claim about the world are `m7_outcome_assertion` (an explicit assertion) and `m7_evidence_submission` (the submission act). Everything else is capability, candidate, storage-identity, storage-operational, audit, control-plane or deletion bookkeeping.

### 20.3 Deliberately not created

| Not created | Why |
| :-- | :-- |
| any `VerifiedValue`, verification, verdict or VS-level table | C1/C2 own them (§22); register §4 |
| any `PurchaseOccasion`, occasion-candidate, source-observation or decomposition-manifest table | B1/B2 own them; M7 must not become the occasion authority |
| any "current status", "latest assertion" or "effective VS level" column or materialized projection | §13.6; P-14 principle |
| any participant, assignment, intent or decision identifier column beyond the trigger-verified `assignmentId` and the FK chain | §7.3; JBA §7.6 forbids trusting a denormalized link |
| any free-text column on a participant-authored row | FINAL §33 minimization |
| any holiday, corpus, protocol or consent table | A1/A2 own them; M7 reads consent events only as the RT-17 deletion trigger |
| any **mutable** storage-location column, application-side backend map, or "current storage" pointer on a historical row | `M7V11-AUD-01`: that is exactly the construction that produces false proofs of deletion (§11.1.1) |
| any second canonical key per intent, or a key derived from the intent alone | `M7V11-AUD-02`: one key per intent permits adoption of a stale epoch's external write (§11.6.1) |
| any column that would let a caller supply a lease epoch, storage profile, backend or object key | §9.3 forbidden list; SI-1 |
| any column holding a signature, presigned URL, token or other write-capability **secret** | §11.7 XF-8: the grant record holds a mode and two instants; a secret in PostgreSQL would be a new exfiltration class and would add nothing to the proof |
| any writable `writeFenceAt`, fence-extension function, or "renew grant" path | §11.7 XF-9: extending a fence retroactively invalidates every absence proof taken against it |
| any function parameter that names an object key, a prefix, a backend, a capability expiry or a capability operation **in a capability request** | `M7V11R3-AUD-01`: an interface shaped `mintCapability(key, validUntil)` puts the envelope in the caller's hands, where no database object can fence it. The signer takes one opaque `generationGrantId` (§11.7.3 XF-12, SD-13) |
| any claim, count, constraint or proof step asserting that **exactly one physical provider token** was minted for a key | `M7V11R3-AUD-01`: the signature is produced outside PostgreSQL, so no `PRIMARY KEY` can establish it. What is asserted instead is envelope immutability — nothing M7 can mint is *wider* (§11.7.0, §11.7.5 step (2)) |
| any column able to hold a provider signature, token, presigned URL or secret on the grant **or the mint** row | §11.7.3 XF-8: it would add an exfiltration class and prove nothing the envelope digest does not already identify |
| any path by which `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` can retire the backend the **active** manifest routes to | `M7V11R3-AUD-02`: it strands the live installation on a retired manifest/profile chain, and a freshly rotated-to backend is drained by definition, so it was the easiest state to reach (§11.10.2 RT-2) |
| any serialization claim resting on a lock that only **one** side of a race takes | `M7V11R3-AUD-02`: round-2 `RC-19` claimed the retirement's `FOR UPDATE` serialized issuance and enqueueing, and issuance never touched it. The two-sided liveness lock replaces it (§11.10.3, §11.10.6) |
| a second definition of "this backend is live enough to accept new work" | the same drift `M7V11R2-AUD-04` produced for "drained": there is exactly one, `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness`, and **T-180** fails a migration containing a second (BL-2) |
| any second definition of "the backend is drained" | `M7V11R2-AUD-04`: two definitions drifted once and stranded bytes; there is now exactly one, `m7.i_backend_is_drained` (§11.9) |
| any outbox timing value read from the **active** manifest | `M7V11R2-AUD-03`: it silently invalidates DL-4 after a rotation (§15.11.6 DL-5) |
| any copy of the intent's issuance profile onto a generation, observation or artifact | `M7V11R2-AUD-02`: after a rotation that is false provenance (§11.8) |
| an `attempts` reset on requeue | `M7V11R2-AUD-03`: it launders an SLA failure into apparent compliance (§15.11.6 DL-6) |
| any parameter, environment switch or signer-side choice that selects **which credential or profile signs** a capability | `M7V11R4` signer-routing requirement: credential selection is a capability decision, so it is resolved by the database after the liveness lock and recorded (XF-17); the signer holds no selection logic of its own (XC-7) |
| a liveness lock on a path that only mutates or removes an obligation | `M7V11R4-AUD-03`: it serializes nothing BL-SAFE needs, and every unnecessary lock is one more edge in the lock graph (§11.10.4 NW-1…NW-6) |
| a lock order stated in prose without a per-function matrix derived from the bodies | `M7V11R4-AUD-02`: round 3's prose and SQL disagreed in three places (§16.2.1). The order is now the published `database.lockProfiles[]` and a source check (§16.2.6, T-181) |
| a transaction-owner table that omits a principal able to open an M7 transaction | `M7V11R4-AUD-01`: TO-8 (§16.2.3); `database.transactionOwners[]` and T-189 make omission detectable |

## 21. B/C firewall

### 21.1 What M7 V1.1 does not establish

| M7 does **not** | Authority |
| :-- | :-- |
| establish `PurchaseOccasion` identity, or become its authority | RAT R-B-01/R-B-02, P-01; JBA BI-01 |
| decide B1/B2 scientific distinctness, or emit any candidate | RAT R-B-11, HR-B-02; JBA §8 |
| define C1 scientific value or C2 scientific independence | RAT §4.5, §8.2; register §4 |
| let an M7 row become a B denominator, or any denominator | RAT P-06, P-07; §20.2 |
| let an M7 status, label, VS level or evidence existence become verification | JBA BI-21, BI-23; §22 |
| persist any final independence, contamination, eligibility, threshold or C2 analytical status | RAT P-06 |
| convert `PROVENANCE_UNKNOWN`, a `failed` label or an absence into a negative finding | RAT P-13; JBA §7.4.1–§7.4.2 |
| infer how many purchase-shaped assertions one `Outcome` encodes, or how many candidates/occasions it may support | JBA §7.2, §23 |
| write, extend, reinterpret or own any B or C artifact | JBA §7.1 |

`m7_outcome` existence is not an occurrence claim: it is one row per accepted `Decision`, created only because RT-09 fixes that entity cardinality and because `SavingEvidence` needs a stable FK target (§13.1–§13.2).

### 21.2 Terminology compliance

This document never uses the superseded label `B1 Opportunity Identity`, and never uses the bare word "occasion" in a B sense: RT-09's unit is written **purchase-decision occasion** and the canonical B2 unit is written `PurchaseOccasion` (register §4; JBA §23; RAT §11).

### 21.3 The trusted-generation facts M7 exposes — minimal and explicit

JBA §18.4.7 assigns the **mechanism** for S-2 trusted generation to B1S "via a named M7 ingestion integration contract", and records the M7-side part as an explicit dependency (OP-5). This section states exactly what M7 V1.1 would make re-provable, in a form B1S can consume. It **claims nothing about grounding**.

| ID | Fact M7 exposes | How it is re-provable | Enforcement class |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **M7-TG-1** | every `m7_outcome_assertion` row was inserted while `current_user = pagamenos_m7_owner` **and** the transaction-local write path was `M7_RECORD_OUTCOME_ASSERTION_V1` | `m7_outcome_assertion_a_guard_insert` + `m7_outcome_assertion_path_ck`; no login role holds any table or column privilege (§19.13 `REL-ACL`, `COL-ACL`) | **E-A** against every non-owner actor |
| **M7-TG-2** | the only object that sets that write path is `m7.p_record_outcome_assertion_v1`, whose EXECUTE grantee set is **exactly** `{pagamenos_m7_participant_rt}` — missing and extra grants both detected | `m7.w_verify_control_plane_catalog_v1` `GRANT-MISSING` / `GRANT-EXTRA` rows; the function's `prosrc` digest is bound by the manifest and compared (`FN-DRIFT`) | **E-E** (capability) + exact catalog check |
| **M7-TG-3** | that function inserted only after validating an unexpired, unrevoked session whose participant equals the assignment owner, with the assignment row locked | `m7.i_require_session`, `m7.i_lock_owned_assignment`, `m7.t_assertion_coherence` | **E-A** against any actor lacking the participant's live session secret |
| **M7-TG-4** | the same three properties hold for `m7_evidence_submission` (`M7_FINALIZE_EVIDENCE_V1`, `m7.p_finalize_evidence_submission_v1`), and its bytes were observed by the storage worker, not claimed by a client | guards + `m7.t_submission_coherence` + `UNIQUE(observationId)` + the observation's own path/role | **E-A** + **E-E** |
| **M7-TG-5** | the S-2 source identity pair is stable forever: `m7_outcome_assertion.id` plus its single originating receipt | `m7_outcome_command_receipt_one_origin` partial unique index | **E-A** |
| **M7-TG-6** | correction/retraction never rewrites a prior observation: a new row explicitly supersedes the prior one, at most one successor each | §14.2; `m7_outcome_assertion_single_successor` | **E-A** |
| **M7-TG-7** | the control plane the above depends on is itself checkable at read time, without trusting any row field, and the check is an **exact-set** comparison against the reviewed manifest | `m7.w_verify_control_plane_catalog_v1` returns zero rows; the active installation's manifest digest equals the expected manifest digest (§23.6) | **E-E**, subject to JBA §18.3/BI-32 |
| **M7-TG-8** | an evidence submission's bytes are bound to **one immutable storage authority** and **one fenced generation**, so "which object, on which backend, produced by which epoch" is a database fact rather than an application inference | `backendSha256` on every storage-bearing row; `(uploadIntentId, acceptedLeaseEpoch)` composite FK to `m7_canonical_generation` | **E-A** |
| **M7-TG-9** | a recorded deletion of that evidence was confirmed absent **on that same authority** | `m7_storage_effect_attempt(outboxId, executingBackendSha256)` composite FK + `t_outbox_guard` O6 | **E-D** (proof of absence) |
| **M7-TG-10** | the **executing** storage profile and codec pipeline that produced the accepted bytes are recorded on the accepted generation, its observation and the artifact, and the recorded `encoderGeneration` is that profile's pinned value — so a credential or codec rotation is legible in the record instead of being smoothed over (§11.8) | `m7_evidence_artifact(uploadIntentId, acceptedLeaseEpoch, acceptedExecutingProfileId, backendSha256)` composite FK; `m7_storage_observation(executingProfileId, encoderGeneration)` composite FK to `m7_storage_profile(id, encoderGeneration)` | **E-A** |
| **M7-TG-11** | the absence in M7-TG-9 is **permanent, not momentary**: the confirming attempt could not be recorded before the object's `writeFenceAt`, and **no authorization envelope M7 can mint** carries a `validUntil` later than that key's own `grantExpiresAt`, so nothing M7 can mint authorizes creating it at or after the fence (§11.7 XF-THEOREM, envelope form). **A consumer must not read this as "only one token was ever signed"** — that claim was withdrawn in round 3 (§11.7.0) | `m7_canonical_generation.writeFenceAt` / `m7_evidence_upload_intent.stagingWriteFenceAt`; `m7.i_object_write_fence` enforced in `m7.i_enqueue_delete` and re-checked in `m7.t_outbox_coherence`; the envelope `UNIQUE` + `m7_generation_capability_mint_envelope_fkey` (M7-I118); XC-1…XC-6 verified operationally | **E-D** for the provider half and **E-E** for the signer half — see the two boundary rows below |

**Boundaries stated honestly, not hidden:**

| Limit | Consequence |
| :-- | :-- |
| the A1 consent predicate having authorized the collection is **not** DB-provable (§9.6) | a consumer may rely on M7-TG-1…9 for *generation*, never for *consent* |
| participant identity ultimately rests on authentication (FINAL §28; A1 §12 puts full authentication out of A1 scope) | M7-TG-3 is proof against an actor lacking the session secret, not proof of who the human was |
| owner-class actors (superuser, migration owner, table owner, any member of `pagamenos_m7_owner`) | **no technical guarantee** (JBA §19.4, PR-5); the exact-set catalog check makes many such changes detectable to an unmodified verifier, which is all BI-32 permits claiming |
| object-store ACLs and provider behaviour | not checkable from PostgreSQL; SP-1…SP-10 are verified operationally (IMP-04, IMP-15) and recorded as residual **M7-R-04**/**M7-R-05**/**M7-R-09** |
| **M7-TG-11 rests on facts PostgreSQL cannot see — of two different kinds.** *Provider facts:* no M7 credential can write under `<evidencePrefix>` (XC-1), the provider rejects a create for a key the capability does not name (SP-10), and it bounds in-flight write visibility by `W` (SP-9). *Deployment-topology facts:* the capability signer signs only the envelope the database returned, and holds the only credential able to sign one (XC-5, XC-6) | a consumer may treat M7-TG-11 as established only where the deployment demonstrates **T-138b, T-142 and T-167** on the real provider **and T-171b** on the real deployment. The database alone proves the *scheduling* half (no effect executes before the fence, M7-I109) and the *envelope* half (nothing M7 mints is wider, M7-I118) — never the provider half (residual **M7-R-09**, class E-D) and never the signer half (residual **M7-R-12**, invariant **M7-I119**, class **E-E**). §28.3 states both |
| an actor holding the object-store credentials themselves | outside M7's threat boundary. Such a write after a confirmed deletion appears as a `CANONICAL_OBJECT_PRESENT_AFTER_DELETION` integrity finding, which stands permanently beside the completion record and is **not** silently reconciled away (§17.4). Residual **M7-R-10** |

```
M7 CLAIMS S-2 IS GROUNDING: NO
M7 CLAIMS TO SATISFY DB-03B: NO — IT EXPOSES FACTS; B1S DECIDES
B1 IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORIZED: NO
WITHOUT ACCEPTED M7 TRUSTED-GENERATION CONTRACT:
S-2 MAY REMAIN NON-GROUNDING
```

The JBA-defined fallback is **unchanged** by this candidate: absent an **accepted** M7 ingestion integration contract, every S-2 observation remains non-grounding (JBA §18.4.6, §18.4.7, AM-9), and that default is complete without any decision by M7. Whether the facts above suffice for `DB-03B` is **B1S's** question, answered in a B-scoped artifact under B-scoped acceptance — not here.

### 21.4 What a B reader may and may not take from an M7 row

| M7 row | B may read it as | B may **not** read it as |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7_outcome_assertion` with `occurrenceAssertion <> 'NONE'` | an explicit purchase-shaped assertion actually present in the authoritative representation (JBA §7.3 case 3) | an established occasion; a candidate; a count |
| `m7_outcome_assertion` whose only content is a `statusLabel` | provenance metadata (JBA BI-23) | any occurrence evidence, including for `ATTEMPTED` or `SELF_REPORTED` |
| `m7_evidence_submission` | the fact of submission, with a re-provable link (JBA §7.6) | a verification, a verdict, or a verified amount |
| `m7_evidence_integrity_finding` | a storage-integrity observation on a named backend | a scientific or verification judgement |
| `m7_evidence_upload_intent`, `m7_canonical_generation` | nothing — a capability and a key reservation, not sources | any assertion whatsoever |
| a superseded generation, or an orphan object | storage hygiene | a second piece of evidence, or a duplicate submission |
| absence of a row, a `FAILED`/`ABANDONED` label, or a purged record | unknown (RAT P-13; JBA BI-31) | evidence that no purchase occurred, or that fewer occurred |

### 21.5 C firewall

M7 V1.1 contains no verifier capability, no verification record, no verdict column, no value field, no baseline, no numerator or denominator input, and no analysis window. C1 and C2 remain **NOT AUTHORIZED** (register §4, §6.1). C2's treatment of missingness created by lawful deletion is C2's (JBA §16.6.2, obligation C2-4a); M7 only makes the missingness typed where residue is lawful, and ordinary where it is not.

## 22. VerifiedValue boundary

### 22.1 Four things, never collapsed

```
Outcome            one root per accepted Decision                        M7   (this document)
SavingEvidence     one participant submission act + its raw artifact     M7   (this document)
Verification       a verifier's judgement about submitted evidence       C1   NOT AUTHORIZED
VerifiedValue      the data-bearing union of Rev2 §5 (RT-10)             C1/C2 NOT AUTHORIZED
```

M7 V1.1 persists the first two and **not one field** of the last two. No M7 table, column, enum label, function, view or index encodes a verification, a verdict, a VS level, a saving amount, a paid amount, a counterfactual, a baseline kind or an evidence reference held by a verifier.

### 22.2 Which M7 facts may exist before any value verification

| Fact | May exist pre-verification | Note |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7_outcome` root | yes | one per accepted `Decision` |
| participant assertions, including `SELF_REPORTED` and an explicit occurrence assertion | yes | participant-authored; no value fields (§13.3) |
| `m7_evidence_submission` + `AVAILABLE` artifact + observation digest | yes | the submission act and its bytes, on a named backend |
| corrections, retractions, replacements | yes | §14 |
| integrity findings, reconciliation findings, deletion records | yes | storage scope |

**Raw evidence may be deleted before any verification ever occurs**, because RT-17's never-verified window runs regardless and no verification decision can exist in V1.1 (§15.2). That is the inherited SLA, not an M7 choice; it is recorded as implementation prerequisite **IMP-09** (§28.1).

### 22.3 Transitions not permitted merely because evidence exists

| Tempting inference | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| evidence submitted ⇒ `evidence-submitted` status label | refused: that label is object-implied, never stored (§6.3) |
| evidence submitted ⇒ VS2 or VS3 | refused: no VS level is stored, cached or projected (§22.4) |
| evidence verified somewhere ⇒ an M7 row may record it | refused: M7 has no verification write path; adding one requires an accepted C1S |
| a `VERIFIED_PEN_SAVING` exists ⇒ M7 may store the amount | refused: Rev2 §5 attaches `VerifiedValue` to M7 as a *milestone deliverable*, but its production is verification, which is C1 and unauthorized; V1.1 reserves the dependency instead of inventing it (AC-04) |
| one terminal VS3 per `Outcome` (RT-09) ⇒ M7 must enforce it now | refused and **carried**: the constraint is a C1S obligation (§22.5); M7 enforces only what it persists |

### 22.4 No VS level is persisted or projected

| Level (FINAL §21) | M7 V1.1 representation |
| :-- | :-- |
| VS0 theoretical | **not stored**; the underlying facts are A2/M3.5A's `purchase_intent_decision_binding` + `decision_snapshot` |
| VS1 intended | **not stored**; underlying fact is an `INTENDED` assertion |
| VS2 self-reported | **not stored**; underlying fact is a `SELF_REPORTED` assertion (no value fields) |
| VS3 transaction-corroborated | **not stored**; requires a C1 verification that cannot exist |
| VS4 dual-corroborated | **not stored**; undefined by inherited authority beyond its name — M7 invents nothing |

Ladder position is never authority: nothing in M7 computes a maximum, a latest or a current level, and `AnalysisProtocol` (UNFROZEN) remains the classification owner (FINAL §27).

### 22.5 Obligations carried to a future C1S, not decided here

| # | Obligation |
| :-- | :-- |
| C1-OB-1 | RT-09 *"one terminal VS3 per `Outcome`"* must be enforced by whatever persists VS3; `m7_outcome.id` is the available FK target |
| C1-OB-2 | Rev2 §5 invariants: `verifiedSavingCentimos = counterfactual − paid`, `> 0` for VS3, only the two accepted `BaselineKind` values, provider-relative list prices rejected |
| C1-OB-3 | nominal outcomes never enter PEN VS3 (FINAL §21, RT-06) |
| C1-OB-4 | a verifier write must never mutate, re-author or redact a participant row; M7's guards already make that impossible without the redaction path |
| C1-OB-5 | verify-then-purge ordering: a verification decision creates the RT-17 ≤ 7-day basis. C1S MUST add it as a **fourth deletion basis** instantiating the §15.11 model — its own `hardDeadline`, `scheduleAfter` and shared `effectCompletionBudget`, with DL-1…DL-4 holding for it — and MUST NOT mutate an existing basis or reinterpret an existing per-row deadline |
| C1-OB-6 | any verifier read of evidence bytes requires the download-URL bounds V1.1 leaves undefined and unissued (§11.5), **and** must resolve the object through the artifact's own `storageProfileId`, never through the active manifest (SI-1) |

## 23. Control-plane manifest

### 23.1 Purpose

One independently reviewable artifact that fixes every operational value M7's guarantees depend on, so that a reviewer can check the deployed database and runtime against a digest rather than against prose. It is **not** accepted, published or rotated by this authoring task.

### 23.2 Identity versus installation (closes `M7V11-AUD-03`)

| Concept | Table | Cardinality rule |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **manifest identity** — the reviewed artifact | `m7_control_plane_manifest` | `manifestVersion` is the primary key; `manifestSha256` is UNIQUE. Therefore **one version ↔ exactly one digest**, and **one digest ↔ exactly one version**, forever |
| **installation event** — an act of making a manifest active | `m7_control_plane_installation` | `id` and a monotonic `installationSeq`; **no uniqueness on the manifest**, so the same `manifestVersion` may be installed again; at most one row is active (partial unique index) |

Consequences, each executable:

| Requirement | How it holds |
| :-- | :-- |
| one manifest version always maps to exactly one digest | PK + `c_register_manifest_v1` refusing a re-registration with different content |
| one digest always maps to exactly one manifest | `UNIQUE(manifestSha256)` + `c_register_manifest_v1` refusing a digest already bound to another version |
| the same reviewed manifest may be installed again later | `c_activate_manifest_v1` inserts a **new installation row** referencing the existing manifest |
| only one installation is active | partial unique index `m7_control_plane_installation_one_active` |
| **rollback A → B → A is executable** | three activation events: A, B, A. Nothing is reused, nothing is un-retired, nothing collides (T-110) |
| historical rows keep the correct control-plane identity | every historical row stores `installationId` (the event it was created under) **and** its own `retentionPolicyVersion` / `storageProfileId` / `backendSha256`, which is what it actually resolves through (SI-1) |
| no policy bound to existing data is retroactively changed | per-row policy binding plus per-row deadline columns (§15.11.3): an activation changes only what **new** rows get |
| rollback cannot resurrect retired storage | `c_activate_manifest_v1` refuses a manifest whose storage profile or backend is retired (`M7011`) |
| rollback cannot extend a retention window already bound | the window lives on the row (`rawDeleteHardDueAt`), not in the active policy |

### 23.3 Canonical representation, identity and digest

| Item | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| format | JSON; canonicalized with the accepted project serializer (`src/persistence/canonical.ts`), the same one A2 §33.2 and §13.9 use |
| identity | `manifestVersion`, matching `^pagamenos\.m7\.control-plane\.[a-z0-9.-]{1,64}$` |
| digest | `manifestSha256 = 'sha256:' ‖ hex(sha256(utf8(canonical(manifest without the digest field))))` |
| immutability | a `manifestVersion` binds exactly one digest forever; any content change requires a **new version** (A2 §13.10 pattern) |
| storage | the manifest lives in the machine-readable authority namespace (§24), **not** in this document; the database stores its version, its digest and its bindings (`m7_control_plane_manifest`) plus its expected catalog state (§19.5) |

### 23.4 Fields

| Group | Fields | Bound to |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `authority` | `specArtifactPath`, `specSha256`, `specAcceptanceVerdict`, `registerSection`, `baselineCommit` | the accepted M7 specification and the register entry that accepted it |
| `database` | `schema`, `migrationName`, `migrationSha256`, `roles[]` (name, login, inherit, schema usage, memberships, allowed EXECUTE set), `functions[]` (signature, `prosecdef`, `proconfig`, `prosrc` digest, **exact** EXECUTE grantee set), `relations[]` (name, kind), `relationObjects[]` (constraints, indexes, triggers per relation), `assignmentLockingFunctions[]` (LO-3), `implicitAssignmentReferenceFunctions[]` (LO-3, IW-1), **`capabilitySignerFunctions[]`** (MA-14), **`backendLivenessFunctions[]`** (MA-16, LO-4), **`transactionOwners[]`** (TO-1…TO-8: owner id, CCA class, role, function set, process kind, whether it may lock `experiment_assignment`, class-10 mode — MA-17), **`lockProfiles[]`** (per function: P1 sequence, P2 kind, P3 implicit-wait identifiers, exactly as §16.2.6 — MA-18), `legacyRuntimeRoles[]` | §18, §19; loaded into §19.5 by `c_load_catalog_expectations_v1` |
| `database.controlPlaneInstall` | the exact literal arguments of the single `c_register_*` → `c_load_catalog_expectations_v1` → `c_activate_manifest_v1` sequence (§19.13.4) | §19.11.2 |
| `retention` | `policyVersion` and every policy value, including the §15.11 triple (`hardDeadline*`, `scheduleAfter*`, `schedulerWorstCaseLag`, `effectCompletionBudget`, `outboxBackoffCap`, `outboxMaxAttempts`) and the §11.7 fence parameters (`generationWriteGrantTtl`, `writeFenceSkewAllowance`) | RT-17, §11.7, §15.10–§15.11 |
| `merchantVocabulary` | `vocabularyVersion`, `corpusId`, `entryCount`, `entriesSha256`, ordered `merchantRefs[]`, and the RP-5 stability declaration | §13.4, A2 §33.10 |
| `storage.backend` | `providerClass`, `containerId`, `regionId`, `endpointIdentity`, `stagingPrefix`, `evidencePrefix`, `providerWriteCompletionWindowSeconds`, and the resulting `backendSha256` | §11.1.2, §11.7 |
| `storage.profile` | `storageProfileVersion`, `credentialProfileId`, `credentialGeneration`, `uploadTransport`, `decoderGeneration`, `encoderGeneration`, `storageCapabilityVersion`, `conditionalCreateMode`, `writeCapabilityMode`, **`envelopeEnforcement`** (`PROVIDER_IAM` \| `SIGNER_TOPOLOGY`, MA-13), and the resulting `profileSha256` | §11.1.2, §11.7.4 |
| `storage.capabilities` | `publicAccessBlocked`, `versioningDisabled`, `conditionalCreateSupported`, `prefixListingSupported`, `strongConsistency`, `credentialScopes[]` (which MUST record that no scope grants write under `evidencePrefix` — XC-1), `exactKeyWriteCapabilitySupported`, `writeCompletionWindowEnforced`, **`envelopeEnforcement`** and, when it is `PROVIDER_IAM`, `envelopePolicyDocumentRef` (MA-13), `maxBytes`, `maxPixels`, `allowedMagicByteFamilies[]`, `canonicalMediaType`, `signedUrlMaxTtlSeconds`, `downloadUrlsIssued: false` | §11.2 SP-1…SP-10 |
| `storage.fencing` | the arithmetic check published for review: `generationWriteGrantTtlSeconds + providerWriteCompletionWindowSeconds + writeFenceSkewAllowanceSeconds <= workerLeaseSeconds` (XF-DL-1), with the three inputs restated | §11.7.2 |
| `storage.retiredBackends[]` | previously registered `backendSha256` values and their drain status | §11.1.5 |
| `session` | `ttlSeconds`, `secretBytes: 32`, `digestAlgorithm: "sha256"` | §8.2 |
| `operational` | `schedulerCadenceSeconds` (≤ `schedulerWorstCaseLag`), `workerLeaseSeconds`, `orphanGraceSeconds`, `captureSkewToleranceSeconds`, `auditSampleRate`, `generationSweepCadenceSeconds` | §12, §15.11, §17.4 |
| `deployment` | `environment`, `databaseIdentifier`, `appContractVersion`, `minAppContractVersion`, **`capabilitySigner`** (the one module that reads `M7_CAPABILITY_SIGNER_DATABASE_URL` and the provider write-signing credentials, the fact that it runs as its own process (TO-8), its single exported entry point, `credentialProfileIds[]` — the signing credentials it holds, which MUST equal the live profiles' `credentialProfileId`s (XC-7) — the commit-before-sign declaration (XF-16), and the declaration that no other module in the dependency closure imports the provider signing SDK — MA-15). **This is the manifest's only field carrying an E-E claim**, and it is published here precisely because no database object can hold it (§11.7.4, M7-I119) | §23.5, §11.7.4, IMP-18 |
| `compatibility` | `manifestSchemaVersion: "pagamenos.m7.control-plane-manifest.v1"`, `specSchemaVersions[]` | §23.5 |

### 23.5 Allowed operational selectors

Exactly three fields are *selectors* a deployment may legitimately differ on: `deployment.environment`, `deployment.databaseIdentifier`, and — through the storage profile — `storage.profile.uploadTransport`. Every other field is a fixed value of the reviewed manifest.

**No selector may weaken an invariant**: there is no selector that disables a guard, a role separation, a window bound, the magic-byte check, the re-encode step, the deletion-evidence requirement, the exact-set catalog check, or the routing check of SI-3. In particular, `uploadTransport` is *not* a free runtime switch: changing it is a **new storage profile** (§11.1.3), so historical intents keep the transport they were issued under (RP-3).

The runtime refuses to start its M7 modules unless `manifestSchemaVersion` is one it implements, the spec digest matches the accepted artifact, and `appContractVersion ≥ minAppContractVersion`. A manifest that binds a different `migrationSha256` than the migration actually installed is a mismatch, not a warning.

### 23.6 Runtime selection and fail-closed behaviour

```text
build embeds the reviewed manifest  ─┐
env M7_CONTROL_PLANE_MANIFEST_SHA256 ┼─ all three must be equal, or M7 operations are refused
DB active installation's manifest   ─┘
```

1. at startup the M7 modules compute the digest of the embedded manifest and compare it with the environment value; a mismatch, an absent value, or a malformed value ⇒ **refuse to serve any M7 operation**;
2. every `m7.p_*`, `s_*`, `r_*`, `w_*`, `a_*` entry function receives the expected digest and calls `m7.i_assert_control_plane`, which raises `55000 M7_CONTROL_PLANE_MISMATCH` unless it equals the active installation's manifest digest — so a drifted deployment cannot write even if a module forgot to check;
3. a periodic job runs `m7.w_verify_control_plane_catalog_v1`; any returned row is an alert and, per `IMP-07` (§28.1), disables M7 write operations until resolved;
4. a periodic job runs `m7.w_list_deletion_sla_v1`; `LAG` rows are a scheduling alarm, `CRITICAL` and `BREACH` rows are SLA alarms (§15.11.4). A separate scheduled step runs `m7.w_assert_deletion_sla_failures_v1`, which records budget overruns as durable `m7_deletion_sla_failure` facts (DL-8); monitoring itself never writes;
4a. a manifest whose `(G, W, Λ, workerLease)` do not satisfy XF-DL-1 **cannot be activated** (`M7012`), so a deployment can never be running with a write fence that outlives the lease it is issued with (§11.7.2);
5. **there is no fallback path**: no M7 operation has an alternative connection, role, storage backend or "degraded" mode. Absent or mismatched control plane ⇒ no M7 writes, no uploads, no deletions executed (scheduling included). An unroutable backend ⇒ no confirmations, only SLA-critical rows.

### 23.7 Review, publication, rotation, rollback, audit

| Concern | Requirement |
| :-- | :-- |
| review | the manifest is reviewed **independently** of the implementation that consumes it, against §18, §19 and §23.4; reviewers must be able to reproduce `manifestSha256` from the published content, and `backendSha256`, `profileSha256`, `policySha256`, `entriesSha256` and `vocabularySha256` from their own inputs |
| publication | published only in the machine-readable authority namespace of an accepted authority-baseline commit (§24), never edited in place |
| rotation | a new `manifestVersion` + digest; the rotation script runs the `c_register_*` → `c_load_catalog_expectations_v1` → `c_activate_manifest_v1` sequence **inside one transaction**, which retires the previous installation and installs the new one atomically; the schema is **not** re-created (`IA-07` refuses re-install) |
| what rotation may not do | rotation MUST NOT retroactively change a bound policy, a bound deadline or a bound storage identity for existing rows. Upload intents, generations, observations, artifacts, submissions and outbox rows carry their own bindings, so a shortened or lengthened window, a new vocabulary, a new transport or a new backend applies only to rows created afterwards (SI-1, SI-2, §15.11.3) |
| credential rotation | register a new storage profile over the **same** `backendSha256` (`credentialGeneration + 1`), activate a manifest naming it, then retire the old profile. Historical objects stay addressable throughout (§11.1.3) |
| backend rotation | register a new backend and a profile over it, then activate. The old backend keeps every historical object and MUST be **drained**, never reassigned; `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` enforces the drain (§11.1.5) |
| rollback | rolling back to a previous manifest is a **new installation event** of that already-registered manifest. It MUST NOT reuse or un-retire an installation row, MUST NOT be used to extend a retention window for rows already bound to a stricter policy, and is refused if that manifest's storage profile or backend has been retired |
| audit trail | `m7_control_plane_manifest` (immutable identities) and `m7_control_plane_installation` (`installationSeq`, `installedBy`, `installedAt`, `retiredBy`, `retiredAt`) form an append-only history of *which manifest was active when*; storage backends and profiles carry their own registration and retirement attribution |

```
M7 CONTROL-PLANE MANIFEST: NOT ACCEPTED
M7 CONTROL-PLANE MANIFEST PUBLISHED OR ROTATED BY THIS TASK: NO
CONCRETE MANIFEST VALUES ASSERTED BY THIS DOCUMENT: NONE
```

### 23.8 Versioned-identity reuse: one rule, applied to every identity

The independent audit's §3 check generalises beyond the vocabulary: **reusing any versioned control-plane identity with different immutable content MUST fail.** V1.1 applies one mechanism uniformly — a **content digest recomputed in PostgreSQL** from the stored rows, compared against both the stored digest and the supplied values, with an explicit field-by-field comparison where the digest could not cover everything.

| Versioned identity | Digest recomputed in SQL | On reuse with identical content | On reuse with **any** different content |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `m7_storage_backend.backendSha256` | `i_backend_digest` over all six identity fields — the digest **is** the key, so a different backend is a different row | no-op, returns the same digest | impossible to alias: a changed field yields a different key. A digest collision is additionally field-checked |
| `m7_storage_profile.storageProfileVersion` | `i_profile_digest` over the version, `backendSha256`, credential identity and generation, transport, decoder, encoder, capability version, conditional-create mode | no-op, returns the existing `id` | `55000` — *"storage profile version X already exists with different content"* |
| `m7_retention_policy.policyVersion` | `i_policy_digest` over **every** policy column | no-op | `55000` — *"policy version X already exists with different content"*. Additionally DL-4 is re-verified |
| `m7_merchant_vocabulary.vocabularyVersion` | `i_vocabulary_entries_digest` over the stored entry rows **and** `i_vocabulary_digest` over `(version, corpusId, entryCount, entriesSha256)` | no-op | `55000` on **any** difference — a different `corpusId`, a different entry count, a different entry set, or an `entriesSha256` that disagrees with the stored rows. This is the specific gap §3 of the audit brief named |
| `m7_control_plane_manifest.manifestVersion` | not a content digest — the manifest's digest is supplied and is its identity | no-op | `55000` on a different digest **or** a different policy/vocabulary/profile binding |
| `m7_control_plane_manifest.manifestSha256` | — | — | `55000` — *"digest already bound to manifest version Y"* |
| catalog expectation set per `manifestVersion` | — | no-op (loaded once, immutable) | cannot be reloaded at all; a different expectation set requires a new manifest version |
| `m7_retention_policy.policySha256`, `m7_storage_profile.profileSha256`, `m7_merchant_vocabulary.vocabularySha256` | UNIQUE | — | two versions cannot share identical content, so identity churn is also refused |

Audit of every versioned identity for this property: **complete**, and the adversarial suite executes each row (T-111…T-116).

## 24. Machine-readable authority requirements

### 24.1 Two different things called authority

| | Documentation authority | Machine-readable authority |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| what | this document and the other `PAGAMENOS_*.md` artifacts | the JSON artifacts CI gates consume, in the `authority/` namespace of a separately selected commit |
| selected by | the root register | the protected external variable `PAGAMENOS_ACCEPTED_AUTHORITY_BASE_SHA` |
| read by CI | no | yes |
| changed by this candidate | it **adds** one document | **nothing** |

Register §2.4 records that `authority/` is absent from this tree and that the selector's value is externally governed. This candidate **does not assert, infer, invent, derive or rotate** that value, and reads no in-tree comment as evidence of it.

```
PAGAMENOS_ACCEPTED_AUTHORITY_BASE_SHA ASSERTED HERE: NO
MACHINE-READABLE AUTHORITY ARTIFACTS CHANGED HERE: NONE
SELECTOR ROTATED HERE: NO
```

### 24.2 What a later rotation must prove before M7 implementation can be accepted

These are **normative requirements on a future rotation**, not actions taken now.

| # | A rotation adding M7 control-plane authority MUST prove |
| :-- | :-- |
| MA-1 | the new authority-baseline commit contains the M7 control-plane manifest at a fixed path in `authority/`, and the manifest's own digest is reproducible from its published bytes |
| MA-2 | the manifest's `authority.specSha256` equals the SHA-256 of the **independently accepted** M7 specification artifact, and `authority.specAcceptanceVerdict` names the verdict recorded in the register |
| MA-3 | every pre-existing `(corpusId, digest)` ledger entry and every historical holiday-registry version is unchanged (A2 §34.4, §34.5) — M7 additions are **additive only** |
| MA-4 | `merchantVocabulary.corpusId` is an entry of the accepted `CORPUS_RELEASE_LEDGER_V1`; `entriesSha256` is reproducible from the listed refs in the same canonical form PostgreSQL recomputes (§19.11.1); and **RP-5** holds — no `merchantRef` in the new vocabulary denotes a different merchant than it denoted in any earlier vocabulary version |
| MA-5 | the candidate cannot satisfy the gate by editing repository files: the historical comparison is loaded from the externally supplied SHA (A2 §34) |
| MA-6 | the selector rotation happens **after** independent acceptance, by a privileged owner, with no force-moved tag, no branch-as-authority, and no candidate-chosen base (A2 §34.1 step 8) |
| MA-7 | a deployed database can be verified against the manifest with `m7.w_verify_control_plane_catalog_v1` returning zero rows, and its active installation's manifest digest equal to the manifest digest |
| MA-8 | the M7 CI gate fails closed when the selector is unset, blank, malformed, or points at a commit lacking the manifest — matching the accepted workflow behaviour for the existing gates |
| MA-9 | `storage.backend` reproduces `backendSha256` exactly as `m7.i_backend_digest` computes it, and `storage.profile` reproduces `profileSha256` exactly as `m7.i_profile_digest` computes it |
| MA-10 | the manifest's §15.11 values satisfy DL-1…DL-4 arithmetically **in the published document**, and `operational.schedulerCadenceSeconds ≤ retention.schedulerWorstCaseLag` |
| MA-11 | `storage.retiredBackends[]` lists every previously registered backend, and for each one the rotation demonstrates either that it is drained or that it remains live with at least one live profile — no historical object may be left unroutable |
| MA-12 | `database.assignmentLockingFunctions[]` equals exactly `{m7.w_execute_row_redaction_v1, m7.w_execute_row_purge_v1}` (LO-3) |
| **MA-13** | `storage.capabilities.envelopeEnforcement` is declared per profile as `PROVIDER_IAM` or `SIGNER_TOPOLOGY`, is inside `profileSha256` (MA-9), and — when `PROVIDER_IAM` — names the exact provider policy document that pins operation, key, backend and a non-extendable `validUntil` (§11.7.4) |
| **MA-14** | `database.capabilitySignerFunctions[]` equals exactly `{m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1}`, its EXECUTE grantee set equals exactly `{pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt}`, that role's total EXECUTE set in `m7` has cardinality 1, and `pagamenos_m7_storage_worker_rt` is absent from the grantee set (XF-13, IA-14, T-171b) |
| **MA-15** | `deployment.capabilitySigner` names the one module that reads `M7_CAPABILITY_SIGNER_DATABASE_URL` and the provider write-signing credentials, declares that it runs as its own process, that it signs only after commit and only with the returned signing profile's credential, lists `credentialProfileIds[]` equal to the live profiles' `credentialProfileId`s, and declares that no other module in the dependency closure imports the provider signing SDK (XC-5, XC-6, XC-7). These are the **E-E** claims of M7-I119, M7-I125 and M7-I126, and the manifest is where they are published, because the database cannot hold them |
| **MA-16** | `database.backendLivenessFunctions[]` equals exactly the entry functions that call `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness` or `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness`, that set equals §11.10.4's enumeration, and it equals the mechanical derivation rule of §11.10.4 (every function inserting into an intent, generation, artifact or `PENDING` outbox row, or a capability mint) — all three in both directions (LO-4, BL-2, T-180) |
| **MA-17** | `database.transactionOwners[]` lists exactly TO-1…TO-8 as §16.2.3 and §18.6 do; each owner's function set equals the EXECUTE set of its role (TO-4 ∪ TO-5 = the worker role's set; TO-8 = `{m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1}`); and the `DatabaseExecutionContext` registration of every owner, TO-8 included, is demonstrated (T-189) |
| **MA-18** | `database.lockProfiles[]` has one row per `SECURITY DEFINER` function, each equal to its §16.2.6 row, and the source check T-181 passes against the migration's `prosrc` |

> **What a later rotation must additionally prove after round 2.** A manifest rotation MUST re-publish, and CI MUST re-check: (a) the XF-DL-1 arithmetic for the new `(policy, backend)` pair; (b) the `storage.capabilities.credentialScopes[]` statement that no scope grants write under `evidencePrefix` (XC-1), together with a fresh T-138b result against the deployed provider; (c) that every `w_*` function touching the outbox resolves its policy through `m7.i_outbox_bound_policy` — enforced by the `prosrc` digests the manifest already pins (T-155); and (d) that `m7.i_backend_is_drained` is the only drain predicate in the migration source (a single-definition check, T-163).

> **What a later rotation must additionally prove after round 3.** Also re-published and re-checked: (e) `envelopeEnforcement` per profile, with a fresh **T-171b** dependency-closure result and, for `PROVIDER_IAM`, the named policy document (MA-13, MA-15); (f) that `m7.x_mint_generation_capability_v1` is still the only `x_*` function, still takes exactly `(text, uuid)`, and still has exactly one grantee holding exactly one grant (MA-14, IA-14, T-135); (g) that `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness` is the only backend-liveness predicate in the migration source and that every backend-scoped writer calls it — the BL-analogue of (d) (MA-16, **T-180**); and (h) a fresh **T-172** result, because RT-2 is the one retirement rule a rotation can invalidate by construction: the backend that was safe to retire before the rotation is exactly the one that becomes active after it.

> **What a later rotation must additionally prove after round 4.** Also re-published and re-checked: (i) `transactionOwners[]` and `lockProfiles[]` against the migration (MA-17, MA-18, T-181, T-189); (j) that `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness` is the only multi-backend liveness path and that `backendLivenessFunctions[]` still equals the §11.10.4 derivation rule rather than a hand-kept list (MA-16, T-180); (k) `deployment.capabilitySigner.credentialProfileIds[]` against the live profiles **of the rotated control plane**, with a fresh **T-171c**, because a credential rotation is exactly when the signer's credential set can drift from the database's (MA-15, XC-7); and (l) fresh **T-185**, **T-186** and **T-187** results, because a rotation is itself one of the transactions those cases race.

### 24.3 What this candidate requires of CI (specification only)

`verify` and `authority-gate` remain exactly as accepted; this candidate changes no workflow. A future M7 implementation candidate must **add** (not weaken) gates:

- the real-PostgreSQL adversarial suite of §25 on the hosted required-check surface (the M7 analogue of R-B-16);
- the exact-set catalog verification of §19.13 against a real database, asserting **zero** rows;
- the capability/dependency-closure checks CCA §42–§43 already require, extended to M7 modules, the five new credential names (§18.3) and the LO-3 function allowlist;
- the manifest gates MA-1…MA-18.

---
## 25. Adversarial verification contract

### 25.1 How this suite must run

| # | Requirement |
| :-- | :-- |
| VC-1 | Every case below runs against **real PostgreSQL ≥ 15** with the §19 script installed and the **seven** roles provisioned, on the **hosted required-check surface** — the M7 analogue of R-B-16/§6.2 of the register. Migration-text inspection, Prisma-level assertions and mocks are **insufficient evidence** for any case |
| VC-2 | Cases marked **STORE** additionally require a real object store satisfying §11.2 (a conformance double is acceptable only if it enforces SP-1…SP-10 and is itself tested against the real provider in a separate suite). Cases marked **2STORE** require **two distinct backends** (two containers, or two conformance doubles with different `containerId`), because a single backend cannot exhibit routing failure. **Family Q (§25.18) is the exception to the double rule**: T-138b, T-142, T-166…T-171 and T-171c assert what the *real* provider refuses, accepts and aborts, so a conformance double cannot stand in for them at all (IMP-16) |
| VC-3 | Each case connects **as a named role**: `owner-class` (migration/rotation role), `participant`, `issuer`, `privacy`, `worker`, `authority`, **`signer`**, or `legacy` (the pre-existing application runtime role). Cases that say "direct SQL" issue arbitrary statements through that role's own connection, never through application code (RAT P-10) |
| VC-4 | Concurrency cases use **two or more real sessions** with explicit statement interleaving, run **both** orders, and fail on any `40P01 deadlock_detected` — PostgreSQL's deadlock detector resolving a cycle is a failure of LG-THEOREM, never a pass; crash cases abort the backend (or roll back after the stated boundary) and then run recovery |
| VC-5 | A case passes only if **all** of: the PostgreSQL result, the persisted state, the object-store state and the recovery expectation match. A correct error with wrong persisted state is a failure |
| VC-6 | No case may be replaced by a count of other cases, and no required case may be marked "covered by" a different family |
| VC-7 | Cases that assert *absence* of bytes MUST verify absence **on the backend the row is bound to**, by reading that backend directly, and MUST additionally verify **presence** on any other backend where the bytes could still be — a `HEAD` 404 on the wrong container is never evidence (SI-3) |
| **VC-8** | Cases marked **SIGN** additionally require the **deployed capability signer**: the real `pagamenos_m7_capability_signer_rt` connection, the real signer module and its real provider signing credential. A case marked SIGN may **not** be discharged by inserting a row, by calling the database function from a test harness with a different role, or by a stub signer. T-166…T-171b, T-171c and T-171d are SIGN; T-171b additionally requires the deployment's real dependency graph (IMP-18), and T-171c the deployment's real credential inventory (XC-7). **A SIGN case that was run without the deployed signer has not been run** |

Every case in this family asserts a **provider** or **signer** outcome, not only a database error. Cases marked **STORE** run against a real provider profile as well as the conformance double; cases marked **SIGN** run through the deployed capability signer (VC-8). A database-only pass does **not** close either finding.

**The external minting boundary (`M7V11R3-AUD-01`).** T-166…T-171b are the round-3 additions and are the cases round 2 did not have: they exercise the **real** signer path, not a second SQL row. Each is **SIGN**, and T-171 is additionally **STORE**. They implement the six required cases A–F of §11.7.6 in order. Round 4 adds **T-170b** (a database-level two-session case run as the `signer` role, not SIGN: the expiry refusal must hold after a lock wait), **T-171c** (SIGN, STORE: signer routing under credential rotation) and **T-171d** (SIGN: no signature without a committed mint), and re-scopes T-168, T-169 and T-170.

(ii) as the signer role, mint twice for one generation and compare. (c) control: S1 releases at `T − 0.2 s` | (a) and (b): S2 **waits**, wakes after `T`, and raises **`M7013`**; no mint row exists; no envelope is returned. (i)–(iii) are E-A facts the catalog proves; (iv) is deployment topology PostgreSQL cannot see, and the specification does not pretend otherwise (§11.7.4, M7-R-12) |

### 25.19 R — issuance versus executing profile — `M7V11R2-AUD-02`

| ID | Scenario | Action | Expected |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |

| **T-145** | the intent's issuance profile is **not** required to equal any generation's executing profile | claim an intent after a credential rotation | the generation commits with `executingProfileId ≠ issuanceProfileId`; **no** trigger, CHECK or FK objects (EP-2) |
| **T-146** | an observation cannot name a profile its generation did not run under | forge `executingProfileId` = A1 on an observation of an A2 generation | `23503` on `m7_storage_observation_generation_fkey` |
| **T-147** | an observation cannot name an encoder its executing profile does not pin | forge `encoderGeneration` = E1 with `executingProfileId` = A2 | `23503` on `m7_storage_observation_encoder_fkey`, before any trigger runs (EP-4) |
| **T-148** | an artifact cannot inherit the issuance profile | forge `acceptedExecutingProfileId` = A1 on an artifact whose accepted generation ran under A2 | `23503` on `m7_evidence_artifact_generation_fkey` |
| **T-149** | retiring the executing profile strands nothing | retire A2 after the artifact exists, with A3 live on the same backend | deletion still routes (SI-3), `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` under A3, artifact `DELETED`; the historical rows still name A2 (EP-7) |
| **T-150** | replay reports issuance, projections report execution | SO-2 replay and the §21.3 projection for the same submission after a rotation | replay returns A1's transport/version/credential profile; the projection returns A2 and E2; neither returns the other's (EP-8) |

### 25.20 S — bound-policy resolution — `M7V11R2-AUD-03`

| ID | Scenario | Action | Expected |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **T-151** | **MANDATORY: every timing parameter of a deletion-linked effect stays with P1** | schedule a deletion under P1 (record `hardDueAt`, `completionBudgetDueAt`, `deadlinePolicyVersion`); rotate to a materially different P2 (`workerLease`, `outboxMaxAttempts`, `outboxBackoffCap`, `effectCompletionBudget` all changed); run lease → renew → retryable failures → permanent failure | every observed `leaseExpiresAt − now` equals **P1**'s `workerLease`; every renewal window equals P1's; the attempt ceiling is **P1**'s `outboxMaxAttempts`; every `nextAttemptAt` gap equals `min(2ⁿ s, `**P1**`.outboxBackoffCap)`; `hardDueAt` and `completionBudgetDueAt` are unchanged; DL-4 still holds for that effect |
| **T-152** | an `UPLOAD_INTENT`-family effect keeps its intent's policy | enqueue a staging/generation delete under P1, rotate to P2, execute | `boundPolicyVersion` = the intent's; all timing from P1; a forged `boundPolicyVersion` = P2 → `23503` on `m7_storage_outbox_bound_intent_fkey` |
| **T-153** | a `RECONCILIATION_RUN`-family effect keeps its listing run's policy | list under P1, rotate to P2, execute the finding's effect | `boundPolicyVersion` = the finding's; all timing from P1; a forged value → `23503` on `m7_storage_outbox_bound_finding_fkey` |
| **T-154** | **a requeue is recovery, not compliance** | exhaust P1's attempts on a deletion-linked effect, then `w_requeue_failed_effect_v1` with a justification digest, then let it succeed | `attempts` is **not** reset (it strictly increases across the requeue); `attemptBudgetBase` = the pre-requeue `attempts`; exactly one `m7_outbox_requeue_record` with `budgetExhausted = true`; one `m7_deletion_sla_failure(REQUEUED_AFTER_BUDGET_EXHAUSTION)`; and the eventual completion carries `withinCompletionBudget = false`. A direct `UPDATE` setting `attempts = 0` → `restrict_violation` |
| **T-155** | no outbox-execution function reads the active policy | source-level check over the `prosrc` digests the manifest pins for `w_lease_outbox_v1`, `w_renew_outbox_lease_v1`, `w_record_effect_attempt_v1`, `w_requeue_failed_effect_v1` | none references `i_manifest` or `i_policy`; each references `i_outbox_bound_policy`. A variant that reads the active policy is rejected by the check **and** produces `FN-DRIFT` in `w_verify_control_plane_catalog_v1` |
| **T-155b** | a permanent failure and a budget overrun become durable facts | drive an effect to `FAILED_PERMANENT`; separately let an execution pass `completionBudgetDueAt` and run `w_assert_deletion_sla_failures_v1` | one `m7_deletion_sla_failure(EFFECT_FAILED_PERMANENT)` and one `(COMPLETION_BUDGET_ELAPSED)`; both appear in `v_deletion_sla_critical` and **survive** a later completion; an attempt to delete either outside an authorized `ROW_PURGE` → `restrict_violation` |

### 25.21 T — the drain predicate, active-control-plane coherence and retirement concurrency — `M7V11R2-AUD-04`, `M7V11R3-AUD-02`

Each case is run **twice**: once against `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` on the backend's **last** live profile (expecting `M7011`), and once against `c_retire_storage_backend_v1` (expecting `M7009`). T-163 asserts both report the **same** blocking class.

| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **T-156** | a live `m7_evidence_artifact` | `CLASS_1_LIVE_ARTIFACTS` |
| **T-157** | an `ISSUED` upload intent; and, as a second sub-case, a `PROCESSING` one | `CLASS_2_OPEN_INTENTS` |
| **T-158** | a `PENDING` outbox row; and, as a second sub-case, a `FAILED_PERMANENT` one | `CLASS_3_OPEN_EFFECTS` |
| **T-159** | a generation still inside `writeFenceAt` | `CLASS_4_UNFENCED_GENERATIONS` |
| **T-160** | an intent still inside `stagingWriteFenceAt` | `CLASS_5_UNFENCED_STAGING` |
| **T-161** | a generation whose key has no `CONFIRMED` `DELETE_OBJECT` effect | `CLASS_6_UNEVIDENCED_CANONICAL_KEYS` |
| **T-162** | an intent whose staging key has no `CONFIRMED` `DELETE_OBJECT` effect | `CLASS_7_UNEVIDENCED_STAGING_KEYS` |
| **T-163** | **the anti-drift case**: for each of T-156…T-162, both retirement functions are called and their `DETAIL` strings compared | identical class **and** identical count in every sub-case. A migration containing a second, independent drain predicate fails this test |
| **T-164** | fully drained backend | `i_backend_is_drained` returns NULL; **both** retirements succeed; all profiles of A are retired with A |
| **T-165** | non-last profile with a live replacement on the same backend | `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` **succeeds** without consulting the drain predicate (ordinary credential rotation); lifecycle operations continue under the replacement |

**Retirement safety (`M7V11R3-AUD-02`, `M7V11R4-AUD-03`, `M7V11R5-AUD-01`).** T-172…T-180 are the round-3 additions, T-182…T-184 the round-4 additions and T-193 the round-5 addition (the governed retry contract of the non-waiting retirement; the three-session schedule itself is T-190 in family L). **T-173…T-176, T-179 and T-182…T-184 use two real PostgreSQL sessions with explicit statement interleaving** (VC-4) and each is run in **both** orders; a single-session test cannot exhibit any of them, and a passing single-session run is not evidence. Round 2 had **no** case in this family, which is how an unsupported serialization claim survived review.

| ID | Case | Interleaving / action | Expected |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **T-172** | **the active manifest's backend cannot be retired** | backend `A` is the active manifest's and is **fully drained** (`i_backend_is_drained(A)` returns `NULL`); call `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)` | **`55000`**, message `cannot retire the backend of the active manifest`, `DETAIL` naming the RT-3 order. Raised **before** the drain predicate is consulted, so the auditor can see it is a coherence refusal and not a drain refusal. `A` and every profile over it are still live; `i_active_storage_profile` still returns a live profile. Run again with `A` **not** drained: still `55000`, still RT-2, never `M7009` |
| **T-173** | **retirement vs SO-2 issuance** *(the path round 2's RC-19 claimed and did not serialize)* | **order 1:** S1 begins `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)` and holds the class-10 `FOR UPDATE` (acquired `NOWAIT`); S2 runs SO-2 targeting `A`; commit S1, then S2. **order 2:** S2 runs SO-2 and holds its `FOR SHARE` uncommitted; S1 begins the retirement; commit S2, then S1 | **order 1:** S1 commits; S2 raises **`M7011`** at `i_hold_backend_liveness` and writes **nothing** (BL-6). **order 2:** S1 raises **`M7014`** `BACKEND_LIVENESS_HELD` at once and never appears as a waiter in `pg_locks` (LG-10); re-run after S2 commits, it evaluates the predicate and is refused **`M7009`** with `DETAIL = CLASS_2_OPEN_INTENTS=1`. In neither order does an `ISSUED` intent exist on a retired backend, and in neither order is a retirement recorded over a live intent |
| **T-174** | **retirement vs canonical-generation allocation** | as T-173 with S2 running `w_claim_upload_intent_v1` on an intent of `A` | either the generation and its envelope commit and the retirement is refused (`CLASS_4_UNFENCED_GENERATIONS` or `CLASS_6_UNEVIDENCED_CANONICAL_KEYS`), or the retirement commits and the claim raises **`M7011`**. **No generation, and therefore no authorization envelope, ever exists on a retired backend** |
| **T-175** | **retirement vs outbox enqueue** | as T-173 with S2 running, in turn, each enqueuing function of §11.10.4 (WC-5…WC-10) on `A` | either the effect commits and the retirement is refused `CLASS_3_OPEN_EFFECTS=1`, or the retirement commits and S2 raises **`M7011` at its own P2 call, before its first write** — the case asserts that no intent `UPDATE`, execution `INSERT` or finding `INSERT` was attempted. **No newly created effect is ever unrouteable** |
| **T-176** | **retirement vs reconciliation classification** | as T-173 with S2 running `w_classify_object_key_v1` on an **unissued** key of `A` — the one path that can open an effect on an otherwise fully drained backend (WC-10). Third sub-case: S2 holds its `FOR SHARE` indefinitely | orders 1 and 2 as above. Third sub-case: **the retirement is the side that fails** (`M7014` immediately — elapsed time far below `lock_timeout` —, full rollback, `A` still live, S2 unaffected) — BL-7, the fail-closed direction |
| **T-177** | **a full backend rotation still reaches retirement** | register backend `B` and a profile over it; `c_activate_manifest_v1`; drain `A` completely; `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)` | **succeeds.** Every profile of `A` is retired with it (RT-4), and by RT-2 none was active. Attempting the same steps in any other order fails at RT-2, so the order is forced by the database and not by a runbook (RT-3). **2STORE** |
| **T-178** | **credential rotation on a live backend is preserved** | register `A2` over the live backend `A`, activate the manifest naming `A2`, then `c_retire_storage_profile_v1(A1)` while `A2` remains live | **succeeds without consulting the drain predicate** (RT-5, and the drain predicate is asserted *not* to have been evaluated). `A` stays fully usable: a subsequent claim, observation, artifact, enqueue, lease and `ABSENT_CONFIRMED` all complete under `A2`. **The repair costs no credential rotation** — this is the case that would fail if RT-2 had been written against profiles instead of backends |
| **T-179** | **retirement vs requeue, and BL-4 ordering** | (a) S2 requeues a `FAILED_PERMANENT` effect on `A` against S1's retirement, both orders, and `pg_locks` is sampled while S2 holds its transaction; (b) two sessions each run a **multi-backend** batch — each of the five BL-4 functions, and `w_lease_outbox_v1` — spanning backends `A` and `B` whose rows arrive in opposite orders | (a) a `FAILED_PERMANENT` row already blocks class 3, so the retirement is refused in **both** orders; S2 holds **no** lock on any `m7_storage_backend` row (NW-4); after an owner-class bypass retires `A`, the requeue is **`M7011`** from routability. | **T-180** | **BL-2 is exact, in both directions, and BL-5/BL-9 hold** | source-level check over the `prosrc` digests the manifest pins, plus `database.backendLivenessFunctions[]`: (i) compute the §11.10.4 derivation — every function whose body `INSERT`s into `m7_evidence_upload_intent`, `m7_canonical_generation`, `m7_evidence_artifact` or `m7_generation_capability_mint`, or calls `m7.i_enqueue_delete` / `m7.i_enqueue_superseded_generations` — and assert it equals the set of entry functions calling `m7.i_hold_backend_liveness` / `m7.i_hold_backends_liveness`, equals §11.10.4's block and equals the manifest array; (ii) in each such function the liveness call precedes the first `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` and the first enqueue call (P2); (iii) `m7.i_backend_is_drained` contains no `FOR UPDATE`, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, `FOR SHARE` or `FOR KEY SHARE`; (iv) the guard-trigger transition tables admit no transition into `ISSUED`/`PROCESSING`/`VALIDATED` from outside that set, none out of `CONFIRMED`, none into `PENDING`/`LEASED`/`FAILED_PERMANENT` from outside that set, and none out of `DELETED` (BL-9); (v) `w_renew_outbox_lease_v1`, `w_lease_outbox_v1`, `w_record_effect_attempt_v1`, `w_requeue_failed_effect_v1`, both integrity-finding functions and both row mechanisms do **not** call a liveness helper (NW-1…NW-6); (vi) no function has a `p_allow_retired` parameter or argument | each of (i)–(vi) holds. A variant violating any of them fails the check **and** produces `FN-DRIFT` in `m7.w_verify_control_plane_catalog_v1`. **Round 3's version of this case asserted a textual predicate its own function bodies contradicted (WC-13 named renewal); this version derives the set from the definition and compares three sources** |
| **T-182** | **capability mint vs retirement** *(two real sessions, both orders)* | S2: `x_mint_generation_capability_v1` for a live grant on `A`, holding its transaction after the function returns. S1: (a) `c_retire_storage_backend_v1(A)`; (b) `c_retire_storage_profile_v1` of the grant's executing profile while a second live profile of the same kind exists; (c) S1 holds the retirement's backend `FOR UPDATE` across `grantExpiresAt` (T-170b (b)) | (a) refused in both orders (`CLASS_2_OPEN_INTENTS` or `CLASS_4_UNFENCED_GENERATIONS`); (b) if S1 holds class 10 first and commits, S2's mint records the second profile (XF-17); if S2 holds class 10 first, S1 raises `M7014` and, re-run after S2 commits, commits; (c) S2 refuses `M7013`. **No `40P01`**; round 3's mint took class 10 before class 4 |

If S1 commits first, S2 is **`M7013`** (epoch advanced or intent not `PROCESSING`); if S2 commits first, S1 proceeds and its own predicates decide. No mint row ever names a non-current epoch at its commit; **no `40P01`** |

(ii) the first retry after S2 commits reports `M7009 CLASS_3_OPEN_EFFECTS=1` (S2 enqueued an effect) and the loop stops (RR-6). (iii) the pipeline stops after the budget with `RETIREMENT_NOT_ACHIEVED`; `A` and its profiles are live and routable (RR-5). (iv) `M7014 PROFILE_ROW_HELD` |

*Round 3's block said `9` two-backend cases while listing eight family-J cases plus two more, and IMP-06 said `eight`; both are replaced by the enumerated count above.*

> **Why family Q is called out separately.** Every other family in this suite can be executed entirely
> against PostgreSQL and a conformance double. Family Q cannot: `M7V11R2-AUD-01` and
> `M7V11R3-AUD-01` are claims about what an external system will refuse and about what an external
> signer will and will not sign, and only those external systems can falsify them. A deployment that
> runs the other nineteen families and skips Q has **not** closed either finding, and this
> specification does not permit reporting them as closed on database evidence alone.
>
> **Why family T now carries concurrency cases.** `M7V11R3-AUD-02` was reachable partly because the
> round-2 candidate stated a serialization property (its `RC-19`) and provided **no** case that could
> have falsified it. T-173…T-176 and T-179 exist so that the BL-THEOREM of §11.10.6 is falsifiable by
> execution rather than only by reading, and each runs in **both** orders because a one-order pass is
> exactly what an unsupported one-sided lock would produce.

## 26. Normative invariant register

Enforcement layers: **CON** DB constraint (PK/UNIQUE/FK/CHECK/partial index) · **TRG** DB trigger or function · **PRIV** privilege/role boundary · **TX** transaction and lock discipline · **STORE** storage protocol · **CP** control plane · **REV** review/inspection. Classes are JBA §18.2's (**E-A** … **E-E**). Every row names a verification case from §25; **no invariant exists only in prose.**

### 26.1 Layer and class distribution

| Layer | Invariants | | Class | Invariants |
| :-- | --: | :-- | :-- | --: |
| DB constraint (CON) | 36 | | E-A | 110 |
| DB trigger/function (TRG) | 89 | | E-B | 2 |
| Privilege boundary (PRIV) | 16 | | E-C | 2 |
| Transaction/lock (TX) | 14 | | E-D | 9 |
| Storage protocol (STORE) | 17 | | E-E | 6 |
| Control plane (CP) | 16 | | **total** | **129** |
| Review/inspection (REV) | 13 | | | |

**Derivation.** *Layer*: every occurrence of `CON`, `TRG`, `PRIV`, `TX`, `STORE`, `CP` or `REV` in a row's *Layer* cell is counted once under that layer, so a row with two layers counts under each. *Class*: each row is counted once, under the **first** `E-A`…`E-E` token of its *Class* cell (its primary class). *Round 3 printed a distribution (`TRG 75`, `CON 33`, `REV 9`, `E-A 92`, …) that no single rule reproduces from its own §26 rows — the same failure `M7V11R4-AUD-06` names for §19.14 — so both columns are now regenerated by the stated rule.* **129 invariants; 0 prose-only; 0 without a §25 verification case.** The trusted-generation facts **M7-TG-1 … M7-TG-11** (§21.3) are not separate invariants: each is a consequence of M7-I02, I07, I09, I13, I14, I21, I27, I30, I75, I88, I93, I102, I108, I109 and I111, and is listed separately only because B1S consumes them as a named bundle.

**Some invariants are not enforceable from PostgreSQL at all, and they are different kinds of unenforceable.** **M7-I107** is an object-store **ACL** fact: PostgreSQL cannot read a provider ACL, and its only verification is a real-provider test (T-138b), so its class is **E-D**. **M7-I119** is a **deployment capability-topology** fact: which module holds the provider signing credential, and what the signer signs once the envelope has been handed to it. No database object and no provider ACL settles that, so its class is **E-E** and its only verification is the dependency-closure case T-171b. Round 2 had one such dependency and named it; round 3 had two. Round 4 adds three more of the **E-E** kind, each for a reason the database cannot reach: **M7-I123** (a transaction owner's registration and process are application topology), **M7-I125**'s signer half (which credential the signer actually used) and **M7-I126** (whether it waited for commit). Each is named, published in the manifest and tested (T-189, T-171c, T-171d), and none is described as enforced by the SQL of §19.

### 26.2 Invariants deliberately **not** claimed

| Not claimed | Why, and where recorded |
| :-- | :-- |
| that the A1 consent predicate authorized a given write, provably in the database | would require a second consent algorithm, which CCA-SEM forbids; residual **M7-R-01** (§28.3), strengthened only topologically (§18.3.1) |
| that the acting human is the participant | authentication is out of A1's scope (A1 §12) and out of M7's; residual **M7-R-02** |
| any guarantee against owner-class actors | JBA §19.4, PR-5; residual **M7-R-03**. The exact-set catalog check makes many such changes **detectable**, which is all BI-32 permits claiming |
| that a storage worker cannot lie about an observation it reports | the worker is trusted by construction; mitigated by audit sweeps (T-63, T-64) and by the routing check, which removes the *accidental* false confirmation while leaving the *deliberate* one; residual **M7-R-04** |
| that the object store enforces SP-1…SP-10 | not checkable from PostgreSQL; operational prerequisites IMP-04 and IMP-15; residuals **M7-R-04**, **M7-R-09** |
| **that exactly one physical provider token was ever minted for a canonical key** | the signature is produced outside PostgreSQL, so no `PRIMARY KEY`, `CHECK` or trigger can observe a second one. Round 2 claimed it and `M7V11R3-AUD-01` falsified the claim; §11.7.0 records the withdrawal. What is claimed instead is that nothing M7 can mint has a **wider** envelope (M7-I118), which is both implementable and sufficient for every fence and every absence proof (§11.7.5 step (2), Corollary 4) |
| **that the capability signer signs the envelope it was handed** | no database object and no provider ACL settles it. It is deployment capability topology: invariant **M7-I119**, class **E-E**, residual **M7-R-12**, verified only by the dependency-closure case T-171b. The database proves the *surrounding* facts — one function, one grantee, one opaque parameter, a disjoint worker role — and this document does not let those stand in for the one they do not cover |
| that the write fence holds against an actor who **holds the object-store credentials** | the XF-THEOREM's step (1) assumes only M7-issued capabilities exist. A provider-console write after a confirmed deletion is representable, is surfaced as `CANONICAL_OBJECT_PRESENT_AFTER_DELETION`, and is **not** reconciled away silently (§17.4); residual **M7-R-10** |
| that `W` (`providerWriteCompletionWindow`) is the true provider bound | it is a **declared** deployment commitment, exactly like `schedulerWorstCaseLag`. It is verified by T-142 and pinned inside `backendSha256`, so it cannot drift silently — but a provider that violates its own declared bound breaks M7-I108; residual **M7-R-09** |
| that backups or provider replicas contain no deleted bytes | outside M7's technical boundary; residual **M7-R-05** |
| that a legal deletion mechanism is legally sufficient | the controlling authority decides (JBA §16.4); §15.3 |
| that a byte-migration between backends is safe | no such path exists in V1.1 and none is claimed (§11.4, M7-I92); residual **M7-R-07** |
| that freedom from deadlock holds independently of PostgreSQL's row-lock semantics | LG-THEOREM no longer depends on PostgreSQL's **queueing policy** for compatible requests (PG-1 is conservative and admits both behaviours), but it still depends on the conflict matrix, on the implicit lock modes of PG-2 and on a failed `NOWAIT` leaving no waiter (PG-3). Those are checked on the deployed server version (T-188); residual **M7-R-14** |
| that the database proves which credential the signer process used, or that it waited for commit | the database proves which signing profile was resolved and recorded (M7-I125, database half); the rest is signer topology (**E-E**, M7-I125 signer half, M7-I126); residual **M7-R-12** |
| that a row mechanism always makes progress under contention | LG-5 makes TO-5 refuse rather than wait on a busy row (`M7009 ROW_MECHANISM_TARGET_BUSY`); a continuously busy assignment delays erasure until the retry succeeds, which the deletion SLA views surface; residual **M7-R-15** |
| that a storage retirement makes progress while work keeps running on its backend | a retirement yields to every holder of the liveness lock at once (`M7014`) and never waits (LG-10), so under continuous C/M work on a backend — typically credential rotation on the active backend at peak load — it can be delayed until the governed retry budget is exhausted (RR-5). Safety is unaffected; progress is an operational matter (RR-7); residual **M7-R-16** |
| that a revocation prevents the commit of a write that validated the session **before** the revocation committed | such a write holds the session `FOR SHARE` and is serialized before the revocation (RV-2); what is claimed is RV-1 and RV-3 — no later validation succeeds, and after `QUIESCENT` no validated write is still in flight. The session module does not report a revocation as complete before `QUIESCENT` (RV-4) |
| that the count of a residue-prohibited purge survives a lost response, or that its absence can be distinguished from an execution id that never existed | by design neither is possible: storing the count or distinguishing the two cases would be residue (JBA §16.6.1 Case 2). The count exists only in the return value of the call that performed the purge (RM-4…RM-6); residual **M7-R-17** |

## 27. Audit closure matrices

Two matrices are required: the historical V1 blocker families, and the seven findings of the independent V1.1 audit. Statuses are exactly: **CLOSED BY UPSTREAM ACCEPTED AUTHORITY**, **ADDRESSED NORMATIVELY IN THIS CANDIDATE**, **STILL EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY**. *Addressed normatively* means the defect is answered in this document's normative text; it does **not** mean independently accepted.

### 27.7 Independent V1.1 audit matrix, round 5 — `M7V11R5-AUD-01` … `M7V11R5-AUD-02`

| **M7V11R5-AUD-01** — HIGH: PostgreSQL PG-1 premise false; reachable three-way deadlock | Round 4's PG-1 said a `FOR SHARE`/`FOR KEY SHARE` request compatible with the current holders is granted even when a conflicting `FOR UPDATE` is already queued; T-188 (i) demanded that behaviour and LG-THEOREM step 3 used it. PostgreSQL's tuple-lock arbitration exists so that incoming share lockers do not starve a waiting exclusive locker; a later share locker may queue behind it. With a **waiting** retirement, *scheduler (holds backend `A` `FOR SHARE`, waits `FOR KEY SHARE` on assignment `X`) → SO-2 (holds `X` `FOR UPDATE`, requests `A` `FOR SHARE` behind the retirement) → retirement (waits `FOR UPDATE` on `A` behind the scheduler)* is a real cycle. Round 4's sink argument (LG-6 a) treated a retirement as harmless once it *held* the lock and ignored it while it *waited* | **make the premise conservative, then remove the waiters that made it matter.** (1) **PG-1 rewritten**: a compatible request *may* wait behind an incompatible waiter; the specification assumes neither outcome. **PG-3** now states that a failed `NOWAIT` leaves no waiter. (2) **Lemma Q**: every wait, including queue-induced ones, collapses to an edge to a holder whose mode lies in `Reach`, computed per relation from table C. (3) **LG-10**: every `FOR UPDATE`/`FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on `m7_storage_backend`, `m7_storage_profile` and `m7_participant_session` is `NOWAIT` — both retirements (backend, then profiles) and the revocation's quiescence probe — so those relations never have an exclusive waiter and a shared holder of them is never a wait target. (4) **`M7014 M7_RETIREMENT_BUSY`** and the governed retry/failure contract **RR-1…RR-7**: transient, raised before any coherence or drain decision, bounded exponential retry, never cancels, delays or disables work, `RETIREMENT_NOT_ACHIEVED` leaves the backend live (fail closed). (5) **LG-6** replaced by never-waiting states N1…N6 and **LG-THEOREM** re-proved with a finite level function (table LV) that strictly decreases along every edge, independently of the queueing policy. (6) Re-derivation found and closed two further cycles of the same kind: the erasure-request / participant-operation / **revocation** cycle (insert-first revocation, RV-1…RV-5, `QUIESCENT`/`DRAINING`) and the **two-scheduler** cycle (**LG-8**, P3 loops ordered by `assignmentId`); **LG-9** excludes waiting upgrades. (7) §16.2.4 re-derived from PA-1…PA-4 without the no-queueing clause.
